10.1 Analysis modules

10.1.1 bearing_capacity — Bearing capacity

bearing_capacity_analysis — Full bearing capacity analysis for a shallow foundation (Vesic/Meyerhof/Hansen, or Terzaghi 1943 via factor_method='terzaghi').

ParameterTypeDescription
widthfloatrequiredFooting width B (m).
lengthfloatoptionalFooting length L (m). Omit for strip.
depthfloatoptionalEmbedment depth Df (m).
shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: strip, square, rectangular, circular
cohesionfloatoptionalSoil cohesion c (kPa).
friction_anglefloatoptionalFriction angle phi (degrees).
unit_weightfloatrequiredSoil unit weight gamma (kN/m3).
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth below surface (m).
layer2_cohesionfloatoptionalSecond layer cohesion (kPa).
layer2_friction_anglefloatoptionalSecond layer phi (degrees).
layer2_unit_weightfloatoptionalSecond layer gamma (kN/m3). Triggers 2-layer analysis.
layer1_thicknessfloatoptionalFirst layer thickness (m) for 2-layer.
layer1_descriptionstroptionalFirst layer label for the result.
layer2_descriptionstroptionalSecond layer label for the result.
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety.
factor_methodstroptionalShape/depth/inclination-factor method. Each takes its own N-gamma unless ngamma_method names another; 'meyerhof' = UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6, with the shape factors 1 under an inclined load (its note A); it has no base-tilt or ground-slope factors (UFC p. 294, Table 5-3), so base_tilt and ground_slope are refused with it. Hansen applies to N-gamma only: use ngamma_method='hansen'. 'terzaghi' = Terzaghi (1943): his Nc, Nq, N-gamma and shape coefficients (1.3cNc; 0.4/0.3 gamma B Ngamma square/circular), no depth or inclination factors; not for inclined loads, slopes or tilted bases (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3). allowed: vesic, meyerhof, terzaghi
ngamma_methodstroptionalNgamma factor method. Default depends on factor_method: the method's own, 'vesic' = 2(Nq+1)tan(phi) (GEC-6 Eq. 5-8), 'meyerhof' = (Nq-1)tan(1.4 phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6), 'kumbhojkar' with factor_method='terzaghi'. 'hansen' = 1.5(Nq-1)tan(phi). Another than the method's own is a mixed method; the result's choices say so. With factor_method='terzaghi' (Terzaghi gave N-gamma only as a chart): 'kumbhojkar' (Kumbhojkar 1993 as tabulated in Das) or 'coduto' (Coduto et al. 2016 approximation, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-2); the result reports the other beside it. allowed: vesic, meyerhof, hansen, kumbhojkar, coduto
failure_modestroptionalfactor_method='terzaghi' only: 'local' applies Terzaghi's local-shear reduction c* = 2/3 c, tan(phi*) = 2/3 tan(phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-4). allowed: general, local
base_tiltfloatoptionalBase tilt angle (degrees). With factor_method 'vesic' only (GEC-6 Table 5-5 factors); 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have none and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3).
eccentricity_BfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along B (m).
eccentricity_LfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along L (m).
load_inclinationfloatoptionalLoad inclination from vertical (degrees), 0 to below 90; with factor_method 'meyerhof' below phi, as UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6 takes theta = atan(H/V) < phi' (refused at phi or more).
ground_slopefloatoptionalGround slope angle down from horizontal (degrees), 0 to 45, this tool's own limit: Vesic's g_q = (1 - tan omega)^2 is 0 at 45 deg. With factor_method 'vesic' only; 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have no ground-slope factors and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 p. 294, Table 5-3). For a footing on or near a slope GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.4 uses N_cq and N_gamma-q (Fig. 5-7).
vertical_loadfloatoptionalRequired with factor_method 'vesic', a load_inclination and a soil with cohesion (or phi = 0): the vertical load V on the footing (kN; kN/m for a strip). Vesic's load inclination factors take H = V tan(load_inclination) over V + A' c cot(phi) (Vesic 1975, EN 1997-1:2004 Annex D.4); with c = 0 that is tan(load_inclination) and V cancels. Without it the call is refused (factor_method 'meyerhof' takes the angle alone, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6).
depth_factor_methodstroptionalDepth factors for an embedded footing. 'hansen': Brinch Hansen's (1970) k = Df/B below Df/B = 1, arctan(Df/B) from 1 (UFC 3-220-20 Tables 5-7, 5-8 note B) in the factor_method's d factors (Meyerhof's: k = Df/B up to 1 as UFC Table 5-6 prints it); at phi = 0 Vesic's cohesion term adds Table 5-7's d_c = 0.4 k, as UFC Eq. 5-21 does. 'gec6' (factor_method 'vesic' only): GEC-6 Eq. 5-14 and Table 5-4, d_q on the surcharge term alone, 1.0 below Df/B = 1. 'none': no depth factors, as GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.3 advises unless the cover over the footing is competent and sure to stay. The result's choices give what each option gives. allowed: hansen, gec6, none

depth_minfloatoptionalMin depth (m).

n_pointsintoptionalPoints on the curve.
pile_areafloatoptionalCustom section (m2): the cross-section area, the steel of an H-pile or a closed pipe, the gross area of a concrete or timber pile (it gives the Nordlund displaced volume of an H-pile and of a solid pile). With pile_perimeter and pile_width it replaces diameter, wall_thickness, width or designation; pile_type still picks the GEC-12 curves (not for pipe_open: its section comes from diameter and wall_thickness).
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalCustom section: the perimeter for the side resistance (m); the box perimeter of an H-pile (GEC-12 Steps 6 and p. 247).
pile_tip_areafloatoptionalCustom section: the toe area (m2). Required for h_pile (its box area; h_pile_toe_area 'steel' takes pile_area) and pipe_closed (the gross area); a concrete or timber pile's is its pile_area when not given.
pile_widthfloatoptionalCustom section: the width or diameter b (m), an H-pile's flange width; for D/b and the width notes.
pile_depthfloatoptionalCustom section: the section's depth (m), an H-pile's; reported only.
pile_namestroptionalCustom section: its name, e.g. 'HP16x101'.
cohesive_phifloatoptionalFALLBACK drained phi' (deg) for cohesive layers under method='beta' (skin AND tip); a per-layer friction_angle on a cohesive layer wins over this global.
toe_stress_limitfloatoptionalLimit on sigma'p at the toe for the Nordlund toe resistance (kPa). Default 143.6 kPa = 3 ksf, GEC-12 Step 8; null for no limit (GEC-12's worked example did not limit it).
inside_friction_ratiofloatoptionalOpen-end pipe, unplugged case: interior over exterior unit side resistance. Default 1/3, the low end of GEC-12's 'typically on the order of 1/3 to 1/2' (Sec. 7.10.7).
open_pipe_toe_limitfloatoptionalOpen-end pipe in cohesionless soil: limiting unit toe resistance (kPa). Default 5027 kPa = 105 ksf (Tomlinson, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7); null for none.
open_pipe_methodstroptionalOpen-end pipe: 'auto' takes Tomlinson's Eq. 7-90 for a pipe under 24 in with the toe in clay and over half its length in clay (GEC-12 p. 407), else the lesser of the plugged and unplugged cases (Eqs. 7-88/7-89, 'paikowsky_whitman'). allowed: auto, paikowsky_whitman, tomlinson
cohesive_Ntfloatoptionalmethod='beta': Nt of a cohesive toe layer. Default 3 (GEC-12: a relatively low Nt in clays unless local correlations suggest higher; Table 7-9 clay 3-30). A layer's own Nt wins.
h_pile_toe_areastroptionalH-pile toe area: 'box' (depth x flange width, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7) or 'steel'. GEC-12 Step 9 leaves it to past experience and local load tests. allowed: box, steel
adhesion_curvestroptionalalpha-method: GEC-12 Fig. 7-17 curves. 'auto' = smooth steel for pipe piles, the concrete/timber/corrugated curve for H-piles (GEC-12 p. 247) and concrete or timber piles. allowed: auto, concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel
adhesion_beyond_chartstroptionalalpha method where a clay layer's su is past the end of the chart's curves (Fig. 7-17, or 7-18 where read); GEC-12 p. 247 and alpha-method Step 1 recommend API RP 2A's alpha there for highly overconsolidated clays. 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated': API alpha in a layer whose su / sigma'vo is at or above highly_overconsolidated_su_ratio, Ca held at the curve's end below it; 'chart_end': Ca held at the curve's end in every such layer (GEC-12's worked example, Vol 3 Table D-100); 'api': API alpha in every such layer. Within the curves Ca is read off Fig. 7-17 as drawn (it can exceed su). allowed: api_if_highly_overconsolidated, chart_end, api
highly_overconsolidated_su_ratiofloatoptionalalpha method: the su / sigma'vo at and above which a clay is highly overconsolidated, for adhesion_beyond_chart 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated'. GEC-12 gives no value; it is the engineer's judgment, so a run with a clay layer whose su is past the chart's curves is refused until this (or adhesion_beyond_chart 'chart_end' or 'api') is given. Ask the user, or state the value taken as a judgment call.
displaced_volumefloatoptionalNordlund displaced volume V per unit length (m3/m). Default: the steel area of an H-pile, the gross area of other piles (an open pipe as a closed pipe; its steel area, if it drives unplugged, is below GEC-12 Fig. 7-9).
adhesion_chartstroptionalalpha-method chart (GEC-12 p. 246): 'fig_7_17' (Tomlinson's Ca, recommended generally), 'fig_7_18' (Tomlinson's alpha for each clay layer's stratigraphy case: sand or sandy gravel over stiff clay, soft clay over stiff clay, stiff clay alone) or 'smaller' (the smaller Ca of the two in each layer, which p. 246 advises the inexperienced user to take). A layer's case is its fig_7_18_case, else from the profile: cohesive layers under a cohesionless layer the sand case, from the ground surface the stiff-clay case; the soft-clay case only where a layer gives it. Eq. 7-90 (open pipe) takes Ca from Fig. 7-17 whatever this is (p. 407). allowed: fig_7_17, fig_7_18, smaller
shrink_swell_depthfloatoptionalDepth (m below the ground surface) of a shrink-swell zone: no shaft resistance in cohesive soil above it (GEC-12 p. 247). Default none.
beta_coefficientsstroptionalmethod='beta': beta and Nt where a layer gives none: GEC-12 Table 7-9 by the layer's soil_class (clay 0.15-0.35, silt 0.25-0.50, sand 0.30-0.90, gravel 0.35-0.80; Steps 2b/5b), a straight line in phi' between Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends). A clay toe takes cohesive_Nt. GEC-12 prints no beta formula from phi' alone; give a layer's beta and Nt for other values (local experience, Steps 2a/5a). allowed: table_7_9
toe_phi_zonestroptionalNordlund toe: the phi near the toe. 'toe_layer' (the toe layer's toe_friction_angle or friction_angle) or 'average_3b' (averaged over the cohesionless soil from the toe to 3b below, GEC-12 Step 7c's zone). allowed: toe_layer, average_3b

make_pile_section — Create a pile section and return its geometric properties.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestrrequiredPile type. pipe_closed/pipe_open require diameter + wall_thickness; concrete_square/concrete_circular require width (side dimension OR diameter); h_pile requires designation; or a custom section (pile_area, pile_perimeter, pile_width, pile_tip_area) for any but pipe_open, timber always. allowed: pipe_closed, pipe_open, concrete_square, concrete_circular, h_pile, timber

wall_thicknessfloatoptionalPipe wall thickness (m).
widthfloatoptionalSide dimension (m) for concrete piles.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g., 'HP14x117').
EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Defaults: steel 200e6, concrete 25e6.
pile_areafloatoptionalCustom section (m2): the cross-section area, the steel of an H-pile or a closed pipe, the gross area of a concrete or timber pile (it gives the Nordlund displaced volume of an H-pile and of a solid pile). With pile_perimeter and pile_width it replaces diameter, wall_thickness, width or designation; pile_type still picks the GEC-12 curves (not for pipe_open: its section comes from diameter and wall_thickness).
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalCustom section: the perimeter for the side resistance (m); the box perimeter of an H-pile (GEC-12 Steps 6 and p. 247).
pile_tip_areafloatoptionalCustom section: the toe area (m2). Required for h_pile (its box area; h_pile_toe_area 'steel' takes pile_area) and pipe_closed (the gross area); a concrete or timber pile's is its pile_area when not given.
pile_widthfloatoptionalCustom section: the width or diameter b (m), an H-pile's flange width; for D/b and the width notes.
pile_depthfloatoptionalCustom section: the section's depth (m), an H-pile's; reported only.
pile_namestroptionalCustom section: its name, e.g. 'HP16x101'.

10.1.4 lateral_pile — Lateral pile analysis

lateral_pile_analysis — Full lateral pile analysis with p-y curves and FD solver.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestroptionalPile type. h_pile requires designation; filled_pipe also requires pile_thickness. For a solid pile/drilled shaft, use 'pipe' with no pile_thickness and set pile_E. allowed: pipe, h_pile, filled_pipe
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile Young's modulus (kPa). DEFAULT IS STEEL (200e6) — for concrete drilled shafts set this explicitly, e.g. ~25e6 gross or a reduced value (e.g. 0.3x) for cracked sections.
pile_thicknessfloatoptionalWall thickness (m) for hollow pipe. Omit for a solid section.
moment_of_inertiafloatoptionalMoment of inertia (m4). Overrides the value computed from diameter/thickness.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g. 'HP360x132') — required for pile_type 'h_pile'.
axisstroptionalBending axis — pile_type 'h_pile' only. allowed: strong, weak
fcfloatoptionalConcrete f'c (kPa) — pile_type 'filled_pipe' only.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {top, bottom, model, ...model params}. Required model params: SoftClayMatlock/StiffClayAboveWT {c, gamma, eps50}; StiffClayBelowWT {c, gamma, eps50} with ks for loading='static' or kc for 'cyclic' (kN/m3, the k of the initial line p = (k x) y; Reese, Cox & Koop, COM624P Table 3.2 / GEC 9 Table A-1: ks 135,700 / 271,400 / 542,900 and kc 54,300 / 108,600 / 217,200 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa); StiffClayBelowWT is Reese et al. (1975), stiff clay with free water: GEC 9 p. 219 keeps it for stiff clay exposed to free water at or near the ground surface, and with the groundwater at depth prefers StiffClayAboveWT (Welch & Reese) even below the water table, gamma then submerged; it does not say how near is near, so which of the two a stiff clay below the water table takes is the engineer's call: state it and why, or ask; SoftClayJeanjean {su, gamma, Gmax} (not checked against a print: neither Jeanjean 2009 nor API RP 2GEO is in the reference library; GEC 9's soft clay criterion is SoftClayMatlock); SandReese/SandAPI {phi, gamma, k} where k (kN/m3) is the k of the initial line p = (k z) y: for SandReese GEC 9 Table A-3 gives it by relative density only, loose / medium / dense 5,429 / 16,287 / 33,931 submerged and 6,786 / 24,430 / 61,076 above the water (20 / 60 / 125 and 25 / 90 / 225 lb/in3); for SandAPI API RP 2A Fig. 6.8.7-1 by phi', e.g. phi' 30 / 35 / 40: 9,260 / 22,260 / 42,510 below the water table and 12,650 / 36,970 / 75,270 above; WeakRock {qu, Er}. SandReese also takes optional construction='reese1974' (default: GEC 9 App. A.4's four-segment curve, linear -> parabola -> straight line -> p_u, A and B from Figs. A-10 and A-11) | 'simplified' (the module's own three-part curve, which no held page prints). StiffClayAboveWT with loading='cyclic' also needs n_cycles, N, the number of times the design lateral load is applied (>= 1; the references give no number to assume; Welch & Reese, COM624P Eq. 3.29, y_c = y_s + y50 C log N, so y50 times 1 + 0.6 log10 N). WeakRock (Reese 1997, FHWA GEC 9 App. A.5) also takes optional RQD (%, default 100: alpha_r = 1/3, the printed lower bound; alpha_r rises linearly to 1.0 at RQD 0), krm (default 0.0005, the softer end of 0.00005-0.0005) and rock_top (depth of the rock surface, m; default the top of the weak-rock layers that hold the layer); its gamma_r is accepted and not used (the criterion does not use the unit weight).
VtfloatoptionalLateral load at pile top (kN).
MtfloatoptionalMoment at pile top (kN-m).
head_conditionstroptionalPile head condition. allowed: free, fixed
QfloatoptionalAxial load at pile top (kN), for P-delta.
stickupfloatoptionalAbove-ground free length (m): head loads/BCs act at the top of the stickup; no soil resistance over it. pile_length stays the EMBEDDED length. Alias: free_length.
n_elementsintoptionalFinite-difference elements along the pile.
tolerancefloatoptionalConvergence tolerance on deflection (m).
max_iterationsintoptionalMost p-y iterations. If they run out, a push of the pile head decides: when the soil cannot resist the load the call fails with 'No solution: the soil cannot resist this load' and the most the pile and soil carry; otherwise the result says converged false with a message (raise max_iterations).

get_py_curve — Extract a single p-y curve at a given depth for any soil model.

ParameterTypeDescription
modelstrrequiredP-y model. Required params: clay models need {c, gamma, eps50} (StiffClayBelowWT also ks for static loading or kc for cyclic); sand models need {phi, gamma, k}; WeakRock needs {qu, Er}. allowed: SoftClayMatlock, StiffClayBelowWT, StiffClayAboveWT, SoftClayJeanjean, SandReese, SandAPI, WeakRock
zfloatoptionalDepth (m).
pile_diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter (m).
n_pointsintoptionalPoints on curve.
cfloatoptionalUndrained shear strength (kPa). For clay models.
gammafloatoptionalEffective unit weight (kN/m3).
eps50floatoptionalStrain at 50% deviator stress. For clay.
phifloatoptionalFriction angle (deg). For sand.
kfloatoptionalk of the initial line p = (k z) y (kN/m3). For sand: SandReese GEC 9 Table A-3 by relative density, SandAPI API RP 2A Fig. 6.8.7-1 by phi' (see lateral_pile_analysis layers).
constructionstroptionalSandReese curve construction. 'reese1974' (default): GEC 9 App. A.4's four-segment Reese (1974) curve, the initial line to y_k, a parabola to the m-point (p_m = B p_s at y_m = b/60), a straight line to the ultimate point (p_u = A p_s at y_u = 3b/80), then p_u; A and B from GEC 9 Figs. A-10 and A-11. 'simplified': the module's own curve, the initial line, a 1/3-power parabola through the ultimate point and API's A; no held page prints it. allowed: reese1974, simplified
qufloatoptionalUniaxial compressive strength of intact rock (kPa). For WeakRock.
ErfloatoptionalModulus of the rock mass E_m (kPa), e.g. from a pressuremeter or dilatometer test. For WeakRock.
loadingstroptionalLoading type. allowed: static, cyclic
n_cyclesintoptionalN, the number of times the design lateral load is applied (>= 1). Required with loading='cyclic' for StiffClayAboveWT, and refused otherwise; the references give no number to assume. Welch & Reese, COM624P Eqs. 3.28-3.29 (GEC 9 A-20, A-21), y_c = y_s + y50 C log N with C = 9.6 (p/pu)^4, so the static curve with y50 times 1 + 0.6 log10 N.
ksfloatoptionalk for static loading (kN/m3), the initial line p = (k x) y of StiffClayBelowWT (Reese, Cox & Koop 1975): required with loading='static' and refused with 'cyclic'. COM624P Table 3.2 (GEC 9 Table A-1): 135,700 / 271,400 / 542,900 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa.
kcfloatoptionalk for cyclic loading (kN/m3), the initial line p = (k x) y of StiffClayBelowWT: required with loading='cyclic' and refused with 'static'. COM624P Table 3.2 (GEC 9 Table A-1): 54,300 / 108,600 / 217,200 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa.
sufloatoptionalUndrained shear strength (kPa). For SoftClayJeanjean (not checked against a print).
GmaxfloatoptionalSmall-strain shear modulus (kPa). For SoftClayJeanjean.
JfloatoptionalMatlock J factor. For SoftClayMatlock, StiffClayAboveWT, SoftClayJeanjean.
gamma_rfloatoptionalRock unit weight (kN/m3). Accepted for WeakRock but not used: the weak-rock criterion (Reese 1997, GEC 9 App. A.5) does not use the unit weight.
RQDfloatoptionalRock quality designation (%), 0-100. For WeakRock: strength reduction alpha_r = 1 - (2/3) RQD/100 (1/3 at RQD 100, 1.0 at RQD 0; GEC 9 p. 231). The default 100 gives the printed lower bound alpha_r = 1/3.
krmfloatoptionalk_rm, strain at 50% of the ultimate, 0.00005-0.0005 (GEC 9 p. 232); the lower value is stiffer. For WeakRock; default 0.0005, the softer end.
rock_topfloatoptionalDepth of the rock surface below the ground (m). For WeakRock: z_r = z - rock_top is the depth below the rock surface its p_ur and K_ir use.

composite_section_ei — Uncracked transformed-section composite EI/EA for a multi-material pile section (concrete-filled steel pipe, cased grout + optional bar ring, or reinforced concrete). Feed the returned EI/inertia into lateral_pile_analysis via moment_of_inertia (at pile_E = E_ref).

ParameterTypeDescription
section_typestrrequiredfilled_pipe = concrete/grout-filled steel pipe (needs outer_diameter, wall_thickness). cased_concrete = steel casing + grout core + optional circular bar ring. reinforced_concrete = circular (diameter) or rectangular (width, height) RC, no outer steel. allowed: filled_pipe, cased_concrete, reinforced_concrete
fcfloatoptionalConcrete/grout compressive strength f'c (kPa). Ec = 4700*sqrt(f'c[MPa]) (ACI 318). Provide fc OR E_concrete.
E_concretefloatoptionalConcrete/grout Young's modulus (kPa), used directly instead of the fc correlation.
outer_diameterfloatoptionalSteel pipe/casing outer diameter (m) — filled_pipe / cased_concrete.
wall_thicknessfloatoptionalSteel pipe/casing wall thickness (m) — filled_pipe / cased_concrete.
E_steelfloatoptionalSteel casing modulus (kPa).
diameterfloatoptionalConcrete diameter (m) — circular reinforced_concrete.
widthfloatoptionalRectangular concrete breadth (m). Bending about the axis parallel to width (I = width*height^3/12).
heightfloatoptionalRectangular concrete depth (m).
n_barsintoptionalNumber of bars in the circular ring (cased_concrete / circular reinforced_concrete); refused on a filled_pipe (use cased_concrete) and on a rectangular section (use bar_layers).
bar_diameterfloatoptionalIndividual reinforcing-bar diameter (m); required with n_bars or bar_layers. Use a standard size, e.g. 0.0254 for a #8 bar.
bar_circle_diameterfloatoptionalPitch-circle diameter of the bar ring (m) — circular reinforcement.
bar_layersarrayoptionalRectangular reinforcement: array of [n_bars, y_from_centroid_m] layers (y signed; symmetric layers keep the neutral axis centred). Requires bar_diameter.
E_barfloatoptionalReinforcing-steel modulus (kPa).

10.1.5 pile_group — Pile groups

pile_group_simple — Simplified elastic vertical group analysis.

n_rowsintoptionalRows for rectangular layout.
n_colsintoptionalColumns for rectangular layout.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.

pile_group_6dof — General 6-DOF rigid cap analysis (axial + lateral + moments).

ParameterTypeDescription
n_rowsintoptionalRows for rectangular layout.
n_colsintoptionalColumns.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.

group_efficiency — Pile group axial and lateral group effects as GEC-12 and UFC 3-220-20 print them: the group efficiency factor eta_g, block failure, the row p-multiplier.

ParameterTypeDescription
n_rowsintoptionalNumber of rows (for block failure).
n_colsintoptionalNumber of columns (for block failure).
pile_diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter or width b (m).
spacingfloatoptionalCentre-to-centre pile spacing (m), both directions.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m), if it differs from spacing. eta_g takes the smaller of x and y.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m), if it differs from spacing.
soil_typestroptionalGives the group efficiency factor eta_g: 'cohesionless' (UFC's coarse-grained) or 'cohesive' (fine-grained), the stratum giving most of the resistance (GEC-12 p. 281). Driven piles, GEC-12 Secs. 7.2.2.1-7.2.2.2 (pp. 282, 284): cohesionless not underlain by a weak deposit, 1.0; clay with su < 2 ksf and the cap not in firm contact with the ground, 0.65 at s = 2.5b to 1.0 at 6b, linear between; else 1.0. Other pile types: UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26 (see pile_type). Below the table's minimum spacing (2.5b driven piles and drilled shafts, 3b the others) the call is refused. The group resistance is the lesser of n*eta_g*R_n and block failure. allowed: cohesionless, cohesive
cap_in_contactbooloptionalWhether the pile cap is in firm contact with the ground (sets eta_g's row). Left out where the row depends on it, the lower eta_g (not in contact) is taken and the result's choices give the other.
cufloatoptionalUndrained shear strength of the clay (kPa): sets eta_g's row against 2 ksf (95.76 kPa) for soil_type 'cohesive' (left out where it matters, su < 2 ksf is taken, said in the choices); and, for block failure, su1 and su2 where those are not given.
pile_typestroptionalThe column of UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26 for eta_g: 'driven' (GEC-12), 'drilled_shaft', 'cfa', 'ddp' (drilled displacement) or 'micropile'; and the resistance factor for block failure: 0.60 driven (GEC-12 Table 7-1, p. 224), 0.55 drilled shafts, 0.60 micropiles (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-27, p. 433); none printed for 'cfa' or 'ddp' (nominal only). allowed: driven, drilled_shaft, cfa, ddp, micropile
pile_lengthfloatoptionalPile embedded length D (m). With su1 and su2 (or cu), n_rows, n_cols, spacing and pile_diameter, gives the resistance to block failure: GEC-12 Eq. 7-36, R = 2D(B+Z)su1 + B*Z*su2*Nc, Nc = 5[1 + D/(5B)][1 + B/(5Z)] <= 9 (Eq. 7-37), B and Z the group's width and length to the outer pile faces (Fig. 7-31). Nominal, and factored by pile_type's printed resistance factor (block_failure_factored_kN).
su1floatoptionalBlock failure: weighted average undrained shear strength along the group's perimeter over the embedded length (kPa); for cohesionless soils along the sides, their weighted average unit shaft resistance (GEC-12 p. 287).
su2floatoptionalBlock failure: average undrained shear strength below the toes to a depth of 2B (kPa; UFC 3-220-20 p. 433: 2B to 3B, whichever lower), that of the weak layer for a group in sand over it.
row_positionintoptionalRow number, 1 = the lead row (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 6-25): gives the row's lateral p-multiplier p_m.
spacing_diameter_ratiofloatoptionals/b for the p-multiplier, s the spacing of the rows in the direction of the load (from spacing/pile_diameter if omitted). Below 3 the call is refused (p_m is printed from 3b).
p_multiplier_methodstroptional'aashto' (default): AASHTO's p_m as GEC-12 prints it (pp. 367, 370): rows 1, 2, 3+ = 0.8, 0.4, 0.3 at 3b and 1.0, 0.85, 0.7 at 5b, interpolated (0.90, 0.625, 0.5 at 4b, as GEC-12 Vol. III takes them), to 1.0 at 6b and beyond (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-38). 'mokwa': Mokwa (1999), UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-38: p_m = 0.06(s/b)+0.64, 0.11(s/b)+0.34, 0.14(s/b)+0.16, 0.16(s/b)+0.04 for rows 1, 2, 3, 4+, each <= 1. allowed: aashto, mokwa

meyerhof_group_settlement — Meyerhof (1976) SPT pile-group settlement in sand, GEC-12 Eqs. 7-50 to 7-52: S[in] = 4·pf[ksf]·If·√B[ft]/N1(60) (8 for silty sand). SI in, mm out.

ParameterTypeDescription
group_widthfloatrequiredGroup plan width B, the SMALLER plan dimension (m).
group_lengthfloatrequiredGroup plan length Z, the larger plan dimension (m). Used with group_width to form the plan area when load_kN is given.
N160floatrequiredAverage corrected SPT N1(60) within a depth B below the pile toe (dimensionless).
load_kNfloatoptionalTotal unfactored permanent load Q (kN); pf = Q/(B·Z), B and Z to the outer pile faces (GEC-12 Vol. III p. 62). Provide this OR pf_kPa.
pf_kPafloatoptionalDesign foundation pressure pf (kPa), supplied directly. Takes precedence over load_kN. Provide this OR load_kN.
embedment_DBfloatoptionalThe embedment D whose 2/3 is D' in If = 1 − D'/(8B) >= 0.5 (Eq. 7-52), m. GEC-12 Vol. I p. 319 and UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 6-47 take the pile embedded length; GEC-12 Vol. III Table D-23 the embedment into the bearing stratum. Default 0.0 (If = 1.0, the upper bound).
silty_sandbooloptionalTrue: Eq. 7-51 for silty sand (coefficient 8, twice Eq. 7-50's).

10.1.6 drilled_shaft — Drilled shafts

drilled_shaft_capacity — Full drilled shaft capacity (GEC-10 alpha/beta/rock socket).

ParameterTypeDescription
diameterfloatrequiredShaft diameter (m).
shaft_lengthfloatrequiredShaft length (m). Alias: length.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, cu, phi, N60, qu, RQD} dicts. soil_type: cohesive/cohesionless/rock. A cohesionless layer at the shaft tip needs its N60 (end bearing q_b = 57.5*N60 kPa, GEC-10 Eq. 10-14, N60 the mean of the cohesionless layers' N60 between the base and two base diameters below it, by thickness, limited to 50, p. 10-15; a layer there with no N60, or of cohesive soil or rock, is left out); without it the call is refused. Under beta_method 'rational' (the default, GEC-10 2018 Eq. 10-13) each cohesionless layer the shaft passes through needs its N60 (sigma'p by Eq. 10-11 or 10-12) or a direct OCR, else the call is refused; it also takes N1_60 (overburden-corrected SPT; phi' = 27.5+9.2*log10[(N1)60], GEC-10 Example 10-1 and Eq. A-2, where the layer gives no phi; a phi given is used and the result's choices give the correlation's value beside it), sigma_p_correlation ('clean_sand' default: Eq. 10-11 with m = 0.6, clean quartzitic sands; 'silty_sand': m = 0.8, silty sands to sandy silts; 'gravel': Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15*N60, gravelly soils; GEC-10 p. 10-11) and sigma_v_ref (kPa, pre-scour effective stress for the OCR; default the layer's own sigma'v). A rock layer's RQD (default 100) sets alpha_E of the side resistance under rock_side_method 'caving' (GEC-10 Table 10-3) and the base under rock_base_method 'rqd'; under the default 'gec10' an RQD below 100 within one base diameter below the base needs rock_base_conditions_met, or the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i. A rock layer also takes GSI (Geological Strength Index of the rock mass, 0 to 100, from the core descriptions; GEC-10 p. 10-23 names GSI, not RMR) and m_i (Hoek-Brown constant of the intact rock, by rock type, GEC 5 Table 9-10, as GEC-10 p. 10-24 points to): with the base in that layer they give GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29, taken where the rock is not taken to meet the conditions of Eq. 10-23 and shown beside 2.5*qu where it is (see rock_base_conditions_met); a rock layer within one base diameter below the base that gives them has its own Hoek-Brown base among the result's alternatives. GSI or m_i on any other layer (above the base, further below it, or with the base in soil) is refused: nothing would use them; capacity_vs_depth takes them on any layer a trial base is in.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety.
beta_methodstroptionalCohesionless side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Eqs. 10-5 to 10-13 (pp. 10-10 to 10-12): f_SN = beta*sigma'v on each layer's average sigma'v, beta = (K/Ko)*Ko*tan(phi'), Ko = (1-sin phi')*OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR = sigma'p/sigma'v, sigma'p from the layer's N60 (Eq. 10-11 or 10-12), beta limited to its value at 7.5 ft, no limit on f_SN; needs each cohesionless layer's N60 or OCR. 'depth' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) beta = 1.5-0.135*sqrt(z, ft) = 1.5-0.245*sqrt(z, m), 0.25-1.2, x N60/15 where N60 < 15, f_s <= 4 ksf = 191.5 kPa (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43, the limit p. 9-133), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print. allowed: rational, depth
K_over_KofloatoptionalK/Ko in the GEC-10 beta (beta_method 'rational'): 1 = 'a rational first-order approximation', no stress change from construction (GEC-10 p. 10-11); 2/3 or lower 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly' or soil caving is allowed (p. 10-12). 0 < K_over_Ko <= 1.
top_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the top of the shaft (m), in every layer, when given. Left out: none over the top 1.5 m in cohesive soil, GEC-10's 'top 5 ft' (p. 10-17, printed in Sec. 10.3.5.2 for cohesive soils, 'or to the depth of seasonal moisture change', 'subject to modification based on local experience and judgment of the designer'), and side resistance from the top in cohesionless soil and rock (Secs. 10.3.5.1 and 10.3.5.3 print no such zone; Examples 10-1 and 10-5 take the sand's from the surface, Example 10-4 the socket's over its whole length). Give 1.5 to leave the top 5 ft out of sand and rock too (frost, seasonal moisture, gapping from cyclic lateral load), or the depth of seasonal moisture change. casing_depth, where deeper, takes its place.
bottom_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the bottom of the shaft (m) in cohesive soil. Default 0: GEC-10 (2018) prints no such zone, and Example 10-2 (p. 10-18) takes the clay's side resistance to the base. FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 9-129 (O'Neill & Reese 1999) leaves out the bottom 5 ft (1.524 m), its Fig. 9-49 the bottom one diameter (give the diameter for that).
alpha_methodstroptionalCohesive side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.2, Eq. 10-18 (p. 10-16): alpha = 0.30+0.17/(su(CIUC)/pa), f_SN = alpha*su(CIUC), su(CIUC) from cu by su_test_type. 'aashto' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) as FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-37a/b print it (p. 9-129): alpha = 0.55 for cu/pa <= 1.5, 0.55-0.1*(cu/pa-1.5) to 2.5, on cu; GEC-10 recommends Eq. 10-18 'as a revision' to it. allowed: rational, aashto
su_test_typestroptionalFor alpha_method 'rational': the lab test each layer's cu came from. 'ciuc' (default) = cu taken as su(CIUC), no transform; 'uc' / 'uu' = transformed to su(CIUC) on the layer's sigma'vo by GEC-10 Eq. 10-16 / 10-17 (Chen & Kulhawy 1993, p. 10-16; Example 10-2 takes a UU strength). The base in clay takes the same su(CIUC) (Example 10-3). allowed: ciuc, uc, uu
clay_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in cohesive soil. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) p. 10-19: q_BN = N*c*su (Eq. 10-19), su the mean of the cohesive soil over 2B below the base, by thickness (p. 10-19; the tip layer at its su(CIUC) as its side resistance took it, each clay layer below on its own cu, transformed alike; cohesionless or rock layers within 2B left out; where the profile ends short of 2B, the mean of what it gives, said in the choices), N*c from Table 10-2 by su (6.5 at 500 psf, 8.0 at 1,000 psf, 9.0 at 2,000 psf or more; held at 6.5 below 500 psf), (2/3)[1 + D/(6B)]*N*c*su where the depth D < 3B (Eq. 10-20), no upper limit. 'oneill_reese' = FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-39, 9-40 (p. 9-131): Nc = 6[1 + 0.2 z/D] <= 9, x 0.67 where su < 0.5 ksf, q_t <= 80 ksf, on the tip layer's cu. allowed: gec10, oneill_reese
rock_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in rock. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Eq. 10-23 (p. 10-22): q_BN = 2.5*qu, for rock massive or tightly jointed to one diameter below the base, no cavities beneath, a clean base (Example 10-4 takes it with RQD 37 to 100); for a fractured rock mass the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29 (pp. 10-23, 10-24; Turner and Ramey 2010): m_b = m_i*exp((GSI-100)/28), s = exp((GSI-100)/9), a = 1/2+(1/6)(exp(-GSI/15)-exp(-20/3)), A = sigma'vb + qu*(m_b*sigma'vb/qu + s)^a, q_BN = A + qu*(m_b*A/qu + s)^a, q_BN/qu limited to 2.5 (p. 10-24), on the tip rock layer's qu, GSI and m_i and the vertical effective stress at the base; resistance factor 0.50 (p. 10-24, Table 8-4); which of the two by rock_base_conditions_met. 'rqd' = q_b/q_u reduced by the tip rock's RQD below 70 (1.5 at 50, 0.8 at 25, 0.4 at 0), cited to GEC-10's 2010 edition, not in the reference library, and not a method GEC-10 Table 8-4 gives a resistance factor for. allowed: gec10, rqd
rock_base_conditions_metbooloptionalFor rock_base_method 'gec10' with the tip in rock: whether the rock below the base meets the three conditions GEC-10 p. 10-22 sets on q_BN = 2.5*qu (massive or tightly jointed, no compressible seams or joints, to at least one diameter below the base; no solution cavities or voids beneath it; a clean base achieved and verified). The engineer's judgment: Example 10-4 takes 2.5 with RQD 37 to 100 because 'Rock coring and local experience indicate the rock mass below the socket tip is competent'. true = 2.5*qu (Eq. 10-23) as stated. false = GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base (Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29), on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i; refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them. Left out = taken as met, said in the result's choices, where every layer within one base diameter below the base is rock with RQD 100 (the layer default), with the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i beside it where they are given; where a layer there has an RQD below 100 or is soil, the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i (2.5*qu bounds it above), and the call is refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them.
large_base_reductionbooloptionalO'Neill & Reese's (1999) reduction of base resistance for a large base: 1.27/B in cohesionless soil for a base wider than 1.27 m, F_r = 2.5/(a*B + 2.5*b) <= 1 in cohesive soil for a base wider than 1.90 m (B the bell's where there is one). Default false: GEC-10 (2018) prints neither (Eqs. 10-14, 10-19, 10-20); true applies it.
pafloatoptionalAtmospheric pressure (kPa) for the rational chains.
rock_side_CfloatoptionalC in the rock side resistance f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) (GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, p. 10-20). Default 1.0, 'recommended for design of "normal" rock sockets' (pp. 10-20, 10-21; Example 10-4): conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls, no caving, no smearing. 0.65 = the value of Eq. 10-22 with alpha_E = 1.0 (rock_side_method 'caving' takes alpha_E from Table 10-3 by RQD). 1.9 for roughened sockets, verified by load tests or local experience (p. 10-22). For rock_side_method 'normal'; refused with 'caving', which takes no C. Needs a rock layer.
rock_side_methodstroptionalRock side resistance. 'normal' (default) = GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) with rock_side_C, for a 'normal' socket: conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls (pp. 10-20, 10-21). 'caving' = Eq. 10-22 (O'Neill and Reese 1999), f_s = 0.65*alpha_E*pa*sqrt(qu/pa), alpha_E from Table 10-3 (p. 10-21) by each rock layer's RQD and rock_joints (closed joints 1.00, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.45; open or gouge-filled 0.85, 0.55, 0.55, 0.50, 0.45 at RQD 100, 70, 50, 30, 20 %; linear between the rows, held at 0.45 below RQD 20), for highly fractured or weathered rock that cannot be drilled without artificial support (casing, plug-ahead) or where caving is anticipated. Needs a rock layer. allowed: normal, caving
rock_jointsstroptionalFor rock_side_method 'caving': the joint condition of GEC-10 Table 10-3, 'closed' (default) or 'open' (open or gouge-filled joints), from the cores. allowed: closed, open
socket_diameterfloatoptionalRock socket diameter (m). Defaults to shaft diameter. One diameter for every rock layer: GEC-10 sizes a socket by one diameter B (Eq. 10-21, Example 10-4) and gives none per rock layer. The rock side resistance and, with the tip in rock, the base (pi/4*B^2, GEC-10 Example 10-4, p. 10-28) take it.
bell_diameterfloatoptionalBelled base diameter (m).
casing_depthfloatoptionalPermanent casing depth (m, no side resistance).
fractured_rock_thicknessfloatoptionalDecomposed or fractured rock (m) below the top of the first rock layer that is 'not considered part of the socket for design purposes' (GEC-10 p. 8-15): no rock side resistance over it, while the soil above keeps its own (casing_depth takes both). 0 = all rock is socket. Needs a rock layer.
concrete_fcfloatoptionalCompressive strength f'c of the shaft concrete (kPa; 28 MPa = 28000, at least 1000). The rock side resistance takes qu no higher than it: 'For design, the value of qu used in Equation 10-21 should not exceed the compressive strength of the drilled shaft concrete' (GEC-10 p. 10-21; Example 10-4 gives qu 360 ksf and f'c 576 ksf), in Eq. 10-22 alike. Left out, that limit is not checked and the result's choices say so. No structural check of the shaft is made. Needs a rock layer.

lrfd_capacity — Drilled shaft capacity with the LRFD resistance factors of GEC-10 Table 8-4.

ParameterTypeDescription
diameterfloatrequiredShaft diameter (m).
shaft_lengthfloatrequiredShaft length (m). Alias: length.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, cu, phi, N60, qu, RQD} dicts. soil_type: cohesive/cohesionless/rock. A cohesionless layer at the shaft tip needs its N60 (end bearing q_b = 57.5*N60 kPa, GEC-10 Eq. 10-14, N60 the mean of the cohesionless layers' N60 between the base and two base diameters below it, by thickness, limited to 50, p. 10-15; a layer there with no N60, or of cohesive soil or rock, is left out); without it the call is refused. Under beta_method 'rational' (the default, GEC-10 2018 Eq. 10-13) each cohesionless layer the shaft passes through needs its N60 (sigma'p by Eq. 10-11 or 10-12) or a direct OCR, else the call is refused; it also takes N1_60 (overburden-corrected SPT; phi' = 27.5+9.2*log10[(N1)60], GEC-10 Example 10-1 and Eq. A-2, where the layer gives no phi; a phi given is used and the result's choices give the correlation's value beside it), sigma_p_correlation ('clean_sand' default: Eq. 10-11 with m = 0.6, clean quartzitic sands; 'silty_sand': m = 0.8, silty sands to sandy silts; 'gravel': Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15*N60, gravelly soils; GEC-10 p. 10-11) and sigma_v_ref (kPa, pre-scour effective stress for the OCR; default the layer's own sigma'v). A rock layer's RQD (default 100) sets alpha_E of the side resistance under rock_side_method 'caving' (GEC-10 Table 10-3) and the base under rock_base_method 'rqd'; under the default 'gec10' an RQD below 100 within one base diameter below the base needs rock_base_conditions_met, or the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i. A rock layer also takes GSI (Geological Strength Index of the rock mass, 0 to 100, from the core descriptions; GEC-10 p. 10-23 names GSI, not RMR) and m_i (Hoek-Brown constant of the intact rock, by rock type, GEC 5 Table 9-10, as GEC-10 p. 10-24 points to): with the base in that layer they give GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29, taken where the rock is not taken to meet the conditions of Eq. 10-23 and shown beside 2.5*qu where it is (see rock_base_conditions_met); a rock layer within one base diameter below the base that gives them has its own Hoek-Brown base among the result's alternatives. GSI or m_i on any other layer (above the base, further below it, or with the base in soil) is refused: nothing would use them; capacity_vs_depth takes them on any layer a trial base is in.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
tip_soil_typestroptionalSoil type at the shaft tip, for the base resistance factor (GEC-10 Table 8-4: 0.40 cohesive, 0.50 cohesionless and rock). Left out, the soil of the layer the base is in; given, it must be that soil, else the call is refused. allowed: cohesive, cohesionless, rock
beta_methodstroptionalCohesionless side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Eqs. 10-5 to 10-13 (pp. 10-10 to 10-12): f_SN = beta*sigma'v on each layer's average sigma'v, beta = (K/Ko)*Ko*tan(phi'), Ko = (1-sin phi')*OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR = sigma'p/sigma'v, sigma'p from the layer's N60 (Eq. 10-11 or 10-12), beta limited to its value at 7.5 ft, no limit on f_SN; needs each cohesionless layer's N60 or OCR. 'depth' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) beta = 1.5-0.135*sqrt(z, ft) = 1.5-0.245*sqrt(z, m), 0.25-1.2, x N60/15 where N60 < 15, f_s <= 4 ksf = 191.5 kPa (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43, the limit p. 9-133), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print. allowed: rational, depth
K_over_KofloatoptionalK/Ko in the GEC-10 beta (beta_method 'rational'): 1 = 'a rational first-order approximation', no stress change from construction (GEC-10 p. 10-11); 2/3 or lower 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly' or soil caving is allowed (p. 10-12). 0 < K_over_Ko <= 1.
top_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the top of the shaft (m), in every layer, when given. Left out: none over the top 1.5 m in cohesive soil, GEC-10's 'top 5 ft' (p. 10-17, printed in Sec. 10.3.5.2 for cohesive soils, 'or to the depth of seasonal moisture change', 'subject to modification based on local experience and judgment of the designer'), and side resistance from the top in cohesionless soil and rock (Secs. 10.3.5.1 and 10.3.5.3 print no such zone; Examples 10-1 and 10-5 take the sand's from the surface, Example 10-4 the socket's over its whole length). Give 1.5 to leave the top 5 ft out of sand and rock too (frost, seasonal moisture, gapping from cyclic lateral load), or the depth of seasonal moisture change. casing_depth, where deeper, takes its place.
bottom_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the bottom of the shaft (m) in cohesive soil. Default 0: GEC-10 (2018) prints no such zone, and Example 10-2 (p. 10-18) takes the clay's side resistance to the base. FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 9-129 (O'Neill & Reese 1999) leaves out the bottom 5 ft (1.524 m), its Fig. 9-49 the bottom one diameter (give the diameter for that).
alpha_methodstroptionalCohesive side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.2, Eq. 10-18 (p. 10-16): alpha = 0.30+0.17/(su(CIUC)/pa), f_SN = alpha*su(CIUC), su(CIUC) from cu by su_test_type. 'aashto' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) as FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-37a/b print it (p. 9-129): alpha = 0.55 for cu/pa <= 1.5, 0.55-0.1*(cu/pa-1.5) to 2.5, on cu; GEC-10 recommends Eq. 10-18 'as a revision' to it. allowed: rational, aashto
su_test_typestroptionalFor alpha_method 'rational': the lab test each layer's cu came from. 'ciuc' (default) = cu taken as su(CIUC), no transform; 'uc' / 'uu' = transformed to su(CIUC) on the layer's sigma'vo by GEC-10 Eq. 10-16 / 10-17 (Chen & Kulhawy 1993, p. 10-16; Example 10-2 takes a UU strength). The base in clay takes the same su(CIUC) (Example 10-3). allowed: ciuc, uc, uu
clay_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in cohesive soil. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) p. 10-19: q_BN = N*c*su (Eq. 10-19), su the mean of the cohesive soil over 2B below the base, by thickness (p. 10-19; the tip layer at its su(CIUC) as its side resistance took it, each clay layer below on its own cu, transformed alike; cohesionless or rock layers within 2B left out; where the profile ends short of 2B, the mean of what it gives, said in the choices), N*c from Table 10-2 by su (6.5 at 500 psf, 8.0 at 1,000 psf, 9.0 at 2,000 psf or more; held at 6.5 below 500 psf), (2/3)[1 + D/(6B)]*N*c*su where the depth D < 3B (Eq. 10-20), no upper limit. 'oneill_reese' = FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-39, 9-40 (p. 9-131): Nc = 6[1 + 0.2 z/D] <= 9, x 0.67 where su < 0.5 ksf, q_t <= 80 ksf, on the tip layer's cu. allowed: gec10, oneill_reese
rock_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in rock. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Eq. 10-23 (p. 10-22): q_BN = 2.5*qu, for rock massive or tightly jointed to one diameter below the base, no cavities beneath, a clean base (Example 10-4 takes it with RQD 37 to 100); for a fractured rock mass the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29 (pp. 10-23, 10-24; Turner and Ramey 2010): m_b = m_i*exp((GSI-100)/28), s = exp((GSI-100)/9), a = 1/2+(1/6)(exp(-GSI/15)-exp(-20/3)), A = sigma'vb + qu*(m_b*sigma'vb/qu + s)^a, q_BN = A + qu*(m_b*A/qu + s)^a, q_BN/qu limited to 2.5 (p. 10-24), on the tip rock layer's qu, GSI and m_i and the vertical effective stress at the base; resistance factor 0.50 (p. 10-24, Table 8-4); which of the two by rock_base_conditions_met. 'rqd' = q_b/q_u reduced by the tip rock's RQD below 70 (1.5 at 50, 0.8 at 25, 0.4 at 0), cited to GEC-10's 2010 edition, not in the reference library, and not a method GEC-10 Table 8-4 gives a resistance factor for. allowed: gec10, rqd
rock_base_conditions_metbooloptionalFor rock_base_method 'gec10' with the tip in rock: whether the rock below the base meets the three conditions GEC-10 p. 10-22 sets on q_BN = 2.5*qu (massive or tightly jointed, no compressible seams or joints, to at least one diameter below the base; no solution cavities or voids beneath it; a clean base achieved and verified). The engineer's judgment: Example 10-4 takes 2.5 with RQD 37 to 100 because 'Rock coring and local experience indicate the rock mass below the socket tip is competent'. true = 2.5*qu (Eq. 10-23) as stated. false = GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base (Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29), on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i; refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them. Left out = taken as met, said in the result's choices, where every layer within one base diameter below the base is rock with RQD 100 (the layer default), with the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i beside it where they are given; where a layer there has an RQD below 100 or is soil, the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i (2.5*qu bounds it above), and the call is refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them.
large_base_reductionbooloptionalO'Neill & Reese's (1999) reduction of base resistance for a large base: 1.27/B in cohesionless soil for a base wider than 1.27 m, F_r = 2.5/(a*B + 2.5*b) <= 1 in cohesive soil for a base wider than 1.90 m (B the bell's where there is one). Default false: GEC-10 (2018) prints neither (Eqs. 10-14, 10-19, 10-20); true applies it.
pafloatoptionalAtmospheric pressure (kPa) for the rational chains.
rock_side_CfloatoptionalC in the rock side resistance f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) (GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, p. 10-20). Default 1.0, 'recommended for design of "normal" rock sockets' (pp. 10-20, 10-21; Example 10-4): conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls, no caving, no smearing. 0.65 = the value of Eq. 10-22 with alpha_E = 1.0 (rock_side_method 'caving' takes alpha_E from Table 10-3 by RQD). 1.9 for roughened sockets, verified by load tests or local experience (p. 10-22). For rock_side_method 'normal'; refused with 'caving', which takes no C. Needs a rock layer.
rock_side_methodstroptionalRock side resistance. 'normal' (default) = GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) with rock_side_C, for a 'normal' socket: conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls (pp. 10-20, 10-21). 'caving' = Eq. 10-22 (O'Neill and Reese 1999), f_s = 0.65*alpha_E*pa*sqrt(qu/pa), alpha_E from Table 10-3 (p. 10-21) by each rock layer's RQD and rock_joints (closed joints 1.00, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.45; open or gouge-filled 0.85, 0.55, 0.55, 0.50, 0.45 at RQD 100, 70, 50, 30, 20 %; linear between the rows, held at 0.45 below RQD 20), for highly fractured or weathered rock that cannot be drilled without artificial support (casing, plug-ahead) or where caving is anticipated. Needs a rock layer. allowed: normal, caving
rock_jointsstroptionalFor rock_side_method 'caving': the joint condition of GEC-10 Table 10-3, 'closed' (default) or 'open' (open or gouge-filled joints), from the cores. allowed: closed, open
socket_diameterfloatoptionalRock socket diameter (m). Defaults to shaft diameter. One diameter for every rock layer: GEC-10 sizes a socket by one diameter B (Eq. 10-21, Example 10-4) and gives none per rock layer. The rock side resistance and, with the tip in rock, the base (pi/4*B^2, GEC-10 Example 10-4, p. 10-28) take it.
bell_diameterfloatoptionalBelled base diameter (m).
casing_depthfloatoptionalPermanent casing depth (m, no side resistance).
fractured_rock_thicknessfloatoptionalDecomposed or fractured rock (m) below the top of the first rock layer that is 'not considered part of the socket for design purposes' (GEC-10 p. 8-15): no rock side resistance over it, while the soil above keeps its own (casing_depth takes both). 0 = all rock is socket. Needs a rock layer.
concrete_fcfloatoptionalCompressive strength f'c of the shaft concrete (kPa; 28 MPa = 28000, at least 1000). The rock side resistance takes qu no higher than it: 'For design, the value of qu used in Equation 10-21 should not exceed the compressive strength of the drilled shaft concrete' (GEC-10 p. 10-21; Example 10-4 gives qu 360 ksf and f'c 576 ksf), in Eq. 10-22 alike. Left out, that limit is not checked and the result's choices say so. No structural check of the shaft is made. Needs a rock layer.

10.1.8 downdrag — Downdrag / neutral plane

downdrag_analysis — Downdrag (negative skin friction), neutral plane method: every method's neutral plane and drag force side by side.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, phi, cu, beta, alpha, skin_friction_method, soil_class, settling, description} dicts. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay'/'settling_fill'). Skin friction: cohesionless = beta x sigma'v (Beta method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-7), beta as given, else from phi' by GEC-12 Table 7-9 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-15, driven piles) for the layer's soil_class ('silt' 0.25-0.50 over 28-34 deg, 'sand' 0.30-0.90 over 32-40 deg, the default, 'gravel' 0.35-0.80 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; soil_class also picks the toe's Nt row (Nt_method); cohesive = alpha x cu (Alpha method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-8, the default; alpha as given, else read off alpha_chart: UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-16 and Fig 6-14 by default), or with skin_friction_method 'beta' beta x sigma'v for long-term, drained conditions (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.1; GEC-12 7.2.1.3.4), beta required (GEC-12 Table 7-9: clay 0.15-0.35; cu then only for a toe in the layer). A cohesive layer takes no phi, and beta only with skin_friction_method 'beta'; a cohesionless layer takes no alpha. Mark settling layers with settling=True; a settling layer also needs its compressibility: cohesionless -> E_s (elastic modulus, kPa, > 0) and optional nu_s; cohesive -> Cc and e0 (optional Cr, sigma_p kPa) or C_ec/C_er.
Q_deadfloatoptionalDead load at pile top (kN).
fill_thicknessfloatoptionalFill thickness causing downdrag (m).
fill_unit_weightfloatoptionalFill unit weight (kN/m3).
gw_drawdownfloatoptionalGroundwater drawdown (m).
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default is steel.
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalPile perimeter (m). Computed from diameter if omitted.
pile_areafloatoptionalPile cross-section area (m2). Computed from diameter if omitted.
structural_capacityfloatoptionalPile structural capacity (kN) for the max-load check.
allowable_settlementfloatoptionalAllowable pile settlement (m) for the settlement check.
NtfloatoptionalToe bearing capacity factor: R_toe = Nt x sigma'v(toe) x A_toe in cohesionless soil, Nt x cu x A_toe in cohesive. Give the MOBILIZED value -- the toe resistance actually developed at the pile's settlement -- not the ultimate. Omitted, Nt is the ULTIMATE value: 9 in clay (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.3.3), and in cohesionless soil from the toe layer's phi' by Nt_method (60-120 in dense sand at 34-38 deg by the default); then the load and resistance curves often do not intersect and the neutral plane is where the pile and soil settle equally, the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; see neutral_plane_method). UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.2: check 0 %, 50 % and 100 % toe mobilization.
Nt_methodstringoptionalWhere a cohesionless toe's ultimate Nt comes from when Nt is not given, both UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17 (p. 421; qb = Nq sigma'zD, Eq 6-20): 'fellenius' (default) = its Fellenius (2021) column, the same values as GEC-12 Table 7-9, by the toe layer's soil_class (silt 20-40 over 28-34 deg, sand 30-150 over 32-40 deg, gravel 60-300 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; 'cheng' = its equation after Cheng (2004), Nq ~= 1.2 (Z/b)^-0.437 exp[6.34 (Z/b)^0.0486 tan phi'], Z the pile length and b pile_diameter, at most 200 unless project-specific information supports more (give Nt then). The result's choices give the other route's value. allowed: fellenius, cheng
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3), times pile_area for the pile's own weight; used only when include_pile_weight is true. Default 78.5 = steel, the same material as the pile_E default (concrete is about 24). For an H or pipe pile give pile_area as the steel area (pile_area defaults to the solid circle).
include_pile_weightbooloptionalWhether the load curve carries the pile's own weight. Default false: left out, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 7.3.6.1 (and their worked examples) do. True adds the weight of the pile above the neutral plane to Q_np and the drag force.
n_sublayersintoptionalSublayers per soil layer for the depth discretization.
neutral_plane_methodstringoptionalWhich method gives the reported numbers; every method is evaluated and returned in neutral_plane_comparison whatever is chosen. 'auto' (default) = the UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 procedure: the intersection of the load and resistance curves with the toe at toe_mobilization, or, when they do not intersect, where the pile and soil settle equally with the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 6-5.8.4.3, Fig 6-19). 'force_equilibrium' (the curves' intersection only; error if they do not intersect); 'settlement_compatibility' (pile and soil settle equally, toe force compatible with the toe penetration); 'bearing_layer_top' (top of the bearing layer, end-bearing pile, UFC 6-7.4 step 5); 'pile_toe' (whole shaft in negative skin friction, upper bound); 'endo' (Endo et al. 1969, CGPR #56 Table 3.1 fraction of the embedment; needs endo_bearing_condition). allowed: auto, force_equilibrium, settlement_compatibility, bearing_layer_top, pile_toe, endo
toe_mobilizationfloatoptionalFraction (0-1) of the nominal toe resistance mobilized where the load and resistance curves intersect. 1.0 = UFC 6-7.4 step 3 full mobilization ('a conservative approach for evaluating the drag force'); 0.5 and 0 = the other UFC 6-5.8.4.2 / GEC-12 7.3.6.1 cases for settlement (all three always reported in the comparison).
endo_bearing_conditionstringoptionalCGPR #56 Table 3.1 condition for Endo et al. (1969). allowed: floating, stiff_flexible, end_bearing
skin_friction_stressstringoptionalEffective stress for Beta-method skin friction (sand, and clay with skin_friction_method 'beta') and the sand toe: 'final' (default; sigma'v0 + fill/drawdown change, as UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 step 2 requires) or 'initial' (sigma'v0). allowed: final, initial
influence_depth_criterionstringoptionalHow deep below the toe the toe load is counted in the settlement (toe force spread 2V:1H from an equivalent footing as wide as the pile): to where its stress increase falls below 'bearing_stress' (default) = 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; 2.16 pile widths for a single pile) or 'effective_stress' = 10% of the existing vertical effective stress (FHWA GEC-12 Vol I step 1c: 7.3.5.3 for clay below the toe, 7.3.5.6 for sand, 7.3.5.5 for both; deeper for a loaded toe in soft soil). Either way the fill / drawdown, which does not decay with depth, compresses the settling layers below the toe down to the bottom of the soil profile; give the profile down to the base of the compressible soil. allowed: bearing_stress, effective_stress
influence_depth_warning_percentfloatoptionalThe result warns when the two influence_depth_criterion rules (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3 and FHWA GEC-12 step 1c) give pile head settlements or drag forces that differ by more than this percentage of the larger of the two (of allowable_settlement / structural_capacity where given), and whenever a settlement or structural check passes with one rule and fails with the other. The rule used is not changed. Default 25 %: the engineer's call, not a reference's figure; neither reference says how far two settlement estimates may differ before it matters.
alpha_chartstringoptionalWhere a cohesive layer's alpha comes from when the layer leaves it out (a given alpha is kept). 'ufc_fig_6_14' (default; UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.2, pp. 415-417, as its drag example App. B-5.4 reads it): soft clay (su below 800 psf) alpha 1 by Table 6-16; firm to very stiff clay off Fig 6-14 by su/Pa, curve A at Z of 40b or more, curve B at Z = 10b, linear between, Z from the ground surface to the clay's base or the pile toe and b = pile_diameter. 'gec12_fig_7_17': FHWA GEC-12 7.2.1.3.2 Step 1, Ca off Fig. 7-17 by su, D/b and fig_7_17_curve, as drawn (Ca may exceed su). choices states each clay's alpha and where it came from. Refused (with fig_7_17_curve and alpha_transition_zone) where no cohesive layer along the pile leaves alpha out. allowed: ufc_fig_6_14, gec12_fig_7_17
fig_7_17_curvestringoptionalWith alpha_chart 'gec12_fig_7_17' only, and then required where a clay leaves alpha out: the Fig. 7-17 curves for the pile, 'concrete_timber_corrugated' (concrete, timber or corrugated steel; an H-pile takes the corrugated curve, GEC-12 p. 247) or 'smooth_steel'. allowed: concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel
alpha_transition_zonebooloptionalWhether the top 10 pile widths of a stiff or very stiff clay (su 1500 psf or more) directly under soft clay take UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-9, alpha = 0.28 (su/Pa)^-0.44 with the unit side resistance at least the soft clay's, and under sand alpha 1.0 (pp. 416-417, as App. B-5.4 does). Left out: true with alpha_chart 'ufc_fig_6_14', false with 'gec12_fig_7_17'. Applies only where the stiff clay's alpha is left out; refused where no such clay lies under soft clay or sand. The zone runs 10 pile widths from the top of the stiff clay however it is split into layers.
ground_elevationfloatoptionalElevation of the ground surface the depths are measured from (m): the top of the layers, where the pile head is taken (the original ground under a fill). Figures only: the calc package's profiles are drawn against elevation; every result stays in depth and no number changes.

endo_downdrag — Endo drag load estimate: assumed neutral plane at a fraction of embedment (CGPR #56 3.2.1).
