tension_crack_water_depthfloatoptionalWater depth in the tension crack (m).
tension_crack_sidestroptionalWhich crest end the tension crack is on: 'entry' (default, low-x / slip-surface entry) or 'exit' (high-x). Put it on whichever side the crest is on; no need to mirror the slope. allowed: entry, exit
tension_crack_modelstroptionalTension-crack mechanism: 'strength' (default) keeps the cracked wedge as zero-shear-strength driving soil; 'truncation' removes it from the sliding mass (mass ends at the vertical crack face, as Slide2/UTEXAS do). Truncation is less conservative. allowed: strength, truncation
reverse_curvaturestroptionalA circle whose centre is below the ground where it comes out would turn back above its centre (Slide2: reverse curvature). 'tension_crack' (default, as Slide2) closes it with a dry vertical crack; 'discard' drops such circles from searches. allowed: tension_crack, discard
pore_pressure_pointsarrayoptionalDiscrete pore-pressure field as [[x, z, u], ...] triples (u in kPa) -- a flow-net / TIN sampling. When given, the base pore pressure at each slice is interpolated from this field (linear on the Delaunay triangulation, nearest-node fallback outside the hull, suction clamped to 0), OVERRIDING the gwt_points piezometric line and per-layer ru. The ponded-water buttress still comes from gwt_points, so set BOTH for a reservoir over a flow-net field.
nailsarrayoptionalSoil nails (per metre of slope run): [{x_head, z_head, length required; inclination deg below horizontal=15, bar_diameter mm=25, drill_hole_diameter mm=150, fy MPa=420, bond_stress kPa=100, spacing_h m=1.5, support_convention}]. Capacity = min(pullout behind slip surface, bar tensile)/spacing_h (FHWA GEC-7).
anchorsarrayoptionalTieback anchors: [{x_head, z_head, length, T_allow kN/m required; inclination=15, support_convention}]. Full T_allow applied when the bond zone crosses the slip surface.
geosyntheticsarrayoptionalHorizontal geosynthetic layers: [{elevation, T_allow kN/m required; x_start, x_end, support_convention optional}]. Every support (nails, anchors, geosynthetics, piles) acts at the base of the slice it crosses (Wright & Duncan 1991). support_convention: 'active' (default; Duncan & Wright Method A / Slide2 Active: the force is not divided by F and reduces the driving side -- give the ALLOWABLE force) or 'passive' (Method B / Slide2 Passive: divided by F with the soil strength -- give the ULTIMATE force; lower FOS for the same force). All methods.
stabilizing_pilesarrayoptionalSingle-row stabilizing/micro piles crossing the slope (Ito & Matsui 1975 or a specified shear): [{x required; spacing m=1.0 (D1); z_head, z_toe optional}]. Set the resistance EITHER by shear_capacity (kN per pile; per-metre force = shear_capacity/spacing) OR ito_matsui=true with diameter (m; D2=spacing-diameter) and optional c/phi/gamma (default: soil layer) giving the Ito-Matsui plastic lateral force integrated from head to slip surface. force_direction 'horizontal' (default) or 'normal'. support_convention 'active' (default) or 'passive' as for geosynthetics. Stabilizing force at the slip crossing.
reinforcement_forcefloatoptionalSingle equivalent horizontal reinforcement force (kN/m). Simpler alternative to nails/anchors.
reinforcement_elevationfloatoptionalElevation of the equivalent reinforcement force (m).
xcfloatoptionalCircle center x (m). Required for circular.
ycfloatoptionalCircle center y (m). Required for circular.
radiusfloatoptionalCircle radius (m). Required for circular.
slip_pointsarrayoptionalPolyline slip surface [[x,y],...] for noncircular. Use instead of xc/yc/radius.
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {'phi': {cov: 0.1}, 'cu:Clay': {mean: 30, std: 5, dist: 'lognormal'}, ...}. Keys are layer parameters (phi, c_prime, cu, gamma, gamma_sat, ru) optionally scoped ':LayerName'; each spec needs cov or std (mean defaults to the layer value); dist is 'normal' (default) or 'lognormal'. Use gamma_sat (not dry gamma) for the unit weight of a submerged slope. A depth-varying undrained-strength law su(z)=a+b*(datum_z-z) is ONE correlated (a,b) variable applied coherently across layers — give an entry with a 'law':'linear_su' key: {'a':{mean,std|cov}, 'b':{mean,std|cov}, 'rho_ab':0..1, 'datum_z': elevation where su=a, 'z_ref':'mid'|'top'|'bottom', 'su_min': floor, 'layers': names|null}. A std-0 component (e.g. fixed intercept) drops out.
methodstroptionalLimit-equilibrium method per realization. allowed: fellenius, bishop, janbu, spencer, morgenstern_price, gle
nintoptionalNumber of realizations.
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility.
research_surfacebooloptionalRe-search the critical surface for every realization (slow; default keeps the surface fixed, standard practice).
time_budget_sfloatoptionalWith research_surface: the time budget of EACH realization's search, in seconds (at most 600), as search_critical_surface. It is per search, not for the run: n realizations may take up to n times it, so keep n small.
n_slicesintoptionalNumber of slices.
correlationsarrayoptionalOptional correlated scalar pairs: [['c_prime','phi',-0.5], ...] (or [{'var1','var2','rho'}]). Each references two SCALAR variable keys from 'variables' (optionally scoped ':LayerName') and a correlation rho in [-1,1]. FOSM adds the Taylor cross-term 2*rho*(dF1/2)*(dF2/2); Monte Carlo draws the pair from a bivariate normal. Omit for independent variables (default). A c'-phi' negative correlation typically lowers the FOS variance.
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance for the iterative methods.

fem2d_footing_capacity — Ultimate bearing capacity of a rigid strip footing by FEM load-control to collapse (plane-strain, the FE analogue of a bearing-capacity calc). Validated vs Prandtl Nc=5.14. Use element_type='t6' (CST locks and never collapses).

ParameterTypeDescription
BfloatrequiredFooting width (m).
cfloatrequiredCohesion / undrained shear strength (kPa).
phifloatoptionalFriction angle (deg). Default 0 (Prandtl / undrained).
gammafloatoptionalSoil unit weight (kN/m3), applied as a body force ramped with the load. Default 0 = classical weightless mechanism (the validated basis).
EfloatoptionalYoung's modulus (kPa).
nufloatoptionalPoisson's ratio.
psifloatoptionalDilation angle (deg).
surchargefloatoptionalUniform surcharge q beside the footing (kPa) — used to size the load ramp and the reported factors.
q_maxfloatoptionalTop of the load ramp (kPa). Default 1.6x the closed-form estimate c*Nc+surcharge*Nq+0.5*gamma*B*Ngamma. Pass explicitly for a c=phi=0 footing.
n_load_stepsintoptionalLoad increments; collapse-load resolution = q_max/n_load_steps.
nxintoptionalMesh divisions in x.
nyintoptionalMesh divisions in y.
element_typestroptionalSoil element. t6 (recommended): collapse load within ~2% of Prandtl. cst LOCKS on the isochoric bearing mechanism and never collapses — do not use for capacity. allowed: t6, cst
q_appliedfloatoptionalWorking/design pressure (kPa). If given, bearing_FOS = q_ult/q_applied is reported.
domain_depthfloatoptionalFE domain depth below the footing (m). Positive; default auto-sized.
domain_half_widthfloatoptionalFE domain half-width (m). Positive; default auto-sized.
max_iterintoptionalMax Newton-Raphson iterations per load step (raise for a hard-to-converge model).
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance (residual norm).

fem2d_slope_srm — Slope stability FOS via Strength Reduction Method (plane strain FEM).

ParameterTypeDescription
surface_pointsarrayrequiredGround surface as [[x,z],...] array.

depthfloatoptionalDepth below lowest surface (m). Default the larger of 2*H and 10 m.
nxintoptionalMesh divisions in x.
nyintoptionalMesh divisions in y.
x_extendfloatoptionalHorizontal margin (m): a number adds 30 % of it on each side, a [left, right] pair gives each side in metres. Default 0.3 max(0.5*H, depth, 5) each side; over undrained (phi = 0) soil below the toe the level ground is carried to twice that soil's depth each side, with nx raised to keep the element size (Taylor's deep circle; the result's notes say so). Pass 0 when the profile already has margins.
srf_tolfloatoptionalSRF bisection tolerance (0.01 for benchmark-grade runs).
mesh_checkbooloptionalAlso run a mesh 1.5x finer each way and report both FOS (mesh_check), warning when they differ by more than 5 %. About 3x the run time.
gwtfloat|arrayoptionalGroundwater table: float elevation, or [[x,y],...] polyline.
element_typestroptionalSoil element. t6 (quadratic, recommended): collapse loads within a few % of published benchmarks. cst locks (overpredicts FOS) - elastic work only. allowed: t6, cst
srm_fieldstroptionalStrengths reduced by the SRF: both (default), cohesion only, or friction only. allowed: c_phi, c, phi

srf_rangearrayoptional[min, max] SRF search range.

layer_polylinesdictoptional{layer_name: [[x,y],...]} bottom-boundary polylines for non-horizontal layering.
gamma_wfloatoptionalUnit weight of water (kN/m3).
n_load_stepsintoptionalNumber of load increments applied before the analysis / SRF sweep.
tfloatoptionalOut-of-plane thickness of the plane-strain slice (m). Every result is per metre run and does not depend on it (the soil, walls, struts and joints all scale with it); leave it at 1.
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance (residual norm).

fem2d_srm_mesh_refinement_study — Slope SRM factor of safety on a sequence of meshes (coarse to fine): per-mesh table, change between meshes, Richardson estimate, convergence flag. Runs fem2d_slope_srm once per mesh.

conv_tolfloatoptionalRelative FOS change between the two finest meshes below which the study reads converged.
depthfloatoptionalDepth below lowest surface (m); held for every mesh. Default as fem2d_slope_srm.
x_extendfloatoptionalHorizontal margin (m); held for every mesh. Default as fem2d_slope_srm.

srf_tolfloatoptionalSRF bisection tolerance for every mesh.

fem2d_local_fos — Local (pointwise) factor-of-safety map for a slope: runs the SRM then evaluates local_FOS = Mohr-Coulomb available shear / mobilized shear at each element using the ORIGINAL strengths. At the critical SRF the minimum local FOS ~ the global SRM FOS and the low-FOS band is the failure mass. Returns summary stats (the full field is for plotting).

ParameterTypeDescription
surface_pointsarrayrequiredGround surface as [[x,z],...] array.
soil_layersarrayrequiredArray of dicts with 'name','bottom_elevation','E','nu','c','phi','psi','gamma' (same as fem2d_slope_srm).

srf_tolfloatoptionalSRF bisection tolerance.
element_typestroptionalSoil element. t6 recommended (cst locks). allowed: t6, cst
srm_fieldstroptionalStrengths reduced by the SRF. allowed: c_phi, c, phi
local_fos_capfloatoptionalUpper cap on local FOS where the mobilized shear is ~0 (deep isotropic stress).

gamma_wfloatoptionalUnit weight of water (kN/m3).

max_iterintoptionalMax Newton-Raphson iterations per load step (raise for a hard-to-converge model).
n_gpintoptionalGauss points per T6 element (3 or 6). allowed: 3, 6
n_load_stepsintoptionalNumber of load increments applied before the analysis / SRF sweep.
srf_rangearrayoptional[min, max] strength-reduction-factor search bracket (default (0.5, 3.0)).
tfloatoptionalOut-of-plane thickness of the plane-strain slice (m). Every result is per metre run and does not depend on it (the soil, walls, struts and joints all scale with it); leave it at 1.

fem2d_excavation — Staged excavation in front of an embedded wall (plane strain FEM): in-situ K0 stresses, then lifts with struts installed as the excavation reaches them; half of a symmetric excavation.

ParameterTypeDescription
widthfloatrequiredFull excavation width (m); the model is half of a symmetric excavation, its right boundary the centre line. For a one-sided cut give at least twice the passive zone in front of the wall.
depthfloatrequiredFinal excavation depth (m).
wall_depthfloatrequiredWall tip depth below the ground (m); must exceed depth.
soil_layersarrayrequiredArray of soil property dicts (E, nu, c, phi, psi, gamma = total unit weight, bottom_elevation; optional K0, else Jaky 1 - sin phi'; optional k = hydraulic conductivity m/s for the seepage of a dewatered excavation, every layer or none: a small k below the tip models a wall cut off into an impervious layer).
wall_EIfloatrequiredWall flexural stiffness (kN*m2/m).
wall_EAfloatrequiredWall axial stiffness (kN/m).
strutsarrayoptionalArray of {depth (m, above the final excavation level), stiffness (kN/m per m)}; each installed stress-free once the excavation reaches its level; no preload.
liftsarrayoptionalExcavation depths (m) at the end of each lift; default one lift to each strut level, then to depth.
wall_contactstroptional'smooth' (default): no wall friction (Rankine). 'bonded': the wall shares the soil's nodes and hangs the retained soil (thrust below active). 'interface': wall friction delta between 0 and phi' (Mohr-Coulomb joints between wall and soil); give interface_delta or interface_ratio. allowed: smooth, bonded, interface
interface_deltafloatoptionalFor wall_contact='interface': the wall friction angle delta (deg, 0-45), the same on every layer. UFC 3-220-20 (2025) Table 4-1, p. 184: steel sheet piles against clean sand 17, clean gravel 22, silty sand 14; formed concrete against clean sand 17-22. Give this or interface_ratio.
interface_ratiofloatoptionalFor wall_contact='interface', in place of interface_delta: delta/phi' (0-1) of the layer at each joint.
interface_adhesionfloatoptionalFor wall_contact='interface': adhesion c_a (kPa) on the wall (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 gives it for clayey soils by undrained strength). Default 0 (friction only).
gwtfloat|arrayoptionalGroundwater table elevation (m, the ground is 0, negative below it): the in-situ table, held outside the excavation. What happens inside where it is above the excavation level is excavation_water.
excavation_waterstroptionalWater inside the excavation where the table is above the excavation level. 'dewatered' (default, the construction case: UFC 3-220-20 p. 97, groundwater control below the table; Caltrans T&S Example 7-2): lowered to the excavation level at each lift, steady seepage under the wall's tip, the wall carries the net water pressure (GEC 4 sec. 5.2.9). 'full': kept full of water to the table (dug in the wet; the water on the two faces balances). 'level': lowered to water_level_inside. allowed: dewatered, full, level
water_level_insidefloatoptionalFor excavation_water='level': depth (m below the ground) of the water inside the excavation, between the table and the excavation depth.
n_stepsintoptionalLoad steps in each stage.
max_iterintoptionalIteration ceiling per load step.
layer_polylinesdictoptional{layer_name: [[x,y],...]} bottom-boundary polylines for non-horizontal layering.
gamma_wfloatoptionalUnit weight of water (kN/m3).
nxintoptionalMesh divisions in x (horizontal).
nyintoptionalMesh divisions in y (vertical).
tfloatoptionalOut-of-plane thickness of the plane-strain slice (m). Every result is per metre run and does not depend on it (the soil, walls, struts and joints all scale with it); leave it at 1.
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance (residual norm).

fem2d_seepage — Steady-state seepage analysis (Laplace equation, CST elements).

ParameterTypeDescription
nodesarrayrequiredNode coordinates [[x,y],...].
elementsarrayrequiredCST connectivity [[n1,n2,n3],...].
kfloat|arrayrequiredHydraulic conductivity (m/s). Scalar or per-element.
head_bcsarrayrequiredDirichlet BCs [[node_id, head_value],...].
gamma_wfloatoptionalUnit weight of water (kN/m3).
tfloatoptionalOut-of-plane thickness of the plane-strain slice (m). The heads and pore pressures do not depend on it; total_flow_m3_per_s_per_m sums |v| x element area x t, so it grows with t. Leave it at 1.

fem2d_consolidation — Coupled Biot consolidation analysis (settlement + pore pressure dissipation).

ParameterTypeDescription
widthfloatrequiredDomain width (m).
depthfloatrequiredDomain depth (m).
soil_layersarrayrequiredSoil property dicts, each with 'E' (kPa), 'nu', 'gamma' (kN/m3) AND 'bottom_elevation' (m; 'top_elevation' optional, defaults to the domain top / the layer above). Add 'fill': true to a layer PLACED during construction: its self-weight then moves from the initial stage into the load stage (monolithic: applied undrained with the load, so it consolidates). Fill layers must be the top layers; they may be placed under water (gwt above their base): below gwt a fill loads the soil by its buoyant unit weight gamma - gamma_w, the water standing on the soil in place before placement being part of the initial stage.
kfloatrequiredHydraulic conductivity (m/s) for 'staggered'; for 'monolithic' pass the MOBILITY m^2/(kPa.s).
load_qfloatrequiredSurface load (kPa, positive downward).
time_pointsarrayrequiredOUTPUT times since the load is applied (seconds, >= 0). t = 0 (the loading instant) is always reported first; U and settlement come back at each of these times. The monolithic scheme integrates on a finer internal schedule between them, so a sparse list (e.g. [1e3, 1e6, 1e7]) is fine.
gwtfloatoptionalGWT elevation (m).
n_wfloatoptionalFor 'monolithic': the Biot modulus M (kPa) (~2.2e6 for near-incompressible water). Governs the undrained load response p0. Ignored by 'staggered'.
nxintoptionalMesh divisions in x (horizontal).
nyintoptionalMesh divisions in y (vertical).
tfloatoptionalOut-of-plane thickness of the plane-strain slice (m). Every result is per metre run and does not depend on it (the soil, walls, struts and joints all scale with it); leave it at 1.
gamma_wfloatoptionalUnit weight of water (kN/m3).
layer_polylinesarrayoptionalOptional explicit layer-boundary polylines [[[x,z],...],...] for non-horizontal layering.
consolidation_schemestringoptionalBiot solver: 'staggered' (default, sequential split; drained at every step, so U = 1 and NO consolidation transient under the load) or 'monolithic' (coupled u-p, Taylor-Hood T6/T3, reproduces the load-induced undrained response p0 and the Terzaghi transient; use it for U and settlement versus time). For 'monolithic', pass k as the MOBILITY m^2/(kPa.s) and n_w as the Biot modulus M (kPa). allowed: staggered, monolithic
thetafloatoptionalTime-integration parameter for the monolithic scheme (1.0 backward Euler; 0.5 Crank-Nicolson, more accurate). Range [0.5, 1.0].
startup_stepsintoptionalMonolithic scheme with theta < 1: the first startup_steps time steps are each taken as two fully implicit half-steps (Rannacher start-up), so Crank-Nicolson does not ring at the drained boundary. 0 = plain theta-stepping from the first step.
reset_displacements_afterstringoptionalWhich stage the reported settlements are measured from. The analysis has two stages: 0 'initial' (self-weight of the soil in place, drained, with the hydrostatic water table and any ponded water) and 1 'load' (load_q + any 'fill' layers, then consolidation). 'initial' = from the end of the initial stage, i.e. the load stage alone (common FE practice; the DEFAULT when omitted). 'start' = cumulative, self-weight settlement included. Omitting it lets the default apply and the result then carries a 'judgment' record if the choice matters. allowed: initial, start

fem2d_staged — Staged construction analysis (multi-phase, activate/deactivate soil groups and beams); reports each stage's own movement, the cumulative movement and the movement since a reference stage.

ParameterTypeDescription
nodesarrayrequiredNode coordinates [[x,y],...].
elementsarrayrequiredElement connectivity [[n1,n2,n3],...].
material_propsarrayrequiredPer-element material dicts.
gammafloat|arrayrequiredUnit weight. Scalar or per-element.
element_groupsdictrequiredGroup name -> list of element indices.
phasesarrayrequiredArray of phase dicts: name, active_soil_groups, active_beam_ids, surface_loads [[edges, qx, qy]], gwt, n_steps, reset_displacements (true = report this phase's movements from its START, PLAXIS 'reset displacements to zero'; reporting only). Phase 0 is normally the initial (gravity) stage; soil PLACED during construction (fill) is a group first activated in a later phase, so its self-weight movement falls in that phase.
beam_elementsarrayoptionalArray of beam element dicts.
reset_displacements_afterint|stringoptionalThe stage at whose END displacement_since_reference is zeroed: a stage index, a stage name, 'initial' (= stage 0) or 'start' (no reset: cumulative). DEFAULT when omitted (and no phase sets reset_displacements): after stage 0, taken as the initial gravity/K0 stage, so construction movements exclude self-weight (common FE practice); the result then carries a 'judgment' record if the choice matters.
gamma_wfloatoptionalUnit weight of water (kN/m3).
max_iterintoptionalMax Newton-Raphson iterations per load step (raise for a hard-to-converge model).
tfloatoptionalOut-of-plane thickness of the plane-strain slice (m). Every result is per metre run and does not depend on it (the soil, walls, struts and joints all scale with it); leave it at 1.
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance (residual norm).

seismic_earth_pressure — Mononobe-Okabe active/passive seismic earth pressure coefficients.

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredFriction angle (degrees).
khfloatrequiredHorizontal seismic coefficient.
kvfloatoptionalVertical seismic coefficient (positive upward). Enters KAE through the seismic angle psi = atan(kh/(1-kv)) (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-15) and, with gamma and H, the thrust PAE = (gamma H^2/2)(1-kv) KAE (Eq. 4-16).

liquefaction_evaluation — Full liquefaction triggering evaluation (SPT-based, simplified method).

depthsarrayrequiredLayer depths (m).
N160arrayrequiredCorrected SPT blow counts.

10.1.16 liquefaction — Liquefaction (unified tool)

liquefaction_analysis — Unified liquefaction triggering. Auto-routes by input type: CPT (q_c/f_s) -> Boulanger & Idriss 2014 (liquepy, with LPI/LSN/LDI and a depth_profile of FS and post-liquefaction volumetric strain); SPT (N160) -> B&I-2014 by default, or NCEER/Youd-2001 via method='nceer2001' for code-compliance work. For post-liquefaction downdrag on a pile, give this result to downdrag.post_liquefaction_downdrag as liquefaction_result.

ParameterTypeDescription
deptharrayrequiredLayer mid-depths / CPT depths (m).
N160arrayoptionalREQUIRED for SPT input: SPT (N1)60 blow counts per layer (presence => SPT input).
FCarrayoptionalREQUIRED for SPT input: fines content (%) per layer.
gammaarrayoptionalREQUIRED for SPT input: total unit weight (kN/m3) per layer.
gwt_depthfloatrequiredREQUIRED: depth to the water table during the design earthquake (m below the ground surface; alias gwl). No default: it sets the effective stress and which soils can liquefy, and the references take the groundwater level as a site input (GEC 5, p. 12-23).
amax_gfloatrequiredREQUIRED: peak ground acceleration (g) for the design earthquake (alias pga). No default: it comes from the site's seismic hazard.
q_carrayoptionalREQUIRED for CPT input: cone tip resistance (kPa) at each depth, at least 2 readings (presence => CPT input).
f_sarrayoptionalREQUIRED for CPT input: sleeve friction (kPa) at each depth.
u_2arrayoptionalPore pressure behind cone (kPa) (CPT, optional).
m_wfloatoptionalMoment magnitude (alias magnitude).
methodstroptionalbi2014 = Boulanger & Idriss 2014 (DEFAULT, both SPT and CPT). nceer2001 = NCEER / Youd et al. 2001 SPT procedure (SPT input only). allowed: bi2014, nceer2001
input_typestroptionalOptional override if both/neither CPT and SPT keys are present. allowed: CPT, SPT
a_ratiofloatoptionalCone area ratio (CPT).
i_c_limitfloatoptionalI_c limit for liquefiable material (CPT).
cfcfloatoptionalFines content correction factor (CPT).
unit_wt_methodstroptionalUnit weight method (CPT). allowed: robertson2009, void_ratio
gamma_predrillfloatoptionalUnit weight above the pre-drill depth (kN/m3) (CPT).
s_gfloatoptionalSpecific gravity of solids (CPT).
p_afloatoptionalAtmospheric pressure (kPa) (CPT).
c_0floatoptionalB&I-2014 SPT CRR curve parameter: 2.8 = 16th percentile / deterministic, 2.6 = median.
gamma_wfloatoptionalUnit weight of water (kN/m3) (method='nceer2001').

site_response_1d — 1D effective-stress site response analysis (PDMY02/PIMY + Lysmer dashpot).

ParameterTypeDescription
layersarrayrequiredSoil layers (required): list of dicts, each with thickness (m), Vs (m/s), density (Mg/m3) and material_type: 'sand' needs phi (degrees; optional K0 (default Jaky 1 - sin phi; it sets only the reference pressure where G = density Vs^2, while the column's own horizontal stress after gravity follows nu), PTAng and the PressureDependMultiYield02 constants contrac1, contrac2, contrac3, dilat1, dilat2, dilat3, liquefac1, liquefac2, default the OpenSees wiki's Dr = 40 % column), 'clay' needs su (kPa, undrained strength in simple shear). Optional for any layer: n_elem (its element count, default n_elem_per_layer; a layer the water table falls inside is meshed in two parts with a node at the water table), nu (Poisson's ratio, default 0.3 sand, 0.495 clay), permeability (hydraulic conductivity k, m/s, default 1e-4 sand, 1e-7 clay), stabilization_alpha (the u-p element's pressure stabilization, default h^2 / (4 (K + 4/3 G)) per element, the element documentation's formula), e_init (void ratio, default 0.77 sand, 0.85 clay), n_surf (yield surfaces, default 20; not with a fitted curve), and curve, the modulus-reduction curve the material's backbone follows to the layer's strength: 'opensees' (default, the material's own hyperbolic backbone, much stiffer than laboratory curves in sand), 'darendeli' (Darendeli 2001; optional plas_index 0, ocr 1, freq_hz 1, n_cycles 10), 'menq' (Menq 2003; needs uniformity_coeff Cu and diam_mean D50 in mm) or 'user' (needs G_Gmax_curve {strain_pct: [...], G_Gmax: [...]}; optional damping_curve {strain_pct: [...], damping_pct: [...]}, reported, not imposed).
motionstroptionalBuilt-in motion name (e.g. 'synthetic_pulse'), taken as a rock outcrop motion. Give motion (a built-in name) OR accel_history + dt: one of the two is required.
accel_historyarrayoptionalCustom acceleration time history (g). Give motion (a built-in name) OR accel_history + dt: one of the two is required.
dtfloatoptionalTime step for custom motion (s).
target_pga_gfloatoptionalScale the input motion linearly so its PGA equals this value (g) before the analysis (the built-in motions have fixed PGAs: synthetic_pulse 0.30 g, synthetic_long 0.15 g). Applied before scale_factor; give one or the other.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater table depth (m).
bedrock_VsfloatoptionalBedrock shear wave velocity (m/s).
bedrock_densityfloatoptionalBedrock mass density (Mg/m3).
dampingfloatoptionalTarget Rayleigh damping ratio.
scale_factorfloatoptionalScale factor for input acceleration.
n_elem_per_layerintoptionalElements per soil layer (a layer's own n_elem overrides it).
rayleigh_freqs_hzarrayoptionalThe two frequencies [f1, f2] (Hz) at which the Rayleigh damping equals damping.
pga_lowpass_hzfloatoptionalCorner (Hz) of the low-pass (fourth-order Butterworth, run forward and backward) behind pga_surface_lowpass_g and pga_input_lowpass_g, and of the test of whether motion above it sets the raw PGA; the tool's choice, no reference prints one. pga_surface_g is never filtered.
linear_elasticbooloptionalKeep the soil linear elastic through the shaking (Gmax = rho*Vs^2, Rayleigh damping only): a check of the column, not a design analysis.

RotD100 of a component paired with zeros is that component's response_spectrum.

write_diggs — WRITE a DIGGS 2.6 file from boring/pit/sounding logs and lab results you have read (e.g. off a report's logs), given inline or as JSON files a helper saved. Checks the file against the DIGGS schema and reads it back; never hand-write DIGGS XML.

ParameterTypeDescription
investigationsarrayoptionalOne object per boring, pit or sounding, with the values read off its log. A number printed on the log goes in as printed. A depth read off the log's own drawn depth scale (log_grid's samples, layers and rows, or measure) is read from the log just as much as a printed one: write it, and note the reading in a prov {page, method: 'grid', note: e.g. 'sample depths off the depth scale +/-0.01 m'} on the value or once in the investigation's prov list. Never infer a value the log does not give, and never hold back a record whose values you have: leave out only what could not be read, and name each thing left out, and why, in your answer. Keys: investigation_id; kind (boring|test_pit|cpt|dcp|hand_auger|well|other); depth_unit ('m'|'ft'); x, y, coordinate_system; elevation {value, unit} (leave out any the source does not give: it is written as unknown, never 0); total_depth {value, unit}; date_started, date_finished; drilling {method, equipment, hammer_type, hammer_energy_ratio, sampler, contractor, logged_by}; layers [{top {value, unit}, bottom {value, unit}, description, uscs}]; samples [{sample_id (may be empty), top, bottom, kind (spt|ring|shelby|bulk|grab|core|cuttings|other), recovery {value, unit} (a printed length), recovery_percent, rqd_percent, water_content, fines_percent, liquid_limit, plastic_limit, uscs}]; spt [{depth_top, depth_bottom, blows [per increment; a string for refusal, e.g. '50/10cm'], increment {value, unit} (the length each drive is counted over, as the form prints it, e.g. 15 cm; 6 in when left out), n (ONLY if printed; a printed refusal such as '>50', 'R' or '50/5"' may be given as n and is recorded as refusal: true with its text kept), refusal, sample_id}]; water [{depth {value, unit}, when (while_drilling|at_completion|after_hours|not_encountered|unknown), hours}] (not_encountered: leave depth out -- it is never written as a water level); remarks; pages (0-based PDF pages the values were read from; none for a record no page gave, such as a placeholder). Every depth or elevation is {value, unit}. Unknown keys are refused by name.
lab_testsarrayoptionalLab results, one object per test on one specimen: kind (atterberg|gradation|compaction|cbr|moisture_content|density|chemical|specific_gravity|unconfined|unconfined_rock|direct_shear|triaxial|swell_consolidation|permeability|organic_content|summary_table|other), investigation_id, sample_id, depth_top {value, unit}, depth_bottom, standard, pages, and result {kind: the same kind, then: atterberg: ll, pl, pi, non_plastic; gradation: gravel_percent, sand_percent, silt_percent, clay_percent, fines_percent, percent_passing [{percent_passing, size {value, unit}, sieve}]; compaction: max_dry_density {value, unit}, optimum_wc; cbr: cbr_percent, swell_percent, soaked; moisture_content: wc; chemical: pH, sulfate, chloride, resistivity (numbers, {value, unit}, or the printed text e.g. '<10')}. A report's lab SUMMARY TABLE goes in too, as one object of kind summary_table with result {kind: summary_table, rows [{investigation_id, sample_id, depth_top, wc, ll, pl, pi, gravel_percent, sand_percent, fines_percent, max_dry_density, optimum_wc, pH, sulfate, chloride}]}: it is cross-checked against the individual sheets.
investigations_filestr|arrayoptionalThe same objects as investigations, from a JSON file in this conversation's folder (a list of them, or {investigations: [...]}), or a list of such files read in order. Records a helper extracts: brief it to save them with save_file as such a file and to name the file in its reply, then pass the name here -- never retype them. Checked as inline records are, each problem naming its file. Combines with inline investigations; one investigation_id in two inputs is refused, naming both.
lab_tests_filestr|arrayoptionalThe same for lab_tests: a JSON file (or files) of lab_tests objects, or {lab_tests: [...]}.
projectdictoptional{name, number, client, location, coordinate_system, elevation_datum} as printed.
output_pathstroptionalA file name for the .xml, e.g. 'site.diggs.xml'; omitted, it is named after the investigations (e.g. 'B-1_to_B-12.diggs.xml'). In the app it is written into this conversation's folder, whatever directory is given, and attached to the conversation.
document_idstroptionalAn identifier for the source document.

validate_diggs_dictionary — Validate DIGGS propertyClass values against DIGGS dictionary (via pydiggs).

ParameterTypeDescription
file_pathstroptionalPath to DIGGS XML file. Provide file_path or content, not both.
contentstroptionalDIGGS XML as string.

10.1.22 gstools — Geostatistics (kriging, random fields & conditional simulation)

kriging — Kriging (ordinary/simple/universal): ONE smoothed best estimate of a property between points -- the mean surface and its kriging variance. It understates the spread and cannot give the probability of a total over an area (use conditional_simulation).

ParameterTypeDescription
xarrayrequiredX-coordinates of measurement points (m).
yarrayrequiredY-coordinates of measurement points (m).
valuesarrayrequiredMeasured values at each point.
model_typestroptionalGSTools covariance model. allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical
kriging_typestroptionalordinary = unknown constant mean; simple = known mean (the sample mean of these observations); universal = linear drift in x and y. allowed: ordinary, simple, universal
grid_x_minfloatoptionalGrid X minimum (m). Omitted: the data's x range less 10%.
grid_x_maxfloatoptionalGrid X maximum (m). Omitted: the data's x range plus 10%.
grid_y_minfloatoptionalGrid Y minimum (m). Omitted: from the data, as x.
grid_y_maxfloatoptionalGrid Y maximum (m). Omitted: from the data, as x.
n_grid_xintoptionalGrid points in X (1 with min = max for one coordinate).
n_grid_yintoptionalGrid points in Y.
variancefloatoptionalSill variance (value units squared). Omitted: the sample variance of THESE observations. With fit_variogram=true (the default) it is only the starting guess and is overridden by the fit.
len_scalefloatoptionalCorrelation length (m). Omitted: a third of the data extent. With fit_variogram=true it is only the starting guess and is overridden by the fit.
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance (measurement error + variation below the data spacing); with a nugget the surface does not pass exactly through the data. With fit_variogram=true the nugget is fitted too, unless fit_nugget=false.
fit_variogrambooloptionalFit variance, len_scale AND nugget to the empirical variogram, overriding values given for them (the fitted values are returned). Refused with too few lag classes: then set false and give variance and len_scale.
fit_nuggetbooloptionalWith fit_variogram: false holds the nugget at the value given (e.g. from the measurement error or twinned borings) and fits only variance and len_scale. Without fit_variogram nothing is fitted and true is refused.
regionsarrayoptionalPlan regions: [{name, polygon: [[x, y], ...], level}], level one number or a list of levels to sweep (same units as values, e.g. an elevation in m). Totals over the cells whose centre is inside the polygon (concave shapes fine): volume_above = sum(max(z - level, 0) x cell area), area_above = cell area where z > level (the 'below' versions mirror it). Here from the kriging only: the kriged surface's totals, and Gaussian POINTWISE expectations (expected volume, expected area, mean cell probability). These are expectations cell by cell; the probability that a TOTAL exceeds a value needs conditional_simulation.
cell_sizefloatoptionalCell size (m) for the region totals; default the smallest round size giving at most ~3,000 cells.
quantitystroptionalRegion totals above (e.g. rock above an excavation level) or below (e.g. fill to a grade) the level. allowed: above, below
marginfloatoptionalMargin (m) of the region lattice around the regions.
output_prefixstroptionalFile name stem for the files this call writes (<stem>_grid.csv for a grid over 2,500 points, <stem>_regions.csv with regions, <stem>_kriging_map.png); default kriging_<time>.
figuresbooloptionalDraw the kriging map: a plan, to scale, of the kriged mean and the kriging standard deviation as labelled contours, the standard deviation with a colour scale too (PNG + interactive). Set false in a sweep of many calls.
namesarrayoptionalObservation names (e.g. boring IDs), one per point; label the map.
value_namestroptionalWhat the values are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'top of hard rock elevation'); names the map. Give it.
value_unitstroptionalUnit of the values (e.g. 'm').
north_degfloatoptionalNorth on the map, degrees clockwise from up, as the source plan shows it; up when not given.
outlinesarrayoptionalWhat the source plan shows besides the borings, drawn on the map for orientation: the property line, buildings, walls, roads. A list of {name, polygon: [[x, y], ...]} (closed, 3 points or more) or {name, line: [[x, y], ...]} (open, 2 or more), in the same x, y as the observations, with kind 'property_line' (drawn dash-dot) or 'outline' (default). Drawing only: they change no number.
observations_namestroptionalWhat the observation points are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'Borings', 'CPT soundings'): the map legend's name for them. 'Observations' when not given.

variogram — Estimate and fit an empirical variogram from spatial data (sill, range, nugget).

ParameterTypeDescription
xarrayrequiredX-coordinates of measurement points (m).
yarrayrequiredY-coordinates of measurement points (m).
valuesarrayrequiredMeasured values at each point.
model_typestroptionalCovariance model to fit. allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical
n_binsintoptionalNumber of lag classes between 0 and the largest pair separation.
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance. Left out: fitted with the sill and range. A number (0 or more): the nugget is fixed at it and only the sill and range are fitted (0 = no nugget). The nugget used is returned, with nugget_fitted.

random_field — Generate ONE UNconditioned 2D random field (mean + correlated variation). It does NOT honour any data; for realizations that pass through observations use conditional_simulation.

ParameterTypeDescription
model_typestroptionalCovariance model. allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical
variancefloatoptionalField variance.
len_scalefloatoptionalCorrelation length (m).
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance.
meanfloatoptionalMean value.
x_minfloatoptionalX-axis minimum (m).
x_maxfloatoptionalX-axis maximum (m).
y_minfloatoptionalY-axis minimum (m).
y_maxfloatoptionalY-axis maximum (m).
n_xintoptionalGrid points in X.
n_yintoptionalGrid points in Y.
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility.

conditional_simulation — Realizations that honour the data (conditioned random field), each integrated over plan polygons: probabilities of a TOTAL over an area -- volume above/below a level (rock to excavate, fill), area, any encounter -- with percentiles, exceedance, CSV files and figures.

ParameterTypeDescription
xarrayrequiredX-coordinates of the observations (m), at least 3.
yarrayrequiredY-coordinates of the observations (m).
valuesarrayrequiredObserved values, e.g. top-of-rock elevation (m) at each boring.
regionsarrayrequiredPlan regions: [{name, polygon: [[x, y], ...], level}], level one number or a list of levels to sweep (same units as values, e.g. an elevation in m). Totals over the cells whose centre is inside the polygon (concave shapes fine): volume_above = sum(max(z - level, 0) x cell area), area_above = cell area where z > level (the 'below' versions mirror it). Every region and level uses the SAME realizations, so differences between footprints or levels are meaningful.
namesarrayoptionalObservation names (e.g. boring IDs), one per point; label the map and files.
model_typestroptionalGSTools covariance model (Exponential is rougher than Gaussian). allowed: Gaussian, Exponential, Matern, Spherical, Linear, Stable, Rational, Cubic, HyperSpherical
variancefloatoptionalSill variance (value units squared, m2 for elevations). Omitted: the sample variance of these observations, flagged. The percentiles follow it -- state its basis.
len_scalefloatoptionalCorrelation length (m). Omitted: a third of the data extent, flagged. State its basis.
nuggetfloatoptionalNugget variance (error + variation below the data spacing); default 0, or the largest measurement_error. With a nugget the field does not pass exactly through the data.
fit_variogrambooloptionalFit variance, len_scale (and the nugget if not given) to the empirical variogram. Off by default: with a handful of borings a fitted variogram is unstable.
kriging_typestroptionalordinary = unknown constant mean; simple = known mean (the sample mean); universal = linear drift in x and y (variance is then the residual's). allowed: ordinary, simple, universal
measurement_errorfloatoptionalError variance at the observations (GSTools cond_err), one number or one per point; not above the nugget (GSTools counts it in the nugget). The field then need not pass through the data.
anisfloatoptionalAnisotropy ratio (minor / main correlation length).
angle_degfloatoptionalDirection of the main correlation length, degrees counter-clockwise from +x (GSTools angles, in degrees here).
cell_sizefloatoptionalCell size (m); default the smallest round size giving <= ~3,000 cells; over 5,000 cells refused (the message names a size).
marginfloatoptionalMargin (m) of the lattice around the regions (kriged-mean file, map).
quantitystroptionalabove = volume/area of the field above the level (e.g. rock to excavate); below = below it (e.g. fill). allowed: above, below
n_realizationsintoptionalRealizations (max 20,000). The convergence table shows if more are needed.
seedintoptionalRealization i uses seed + i (reproducible).
simulation_methodstroptionalkriging_residual = conditioning by kriging (Journel & Huijbregts 1978): draws what the chosen model implies, including the correlation between cells; seconds. condsrf = GSTools CondSRF (kriged field + unconditional field scaled by the kriging std): right pointwise variance, unconditioned correlation, so totals can spread too much; slower. condsrf reproduces a CondSRF notebook. allowed: kriging_residual, condsrf
boundsarrayoptionalInequality data [{x, y, max} or {x, y, min}, optional name], e.g. a boring that ended above rock: rock surface below its bottom elevation -> max.
bounds_modestroptionalreport = how often each bound is violated; reject = keep only realizations satisfying every bound (rejection sampling, not inequality kriging; at most 10 x n_realizations draws; acceptance rate reported). allowed: report, reject
report_valuesarrayoptionalTotals for the exceedance table P(V > v); default round values per region and level.
figuresbooloptionalDraw the exceedance curve and the probability map (PNG + interactive).
output_prefixstroptionalFile name stem for the CSVs and figures (default conditional_sim_<time>).
value_namestroptionalWhat the values are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'top of hard rock elevation'); names the figures. Give it.
value_unitstroptionalUnit of the values and the levels (e.g. 'm').
north_degfloatoptionalNorth on the map, degrees clockwise from up, as the source plan shows it; up when not given.
outlinesarrayoptionalWhat the source plan shows besides the borings, drawn on the probability map for orientation: the property line, buildings, walls, roads. A list of {name, polygon: [[x, y], ...]} (closed, 3 points or more) or {name, line: [[x, y], ...]} (open, 2 or more), in the same x, y as the observations, with kind 'property_line' (drawn dash-dot) or 'outline' (default). Drawing only: they change no number, and the regions are drawn anyway.
observations_namestroptionalWhat the observation points are, in the logs' words (e.g. 'Borings', 'CPT soundings'): the map legend's name for them. 'Observations' when not given.

10.1.23 reliability — Reliability engine

fosm — FOSM / Taylor-series reliability (Duncan 2000, UFC 3-220-20): central differences at +/-1 sigma -> moments of g, beta (normal+lognormal), pf, and the per-variable variance-contribution table (which variable matters). 2n+1 g-evaluations; supports correlation.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.

pem — Rosenblueth point-estimate method (UFC 3-220-20 Eqs. 7-13/7-14): 2^n evaluations at mu+/-sigma (correlation-adjusted weights), or the 2n+1 'multiplicative' reduced scheme for many variables.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
schemestroptional'full' = 2^n points; 'multiplicative' = Rosenblueth 2n+1 (uncorrelated only). allowed: full, multiplicative

monte_carlo — Monte Carlo simulation: seeded numpy sampling (optional Latin Hypercube), correlation via Cholesky in normal space, empirical pf with 95% CI + convergence trace, histogram, lognormal-fit beta. Its variables are scalars; for a property that varies across a site and must honour borings (e.g. a rock surface under a footprint), use gstools.conditional_simulation.

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
nintoptionalRealizations. Aim n >= 10/pf.
seedintoptionalRNG seed for reproducibility.
samplingstroptional'lhs' = Latin Hypercube (variance reduction). allowed: random, lhs
n_binsintoptionalHistogram bins.

form — Native FORM (Hasofer-Lind / Rackwitz-Fiessler): HL-RF iteration with equivalent-normal transformation of non-normal variables; exact for the linear/lognormal cases. Returns beta, pf, design point x*, and alpha sensitivity vector (alpha^2 = uncertainty share).

ParameterTypeDescription
variablesobjectrequiredRandom variables: {name: {mean, cov or std, dist, lower, upper}}. dist one of ['normal', 'lognormal', 'uniform', 'triangular'] (default normal). lower/upper truncate normal/lognormal or bound uniform/triangular. Example: {'su': {'mean': 50, 'cov': 0.3, 'dist': 'lognormal'}}.
g_expressionstrrequiredPerformance function of the variable names. With convention='fos' write a FACTOR OF SAFETY (failure at g<1), e.g. 'R/S'; with 'margin' a margin (failure at g<0), e.g. 'R - S'. Math functions allowed (sqrt, log, exp, tan, radians, ...).
conventionstroptional'fos': g is a factor of safety (failure g<1, lognormal beta reported). 'margin': g = R-S (failure g<0). allowed: fos, margin
correlationobjectoptionalPairwise correlations {'a,b': rho} or full matrix [[...]] in variable order. Omit for independent variables.
max_iterationsintoptionalHL-RF iteration cap.

cov_guidance — Published COV ranges for soil/rock properties with full provenance: Duncan (2000) Table 1, ISSMGE-TC304 (2021) site-specific statistics (clay/sand/rock), Phoon & Kulhawy (1999) transformation uncertainty (via UFC 3-220-20). Use to pick a defensible cov for the engines.

ParameterTypeDescription
propertystrrequiredProperty key or alias: phi/friction_angle, su, gamma/unit_weight, N/spt, qc/cpt, Cc, w, LL, PL, PI, OCR, K0, sigma_ci/ucs, RQD, GSI, ...
soil_typestroptionalFilter: 'clay', 'sand', 'rock'.
teststroptionalFilter by test, e.g. 'SPT', 'CPT', 'VST'.
categorystroptionalUncertainty component. allowed: inherent, site_specific, total_test, transformation

combined_cov — Combine inherent + measurement + transformation COVs (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 7-5), optionally with Vanmarcke spatial-averaging variance reduction on the inherent part. All COVs as fractions (0.3 = 30%).

ParameterTypeDescription
cov_inherentfloatrequiredInherent (spatial) COV, fraction.
cov_measurementfloatoptionalMeasurement-error COV.
cov_transformationfloatoptionalTransformation-model COV.
variance_reductionfloatoptionalGamma^2 from the variance_reduction method (1 = point property).

variance_reduction — Vanmarcke variance reduction Gamma^2(L/delta) for spatial averaging over a failure surface/pile length. Give delta directly or a soil_type to use published scale-of-fluctuation guidance (Cami et al. 2020 / ISSMGE-TC304 2021).

ParameterTypeDescription
LfloatrequiredAveraging length (m).
deltafloatoptionalScale of fluctuation (m). Omit to look up by soil_type.
soil_typestroptionale.g. 'clay', 'sand', 'silt', 'soft clay' — used when delta is omitted (vertical average).
modelstroptional'exponential' (exact Markov ACF) or 'simple' (delta/L). allowed: exponential, simple

10.1.24 salib — Global sensitivity analysis (SALib)

sobol_analysis — ONE CALL Sobol variance-based sensitivity: samples, evaluates the model (an expression or a calculation-module spec) at every point, returns S1/ST indices only. Use this, not sobol_sample + sobol_analyze.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredVariable names (at least 2); the names the expression or variable_map uses.
boundsarrayrequired[min, max] for each variable, in var_names order (uniform over the range).
expressionstroptionalThe model as a safe arithmetic expression of the variables (the reliability engines' g_expression rules): +, -, *, /, **, %, comparisons, 'a if cond else b', and sqrt/log/exp/sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2/sinh/cosh/tanh/log10/ceil/floor/radians/degrees/abs/min/max/pi; scientific notation (1e-3) is fine. E.g. '(c + 18*z*tan(radians(phi)))/40'. Give this OR model (exactly one).
modeldictoptionalThe model as a calculation-module run per sample point, instead of expression: {agent_name, method, parameters (the fixed inputs), output (the result key to analyse; a dotted path such as 'results.fos' reaches into a nested result), variable_map (optional {variable: parameter}; default: each variable sets the parameter of the same name; a dotted path such as 'layers.0.phi' sets a nested value that already exists in parameters)}. E.g. {'agent_name': 'bearing_capacity', 'method': 'bearing_capacity_analysis', 'parameters': {'width': 2, 'depth': 1, 'unit_weight': 18}, 'output': 'q_ultimate_kPa', 'variable_map': {'phi': 'friction_angle', 'c': 'cohesion'}}. Calculation modules only (axial_pile, bearing_capacity, concrete_props, dm7, downdrag, drilled_shaft, fem2d, ground_improvement, lateral_pile, liquefaction, pavement_design, pile_group, pynite, retaining_walls, section_props, seismic_geotech, settlement, sheet_pile, slope_stability, soe, wave_equation); no file parameters. One trial run at the centre of the bounds checks the spec and prices the design against time_budget_s. Give this OR expression (exactly one).
n_samplesintoptionalBase sample size N (a power of 2). Evaluations = N*(D+2), or N*(2D+2) with calc_second_order.
calc_second_orderbooloptionalAlso compute second-order interaction indices S2 (doubles the evaluations).
seedintoptionalRandom seed.
max_evaluationsintoptionalRefuse a design needing more model evaluations than this.
time_budget_sfloatoptionalmodel only: refuse a design whose projected run time (trial run x evaluations) exceeds this, in seconds (max 600).

morris_analysis — ONE CALL Morris elementary-effects screening: samples, evaluates the model (an expression or a calculation-module spec) at every point, returns mu*/sigma only. Cheaper than Sobol: evaluations = n_trajectories*(D+1).

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredVariable names (at least 2); the names the expression or variable_map uses.
boundsarrayrequired[min, max] for each variable, in var_names order.
expressionstroptionalThe model as a safe arithmetic expression of the variables (the reliability engines' g_expression rules): +, -, *, /, **, %, comparisons, 'a if cond else b', and sqrt/log/exp/sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/atan2/sinh/cosh/tanh/log10/ceil/floor/radians/degrees/abs/min/max/pi; scientific notation (1e-3) is fine. E.g. '(c + 18*z*tan(radians(phi)))/40'. Give this OR model (exactly one).
modeldictoptionalThe model as a calculation-module run per sample point, instead of expression: {agent_name, method, parameters (the fixed inputs), output (the result key to analyse; a dotted path such as 'results.fos' reaches into a nested result), variable_map (optional {variable: parameter}; default: each variable sets the parameter of the same name; a dotted path such as 'layers.0.phi' sets a nested value that already exists in parameters)}. E.g. {'agent_name': 'bearing_capacity', 'method': 'bearing_capacity_analysis', 'parameters': {'width': 2, 'depth': 1, 'unit_weight': 18}, 'output': 'q_ultimate_kPa', 'variable_map': {'phi': 'friction_angle', 'c': 'cohesion'}}. Calculation modules only (axial_pile, bearing_capacity, concrete_props, dm7, downdrag, drilled_shaft, fem2d, ground_improvement, lateral_pile, liquefaction, pavement_design, pile_group, pynite, retaining_walls, section_props, seismic_geotech, settlement, sheet_pile, slope_stability, soe, wave_equation); no file parameters. One trial run at the centre of the bounds checks the spec and prices the design against time_budget_s. Give this OR expression (exactly one).
n_trajectoriesintoptionalNumber of Morris trajectories.
num_levelsintoptionalNumber of grid levels.
seedintoptionalRandom seed.
max_evaluationsintoptionalRefuse a design needing more model evaluations than this.
time_budget_sfloatoptionalmodel only: refuse a design whose projected run time (trial run x evaluations) exceeds this, in seconds (max 600).

sobol_sample — Generate Sobol quasi-random sample matrix for variance-based sensitivity analysis (two-step: YOU evaluate the model on every row, then sobol_analyze). Prefer sobol_analysis, which does it in one call.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names (at least 2).
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
n_samplesintoptionalBase number of Sobol samples. Total rows = N*(2D+2) for second-order.
calc_second_orderbooloptionalInclude second-order interaction indices.
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility.

sobol_analyze — Compute Sobol first-order and total-order sensitivity indices from model output.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names.
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
YarrayrequiredModel output array, one value per sample point from sobol_sample().
n_samplesintoptionalBase number of samples used in sobol_sample().
calc_second_orderbooloptionalWhether second-order indices were computed.
seedintoptionalRandom seed for resampling.

morris_sample — Generate Morris one-at-a-time (OAT) sample matrix for screening (two-step: YOU evaluate the model on every row, then morris_analyze). Prefer morris_analysis, which does it in one call.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names (at least 2).
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
n_trajectoriesintoptionalNumber of Morris trajectories.
num_levelsintoptionalNumber of grid levels.
seedintoptionalRandom seed for reproducibility.

morris_analyze — Compute Morris elementary effects (mu*, sigma) for parameter screening.

ParameterTypeDescription
var_namesarrayrequiredList of variable names.
boundsarrayrequiredList of [min, max] bounds for each variable.
XarrayrequiredSample matrix from morris_sample().

10.1.32 calc_package — Calc-package reporting

pavement_design_package — Pavement design calc package: AASHTO 1993 flexible (required SN + layer split) or rigid (slab D) with reliability, drainage, and forward checks, UFC 3-250-01 flexible or rigid, or the two methods compared. US customary units. The parameters of the pavement_design tool design_type names.

ParameterTypeDescription
design_typestroptionalWhich procedure to run and report: AASHTO 1993 flexible or rigid (flexible_pavement_design, rigid_pavement_design), UFC 3-250-01 flexible_ufc or rigid_ufc, or compare (compare_pavement_methods). allowed: flexible, rigid, flexible_ufc, rigid_ufc, compare
w18numberoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible or rigid. design_type=flexible: Design-lane 18-kip ESALs over the performance period (use design_traffic_esals to build it). | design_type=rigid: Design-lane 18-kip ESALs.
layersarrayoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible. List of layer dicts, TOP-DOWN; first must be layer_type 'asphalt'. Each: {layer_type: asphalt|granular_base|granular_subbase|cement_treated_base|bituminous_treated_base; modulus_psi (EAC/EBS/ESB -- required on non-surface layers in design mode); ucs_7day_psi (cement-treated); marshall_stability_lb (bituminous-treated); a (direct coefficient override); m (drainage, unbound layers) or drainage_quality + pct_saturation_time ('<1%'|'1-5%'|'5-25%'|'>25%'); thickness_in (set on EVERY layer for a check instead of a design); min_thickness_in}.
reliability_pctnumberoptionalDefault: compare 95 (design_type). design_type=flexible: Reliability R % (50-99.99), Table 4.1 -> ZR. Or give zr. | design_type=rigid: Reliability R % -> ZR (or give zr). | design_type=compare: AASHTO-side reliability.
zrnumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Standard normal deviate directly (overrides reliability_pct). | design_type=rigid: Standard normal deviate directly.
sonumberoptionalDefault: flexible 0.45; rigid 0.35; compare 0.45 (design_type). design_type=flexible: Overall standard deviation (flexible range 0.40-0.50). | design_type=rigid: Overall standard deviation (rigid 0.30-0.40). | design_type=compare: AASHTO overall standard deviation.
mr_psinumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Effective roadbed resilient modulus, psi (or monthly_mr_psi). | design_type=rigid: Roadbed MR, psi -> simplified k = MR/19.4 (no subbase). | design_type=compare: Subgrade Mr (CBR derived by inversion).
monthly_mr_psiarrayoptionalSeasonal roadbed MR list (psi) -> Fig 2.3/2.4 effective MR.
ptnumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Terminal serviceability. | design_type=rigid: Terminal serviceability (also in the strength-term exponent). | design_type=compare: AASHTO terminal serviceability.
ponumberoptionalDefault: flexible 4.2; rigid 4.5 (design_type). Initial serviceability.
delta_psinumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Serviceability loss directly (else po - pt). | design_type=rigid: Serviceability loss directly.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Round-UP increment. | design_type=flexible_ufc: Round layer thicknesses up to this increment (in). | design_type=rigid_ufc: Round the slab up to this increment (in).
enforce_minimumsbooleanoptionalApply Sec 3.1.4 minimum AC/base thicknesses.
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionaldesign_type=flexible: Frost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr. | design_type=flexible_ufc: {uscs_class, finer_than_0_02mm_pct} -> Ch 19 reduced-subgrade-strength frost check; governing section reported.
design_period_yrnumberoptionalAnalysis period (yr); required with swelling/frost -- their dPSI loss is subtracted from the design budget before the solve.
sc_psinumberoptionalRequired when design_type is rigid. PCC modulus of rupture (28-day, third-point), psi.
ec_psinumberoptionalRequired when design_type is rigid. PCC elastic modulus, psi.
jnumberoptionalLoad transfer coefficient J directly (else Table 2.6 midpoint from pavement_type/shoulder_type/load_transfer_devices).
pavement_typestringoptionalFor the Table 2.6 J lookup. allowed: plain_jointed_jrcp, crcp
shoulder_typestringoptionalFor the Table 2.6 J lookup. allowed: asphalt, tied_pcc
load_transfer_devicesbooleanoptionalDowels present.
cdnumberoptionalDrainage coefficient directly (else Table 2.5 midpoint from drainage_quality).
drainage_qualitystringoptionalFor the Table 2.5 Cd lookup. allowed: excellent, good, fair, poor, very_poor
pct_saturation_timestringoptionalMoisture exposure for the Cd lookup. allowed: <1%, 1-5%, 5-25%, >25%
k_pcinumberoptionaldesign_type=rigid: Effective modulus of subgrade reaction directly, pci. Give exactly one of k_pci / mr_psi / composite_k. | design_type=rigid_ufc: Modulus of subgrade reaction (or give subgrade for Table 10-1).
composite_kobjectoptionalSec 3.2 worksheet spec: {seasonal: [{mr_psi, ...}], dsb_in, esb_psi, dsg_ft, ls}; slab_d_in is iterated automatically.
slab_thickness_innumberoptionalGive to CHECK a slab instead of designing.
passes_18kipnumberoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible_ufc or rigid_ufc or compare. design_type=flexible_ufc: Design-life passes of the 18-kip single axle (design lane). NOT interchangeable with AASHTO W18 conceptually — same count, different damage model. | design_type=rigid_ufc: 18-kip single-axle passes. | design_type=compare: 18-kip single-axle passes (= AASHTO W18; LEF 1.0 by definition).
cbr_subgradenumberoptionalRequired when design_type is flexible_ufc. design_type=flexible_ufc: Subgrade design CBR (%). | design_type=compare: Subgrade CBR (Mr derived via FHWA 2555*CBR^0.64). Give this OR mr_psi.
cbr_basenumberoptionaldesign_type=flexible_ufc: Base course design CBR. | design_type=compare: Base CBR (both sides; AASHTO EBS derived unless ebs_psi given).
cbr_subbasenumberoptionalDefault: compare 30 (design_type). design_type=flexible_ufc: Subbase CBR (omit for a 2-layer section). | design_type=compare: Subbase CBR (both sides).
flexural_strength_psinumberoptionalRequired when design_type is rigid_ufc. Concrete flexural strength R (psi).
subgradeobjectoptional{uscs_group, moisture_pct} -> Table 10-1 k.
stabilized_foundationobjectoptional{ef_psi, hs_in} -> Eq 13-1 reduction.
eac_psinumberoptionalAASHTO asphalt modulus.
ebs_psinumberoptionalAASHTO base modulus override.
esb_psinumberoptionalAASHTO subbase modulus override.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header.
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf

render_figures — The FIGURES of any canned *_package — slope section + trial-surface map, p-y curves, settlement/consolidation plots, wall pressure diagrams, pavement charts, FEM mesh/contours — saved as standalone PNGs WITHOUT building the package. For a bespoke html_to_pdf report (SOE, a multi-analysis narrative, anything with no canned template): run the analysis here, paste each figure's html_img_tag into your HTML. Same inputs as the package.

ParameterTypeDescription
packagestrrequiredWhich package's figures: e.g. 'slope_stability_package', 'axial_pile_package', 'settlement_package'. Any *_package method of this module except html_to_pdf. PLUS every input the named package takes, beside it — describe_method('calc_package', '<package>') lists them. The analysis runs exactly as the package would.
output_dirstroptionalFolder for the PNGs (one per figure). Defaults to the working folder.
name_prefixstroptionalFile-name prefix (default: module).

render_tables — The CALCULATION of any canned *_package as an HTML file, WITHOUT building the package, for a report you compose with html_to_pdf: the given and assumed inputs, the values used, the method choices, each step with its equation, the values put in, its result and its reference, the checks, the calculation tables and the reference list, printed as the package prints them. Same inputs as the package. Paste the returned html_include_tag into your report HTML where the calculation goes. The figures come from render_figures.

ParameterTypeDescription
packagestrrequiredWhich package's calculation: e.g. 'bearing_capacity_package', 'retaining_wall_package', 'soe_package'. Any *_package method of this module. PLUS every input the named package takes, beside it, given and assumptions included: describe_method('calc_package', '<package>') lists them. The analysis runs exactly as the package would.
output_pathstroptionalThe HTML file to write. Defaults to <module>_calculation_<time>.html in the working folder.

html_to_pdf — Render self-contained HTML (e.g. a custom report YOU composed) to a paginated PDF on the REAL filesystem. Use when no canned *_package method matches the analysis — compose the report HTML yourself (inline CSS; figures as a real local PNG path or a base64 PNG/JPEG data URI) and pass it here. Figures it cannot embed are a hard ERROR, never a silent blank. A figure that does not fit what is left of a page starts the next page at its full size; one taller than a page is scaled to fit a page. Backgrounds are not drawn: set things off with borders, bold or coloured text. A canned package's calculation (inputs, steps, tables) goes in from render_tables, its figures from render_figures. Pure-Python (PyMuPDF Story engine).

ParameterTypeDescription
htmlstroptionalSelf-contained HTML content to render: the finished page as ONE string value, written out in full with each figure's <img> tag in place (nothing in the call is run, so no code builds or edits it). Inline all CSS. FIGURES: use <img src="fig.png"> (a PNG/JPEG in the working folder, named as the figure tool returned it, or a real local path, is read and embedded for you — this is the easy path, e.g. the html_img_tag returned by profile_figure) or a base64 PNG/JPEG data URI. Inline <svg>, remote image URLs and literal '[image]' placeholders are REJECTED with a list of what to fix. CALCULATIONS: paste render_tables' html_include_tag, <div data-include="file.html"></div>, empty; that file's calculation is put there, with its styles. Provide this or 'html_path'.
html_pathstroptionalPath to an existing HTML file on the REAL filesystem (a save_file or calc-package output path — NOT a sandboxed scratch-filesystem path). Relative <img> paths inside it resolve against the working folder.
output_pathstroptionalPDF output path. Auto-generated if omitted.
allow_unembeddablebooloptionalEscape hatch: render anyway when the HTML references figures that cannot be embedded, instead of erroring. Those figures WILL BE MISSING from the PDF — the response then carries 'unembeddable' and 'renderer_warnings', and you must tell the user which figures are absent. Prefer fixing the figures.

bearing_capacity_package — Run bearing capacity analysis and generate Mathcad-style calc package, with a table (CSV + printed) of the factors N, s, d, i, b, g and the value of each term.

ParameterTypeDescription
widthfloatrequiredFooting width B (m).
lengthfloatoptionalFooting length L (m). Omit for strip.
depthfloatoptionalEmbedment depth Df (m).
shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: strip, square, rectangular, circular
cohesionfloatoptionalSoil cohesion c (kPa).
friction_anglefloatoptionalFriction angle phi (degrees).
unit_weightfloatrequiredSoil unit weight gamma (kN/m3).
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth below surface (m).
layer2_cohesionfloatoptionalSecond layer cohesion (kPa).
layer2_friction_anglefloatoptionalSecond layer phi (degrees).
layer2_unit_weightfloatoptionalSecond layer gamma (kN/m3). Triggers 2-layer analysis.
layer1_thicknessfloatoptionalFirst layer thickness (m) for 2-layer.
layer1_descriptionstroptionalFirst layer label for the result.
layer2_descriptionstroptionalSecond layer label for the result.
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety.
factor_methodstroptionalShape/depth/inclination-factor method. Each takes its own N-gamma unless ngamma_method names another; 'meyerhof' = UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6, with the shape factors 1 under an inclined load (its note A); it has no base-tilt or ground-slope factors (UFC p. 294, Table 5-3), so base_tilt and ground_slope are refused with it. Hansen applies to N-gamma only: use ngamma_method='hansen'. 'terzaghi' = Terzaghi (1943): his Nc, Nq, N-gamma and shape coefficients (1.3cNc; 0.4/0.3 gamma B Ngamma square/circular), no depth or inclination factors; not for inclined loads, slopes or tilted bases (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3). allowed: vesic, meyerhof, terzaghi
ngamma_methodstroptionalNgamma factor method. Default depends on factor_method: the method's own, 'vesic' = 2(Nq+1)tan(phi) (GEC-6 Eq. 5-8), 'meyerhof' = (Nq-1)tan(1.4 phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6), 'kumbhojkar' with factor_method='terzaghi'. 'hansen' = 1.5(Nq-1)tan(phi). Another than the method's own is a mixed method; the result's choices say so. With factor_method='terzaghi' (Terzaghi gave N-gamma only as a chart): 'kumbhojkar' (Kumbhojkar 1993 as tabulated in Das) or 'coduto' (Coduto et al. 2016 approximation, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-2); the result reports the other beside it. allowed: vesic, meyerhof, hansen, kumbhojkar, coduto
failure_modestroptionalfactor_method='terzaghi' only: 'local' applies Terzaghi's local-shear reduction c* = 2/3 c, tan(phi*) = 2/3 tan(phi) (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-4). allowed: general, local
base_tiltfloatoptionalBase tilt angle (degrees). With factor_method 'vesic' only (GEC-6 Table 5-5 factors); 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have none and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-3).
eccentricity_BfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along B (m).
eccentricity_LfloatoptionalLoad eccentricity along L (m).
load_inclinationfloatoptionalLoad inclination from vertical (degrees), 0 to below 90; with factor_method 'meyerhof' below phi, as UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6 takes theta = atan(H/V) < phi' (refused at phi or more).
ground_slopefloatoptionalGround slope angle down from horizontal (degrees), 0 to 45, this tool's own limit: Vesic's g_q = (1 - tan omega)^2 is 0 at 45 deg. With factor_method 'vesic' only; 'meyerhof' and 'terzaghi' have no ground-slope factors and refuse it (UFC 3-220-20 p. 294, Table 5-3). For a footing on or near a slope GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.4 uses N_cq and N_gamma-q (Fig. 5-7).
vertical_loadfloatoptionalRequired with factor_method 'vesic', a load_inclination and a soil with cohesion (or phi = 0): the vertical load V on the footing (kN; kN/m for a strip). Vesic's load inclination factors take H = V tan(load_inclination) over V + A' c cot(phi) (Vesic 1975, EN 1997-1:2004 Annex D.4); with c = 0 that is tan(load_inclination) and V cancels. Without it the call is refused (factor_method 'meyerhof' takes the angle alone, UFC 3-220-20 Table 5-6).
depth_factor_methodstroptionalDepth factors for an embedded footing. 'hansen': Brinch Hansen's (1970) k = Df/B below Df/B = 1, arctan(Df/B) from 1 (UFC 3-220-20 Tables 5-7, 5-8 note B) in the factor_method's d factors (Meyerhof's: k = Df/B up to 1 as UFC Table 5-6 prints it); at phi = 0 Vesic's cohesion term adds Table 5-7's d_c = 0.4 k, as UFC Eq. 5-21 does. 'gec6' (factor_method 'vesic' only): GEC-6 Eq. 5-14 and Table 5-4, d_q on the surcharge term alone, 1.0 below Df/B = 1. 'none': no depth factors, as GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.3.3 advises unless the cover over the footing is competent and sure to stay. The result's choices give what each option gives. allowed: hansen, gec6, none

lateral_pile_package — Run lateral pile analysis and generate LPILE-style calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of y, slope, M, V, p and Es at every node and each layer's p-y curve.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestroptionalPile type. h_pile requires designation; filled_pipe also requires pile_thickness. For a solid pile/drilled shaft, use 'pipe' with no pile_thickness and set pile_E. allowed: pipe, h_pile, filled_pipe
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile Young's modulus (kPa). DEFAULT IS STEEL (200e6) — for concrete drilled shafts set this explicitly, e.g. ~25e6 gross or a reduced value (e.g. 0.3x) for cracked sections.
pile_thicknessfloatoptionalWall thickness (m) for hollow pipe. Omit for a solid section.
moment_of_inertiafloatoptionalMoment of inertia (m4). Overrides the value computed from diameter/thickness.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g. 'HP360x132') — required for pile_type 'h_pile'.
axisstroptionalBending axis — pile_type 'h_pile' only. allowed: strong, weak
fcfloatoptionalConcrete f'c (kPa) — pile_type 'filled_pipe' only.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {top, bottom, model, ...model params}. Required model params: SoftClayMatlock/StiffClayAboveWT {c, gamma, eps50}; StiffClayBelowWT {c, gamma, eps50} with ks for loading='static' or kc for 'cyclic' (kN/m3, the k of the initial line p = (k x) y; Reese, Cox & Koop, COM624P Table 3.2 / GEC 9 Table A-1: ks 135,700 / 271,400 / 542,900 and kc 54,300 / 108,600 / 217,200 for an average c to five diameters of 48-96 / 96-192 / 192-383 kPa); StiffClayBelowWT is Reese et al. (1975), stiff clay with free water: GEC 9 p. 219 keeps it for stiff clay exposed to free water at or near the ground surface, and with the groundwater at depth prefers StiffClayAboveWT (Welch & Reese) even below the water table, gamma then submerged; it does not say how near is near, so which of the two a stiff clay below the water table takes is the engineer's call: state it and why, or ask; SoftClayJeanjean {su, gamma, Gmax} (not checked against a print: neither Jeanjean 2009 nor API RP 2GEO is in the reference library; GEC 9's soft clay criterion is SoftClayMatlock); SandReese/SandAPI {phi, gamma, k} where k (kN/m3) is the k of the initial line p = (k z) y: for SandReese GEC 9 Table A-3 gives it by relative density only, loose / medium / dense 5,429 / 16,287 / 33,931 submerged and 6,786 / 24,430 / 61,076 above the water (20 / 60 / 125 and 25 / 90 / 225 lb/in3); for SandAPI API RP 2A Fig. 6.8.7-1 by phi', e.g. phi' 30 / 35 / 40: 9,260 / 22,260 / 42,510 below the water table and 12,650 / 36,970 / 75,270 above; WeakRock {qu, Er}. SandReese also takes optional construction='reese1974' (default: GEC 9 App. A.4's four-segment curve, linear -> parabola -> straight line -> p_u, A and B from Figs. A-10 and A-11) | 'simplified' (the module's own three-part curve, which no held page prints). StiffClayAboveWT with loading='cyclic' also needs n_cycles, N, the number of times the design lateral load is applied (>= 1; the references give no number to assume; Welch & Reese, COM624P Eq. 3.29, y_c = y_s + y50 C log N, so y50 times 1 + 0.6 log10 N). WeakRock (Reese 1997, FHWA GEC 9 App. A.5) also takes optional RQD (%, default 100: alpha_r = 1/3, the printed lower bound; alpha_r rises linearly to 1.0 at RQD 0), krm (default 0.0005, the softer end of 0.00005-0.0005) and rock_top (depth of the rock surface, m; default the top of the weak-rock layers that hold the layer); its gamma_r is accepted and not used (the criterion does not use the unit weight).
VtfloatoptionalLateral load at pile top (kN).
MtfloatoptionalMoment at pile top (kN-m).
head_conditionstroptionalPile head condition. allowed: free, fixed
QfloatoptionalAxial load at pile top (kN), for P-delta.
stickupfloatoptionalAbove-ground free length (m): head loads/BCs act at the top of the stickup; no soil resistance over it. pile_length stays the EMBEDDED length. Alias: free_length.
n_elementsintoptionalFinite-difference elements along the pile.
tolerancefloatoptionalConvergence tolerance on deflection (m).
max_iterationsintoptionalMost p-y iterations. If they run out, a push of the pile head decides: when the soil cannot resist the load the call fails with 'No solution: the soil cannot resist this load' and the most the pile and soil carry; otherwise the result says converged false with a message (raise max_iterations).
