slope_report_package — One-call slope stability REPORT for a critical-surface SEARCH: input echo, search story (surfaces tried + rejection diagnostics + critical surface/FOS), FOS-by-method table, slice-force + interslice/thrust-line figures, reinforcement summary, a probabilistic annex (FOSM/Monte Carlo) when 'variables' is supplied, and CSV tables (every slice, every trial surface). No fixed circle needed — the search finds the critical surface.

ParameterTypeDescription
surface_pointsarrayrequiredList of [x, z] ground surface coordinates.
soil_layersarrayrequiredList of dicts: name, top_elevation, bottom_elevation, gamma, phi, c_prime (or cu + analysis_mode). Optional 'bottom_boundary_points' ([[x,z],...]) defines a non-horizontal layer base (e.g. a weak seam).
methodstroptionalLimit-equilibrium method the search minimizes and the report highlights. Default 'spencer' (rigorous — populates the interslice-force / line-of-thrust figure). allowed: spencer, morgenstern_price, gle, bishop, janbu, fellenius
surface_typestroptionalTrial-surface family for the search. 'circular' grids circle centres over x_range/y_range and keeps only circles whose ends fall in x_entry_range/x_exit_range; the others draw their surfaces between x_entry_range and x_exit_range. Ranges not given are set from the slope (toe, crest, height, depth to the base). 'weak_layer' biases trials toward a defined weak seam. allowed: circular, entry_exit, noncircular, noncircular_de, pso, weak_layer
x_rangearrayoptional[min, max] circle-center x for the search grid (circular).
y_rangearrayoptional[min, max] circle-center y for the search grid (circular).
nxintoptionalGrid divisions in x (circular search).
nyintoptionalGrid divisions in y (circular search).
x_entry_rangearrayoptional[min, max] x where a trial surface's low-x end may lie (every search, circular included).
x_exit_rangearrayoptional[min, max] x where a trial surface's high-x end may lie (every search, circular included).
n_trialsintoptionalNumber of random trials (noncircular searches).
n_pointsintoptionalVertices per noncircular trial surface.
n_slicesintoptionalNumber of slices.
gwt_pointsarrayoptionalList of [x, z] GWT coordinates.
khfloatoptionalSeismic coefficient (pseudo-static).
seedintoptionalRandom seed for the search / Monte Carlo (reproducibility).
variablesdictoptionalProbabilistic variable spec {param[:layer]: {mean?, cov|std, dist?, source?}}. When given, adds a reliability annex (FOSM by default) on the critical surface.
monte_carlobooloptionalIf True (and 'variables' given), also run a Monte Carlo simulation on the critical surface for the annex.
nintoptionalMonte Carlo realizations (when monte_carlo=True).
research_surfacebooloptionalMonte Carlo: re-search the critical surface each realization (slower) instead of holding it fixed.
time_budget_sfloatoptionalTime budget of EACH critical-surface search in seconds (at most 600), as slope_stability search_critical_surface: the report's search, and with research_surface each Monte Carlo realization's (per search, not for the run). A search cut short reports the lowest surface in what it covered and says so in its warnings.
fosmbooloptionalWith 'variables': run the FOSM annex.
FOS_requiredfloatoptionalRequired factor of safety for the stability check.
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa).
tolfloatoptionalConvergence tolerance for the iterative methods.
f_interslicestroptionalInterslice force function for the rigorous re-analysis of the critical surface.

settlement_package — Run settlement analysis and generate calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of consolidation settlement per layer (e0, Cc, Cr, stresses) and settlement against time.

ParameterTypeDescription
q_appliedfloatrequiredApplied pressure (kPa).
BfloatrequiredFooting width (m).
EsfloatoptionalElastic modulus for immediate settlement (kPa), for the elastic method. Not given: no immediate settlement is computed (0).
consolidation_layersarrayoptionalArray of consolidation layer dicts.
schmertmann_layersarrayoptionalArray of Schmertmann layer dicts.
cvfloatoptionalCoefficient of consolidation (m2/yr). With consolidation_layers, adds the time curve and t50/t90 to the result.
HdrfloatoptionalDrainage path length (m) for the time curve. Default: consolidating thickness / 2 (double drainage) or the whole thickness (single).
immediate_methodstroptionalImmediate settlement method. allowed: elastic, schmertmann
drainagestroptionalDrainage condition for time rate. allowed: single, double
stress_methodstroptionalStress distribution method. allowed: 2:1, boussinesq, westergaard
q_overburdenfloatoptionalOverburden pressure at footing base (kPa).
LfloatoptionalFooting length (m). Not given: L = B for a square or circular footing; a strip is taken as infinitely long (plane strain), which the elastic method refuses unless Iw is given (its Iw grows with L/B without limit); a rectangular footing needs L.
shapestroptionalFooting shape. allowed: square, rectangular, strip, circular
nufloatoptionalPoisson's ratio for immediate settlement.
IwfloatoptionalElastic influence factor for the elastic method. Not given: GEC-6 Table 5-12's shape factor at the centre of a flexible footing (1.12 for a square, by L/B for a rectangle, interpolated in log(L/B); 1.00 for a circle).
gamma_soilfloatoptionalEffective unit weight below the base (kN/m3), for Schmertmann's sigma'_vp at the depth of the peak strain influence factor (NHI-06-089 Fig. 8-21b). Required with immediate_method 'schmertmann'.
C_alphafloatoptionalSecondary compression index. Enables secondary settlement.
e0_secondaryfloatoptionalOne void ratio for the secondary settlement of every consolidation layer. Not given: each layer's own e0, layer by layer.
t_secondaryfloatoptionalTime for secondary settlement (years).
time_years_schmertmannfloatoptionalCreep time for Schmertmann immediate method (years).

axial_pile_package — Run axial pile capacity analysis and generate APILE-style calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of side resistance per layer, load transfer at the ultimate load and capacity against pile length.

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_typestrrequiredPile type. pipe_closed/pipe_open require diameter + wall_thickness; concrete_square/concrete_circular require width (side dimension OR diameter); h_pile requires designation; or a custom section (pile_area, pile_perimeter, pile_width, pile_tip_area) for any but pipe_open, timber always. allowed: pipe_closed, pipe_open, concrete_square, concrete_circular, h_pile, timber
diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter (m) for pipe piles.
wall_thicknessfloatoptionalPipe wall thickness (m).
widthfloatoptionalSide dimension (m) for concrete piles.
designationstroptionalH-pile designation (e.g., 'HP14x117').
pile_lengthfloatrequiredEmbedded pile length from the pile head to the tip (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts (measured from the GROUND SURFACE): {thickness (m), soil_type, unit_weight (kN/m3), friction_angle (deg, for cohesionless), cohesion (kPa, for cohesive), toe_friction_angle (deg, OPTIONAL: separate end-bearing phi if the pile tip is in this layer; defaults to friction_angle), delta_phi_ratio (OPTIONAL Nordlund delta/phi; default from GEC-12 Fig. 7-9 by pile type and displaced volume), beta and Nt (OPTIONAL, beta method: the layer's beta and toe Nt from local experience, GEC-12 Steps 2a/5a), fig_7_18_case (OPTIONAL, a cohesive layer: 'sand_over_stiff_clay', 'soft_clay_over_stiff_clay', 'stiff_clay', 'none'; GEC-12 Fig. 7-18's case, which starts a clay stratum at the layer's top), soil_class (OPTIONAL: 'clay', 'silt', 'sand' or 'gravel', GEC-12 Table 7-9's soil type for beta_coefficients 'table_7_9'; default clay or sand)}. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay').
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth below ground surface (m).
head_depthfloatoptionalDepth of the pile head below the ground surface (m), e.g. the bottom of a footing 1.5 m down. Layers above the head contribute no skin friction; overburden above the head still raises effective stress at the tip. Default 0 = head at the ground surface.
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety for the allowable capacity. Default 2.5: FHWA NHI-06-089 Table 9-5 (indicator piles with wave equation analysis); 2.00 with a static load test, 2.25 with dynamic testing, 2.75 wave equation only, 3.50 Gates formula. GEC-12 itself designs by resistance factors: the result also gives the factored resistance (Table 7-1, Eq. 7-3).
methodstroptionalauto = by soil type: the Nordlund method in cohesionless soil (GEC-12 Sec. 7.2.1.3.1), the alpha method with Tomlinson's adhesion in cohesive soil (Sec. 7.2.1.3.2); beta = the beta (effective stress) method in every layer (Sec. 7.2.1.3.4). allowed: auto, beta
include_upliftbooloptionalAlso report uplift (tension) capacity.
cohesive_phifloatoptionalFALLBACK drained phi' (deg) for cohesive layers under method='beta' (skin AND tip); a per-layer friction_angle on a cohesive layer wins over this global.
uplift_skin_fractionfloatoptionalFraction of the outside side resistance taken in uplift (with include_uplift). Default 1.0: GEC-12 Eq. 7-38 takes the whole shaft resistance and puts the uplift reduction in the resistance factor; 0.7 is the customary share in free-draining soils GEC-12 cites.
pile_weightfloatoptionalPile self-weight (kN) added to uplift capacity (with include_uplift).
toe_stress_limitfloatoptionalLimit on sigma'p at the toe for the Nordlund toe resistance (kPa). Default 143.6 kPa = 3 ksf, GEC-12 Step 8; null for no limit (GEC-12's worked example did not limit it).
inside_friction_ratiofloatoptionalOpen-end pipe, unplugged case: interior over exterior unit side resistance. Default 1/3, the low end of GEC-12's 'typically on the order of 1/3 to 1/2' (Sec. 7.10.7).
open_pipe_toe_limitfloatoptionalOpen-end pipe in cohesionless soil: limiting unit toe resistance (kPa). Default 5027 kPa = 105 ksf (Tomlinson, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7); null for none.
open_pipe_methodstroptionalOpen-end pipe: 'auto' takes Tomlinson's Eq. 7-90 for a pipe under 24 in with the toe in clay and over half its length in clay (GEC-12 p. 407), else the lesser of the plugged and unplugged cases (Eqs. 7-88/7-89, 'paikowsky_whitman'). allowed: auto, paikowsky_whitman, tomlinson
cohesive_Ntfloatoptionalmethod='beta': Nt of a cohesive toe layer. Default 3 (GEC-12: a relatively low Nt in clays unless local correlations suggest higher; Table 7-9 clay 3-30). A layer's own Nt wins.
h_pile_toe_areastroptionalH-pile toe area: 'box' (depth x flange width, GEC-12 Sec. 7.10.7) or 'steel'. GEC-12 Step 9 leaves it to past experience and local load tests. allowed: box, steel
adhesion_curvestroptionalalpha-method: GEC-12 Fig. 7-17 curves. 'auto' = smooth steel for pipe piles, the concrete/timber/corrugated curve for H-piles (GEC-12 p. 247) and concrete or timber piles. allowed: auto, concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel
adhesion_beyond_chartstroptionalalpha method where a clay layer's su is past the end of the chart's curves (Fig. 7-17, or 7-18 where read); GEC-12 p. 247 and alpha-method Step 1 recommend API RP 2A's alpha there for highly overconsolidated clays. 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated': API alpha in a layer whose su / sigma'vo is at or above highly_overconsolidated_su_ratio, Ca held at the curve's end below it; 'chart_end': Ca held at the curve's end in every such layer (GEC-12's worked example, Vol 3 Table D-100); 'api': API alpha in every such layer. Within the curves Ca is read off Fig. 7-17 as drawn (it can exceed su). allowed: api_if_highly_overconsolidated, chart_end, api
highly_overconsolidated_su_ratiofloatoptionalalpha method: the su / sigma'vo at and above which a clay is highly overconsolidated, for adhesion_beyond_chart 'api_if_highly_overconsolidated'. GEC-12 gives no value; it is the engineer's judgment, so a run with a clay layer whose su is past the chart's curves is refused until this (or adhesion_beyond_chart 'chart_end' or 'api') is given. Ask the user, or state the value taken as a judgment call.
displaced_volumefloatoptionalNordlund displaced volume V per unit length (m3/m). Default: the steel area of an H-pile, the gross area of other piles (an open pipe as a closed pipe; its steel area, if it drives unplugged, is below GEC-12 Fig. 7-9).
pile_areafloatoptionalCustom section (m2): the cross-section area, the steel of an H-pile or a closed pipe, the gross area of a concrete or timber pile (it gives the Nordlund displaced volume of an H-pile and of a solid pile). With pile_perimeter and pile_width it replaces diameter, wall_thickness, width or designation; pile_type still picks the GEC-12 curves (not for pipe_open: its section comes from diameter and wall_thickness).
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalCustom section: the perimeter for the side resistance (m); the box perimeter of an H-pile (GEC-12 Steps 6 and p. 247).
pile_tip_areafloatoptionalCustom section: the toe area (m2). Required for h_pile (its box area; h_pile_toe_area 'steel' takes pile_area) and pipe_closed (the gross area); a concrete or timber pile's is its pile_area when not given.
pile_widthfloatoptionalCustom section: the width or diameter b (m), an H-pile's flange width; for D/b and the width notes.
pile_depthfloatoptionalCustom section: the section's depth (m), an H-pile's; reported only.
pile_namestroptionalCustom section: its name, e.g. 'HP16x101'.
adhesion_chartstroptionalalpha-method chart (GEC-12 p. 246): 'fig_7_17' (Tomlinson's Ca, recommended generally), 'fig_7_18' (Tomlinson's alpha for each clay layer's stratigraphy case: sand or sandy gravel over stiff clay, soft clay over stiff clay, stiff clay alone) or 'smaller' (the smaller Ca of the two in each layer, which p. 246 advises the inexperienced user to take). A layer's case is its fig_7_18_case, else from the profile: cohesive layers under a cohesionless layer the sand case, from the ground surface the stiff-clay case; the soft-clay case only where a layer gives it. Eq. 7-90 (open pipe) takes Ca from Fig. 7-17 whatever this is (p. 407). allowed: fig_7_17, fig_7_18, smaller
shrink_swell_depthfloatoptionalDepth (m below the ground surface) of a shrink-swell zone: no shaft resistance in cohesive soil above it (GEC-12 p. 247). Default none.
beta_coefficientsstroptionalmethod='beta': beta and Nt where a layer gives none: GEC-12 Table 7-9 by the layer's soil_class (clay 0.15-0.35, silt 0.25-0.50, sand 0.30-0.90, gravel 0.35-0.80; Steps 2b/5b), a straight line in phi' between Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends). A clay toe takes cohesive_Nt. GEC-12 prints no beta formula from phi' alone; give a layer's beta and Nt for other values (local experience, Steps 2a/5a). allowed: table_7_9
toe_phi_zonestroptionalNordlund toe: the phi near the toe. 'toe_layer' (the toe layer's toe_friction_angle or friction_angle) or 'average_3b' (averaged over the cohesionless soil from the toe to 3b below, GEC-12 Step 7c's zone). allowed: toe_layer, average_3b
project_namestroptionalProject name for header.
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.

drilled_shaft_package — Run drilled shaft capacity analysis and generate SHAFT-style calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of side resistance per layer, load transfer at the ultimate load and capacity against shaft length.

ParameterTypeDescription
diameterfloatrequiredShaft diameter (m).
shaft_lengthfloatrequiredShaft length (m). Alias: length.
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, cu, phi, N60, qu, RQD} dicts. soil_type: cohesive/cohesionless/rock. A cohesionless layer at the shaft tip needs its N60 (end bearing q_b = 57.5*N60 kPa, GEC-10 Eq. 10-14, N60 the mean of the cohesionless layers' N60 between the base and two base diameters below it, by thickness, limited to 50, p. 10-15; a layer there with no N60, or of cohesive soil or rock, is left out); without it the call is refused. Under beta_method 'rational' (the default, GEC-10 2018 Eq. 10-13) each cohesionless layer the shaft passes through needs its N60 (sigma'p by Eq. 10-11 or 10-12) or a direct OCR, else the call is refused; it also takes N1_60 (overburden-corrected SPT; phi' = 27.5+9.2*log10[(N1)60], GEC-10 Example 10-1 and Eq. A-2, where the layer gives no phi; a phi given is used and the result's choices give the correlation's value beside it), sigma_p_correlation ('clean_sand' default: Eq. 10-11 with m = 0.6, clean quartzitic sands; 'silty_sand': m = 0.8, silty sands to sandy silts; 'gravel': Eq. 10-12, sigma'p/pa = 0.15*N60, gravelly soils; GEC-10 p. 10-11) and sigma_v_ref (kPa, pre-scour effective stress for the OCR; default the layer's own sigma'v). A rock layer's RQD (default 100) sets alpha_E of the side resistance under rock_side_method 'caving' (GEC-10 Table 10-3) and the base under rock_base_method 'rqd'; under the default 'gec10' an RQD below 100 within one base diameter below the base needs rock_base_conditions_met, or the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i. A rock layer also takes GSI (Geological Strength Index of the rock mass, 0 to 100, from the core descriptions; GEC-10 p. 10-23 names GSI, not RMR) and m_i (Hoek-Brown constant of the intact rock, by rock type, GEC 5 Table 9-10, as GEC-10 p. 10-24 points to): with the base in that layer they give GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29, taken where the rock is not taken to meet the conditions of Eq. 10-23 and shown beside 2.5*qu where it is (see rock_base_conditions_met); a rock layer within one base diameter below the base that gives them has its own Hoek-Brown base among the result's alternatives. GSI or m_i on any other layer (above the base, further below it, or with the base in soil) is refused: nothing would use them; capacity_vs_depth takes them on any layer a trial base is in.
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
factor_of_safetyfloatoptionalFactor of safety.
beta_methodstroptionalCohesionless side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.1, Eqs. 10-5 to 10-13 (pp. 10-10 to 10-12): f_SN = beta*sigma'v on each layer's average sigma'v, beta = (K/Ko)*Ko*tan(phi'), Ko = (1-sin phi')*OCR^(sin phi') <= Kp, OCR = sigma'p/sigma'v, sigma'p from the layer's N60 (Eq. 10-11 or 10-12), beta limited to its value at 7.5 ft, no limit on f_SN; needs each cohesionless layer's N60 or OCR. 'depth' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) beta = 1.5-0.135*sqrt(z, ft) = 1.5-0.245*sqrt(z, m), 0.25-1.2, x N60/15 where N60 < 15, f_s <= 4 ksf = 191.5 kPa (FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-41 to 9-43, the limit p. 9-133), which GEC-10 (2018) does not print. allowed: rational, depth
K_over_KofloatoptionalK/Ko in the GEC-10 beta (beta_method 'rational'): 1 = 'a rational first-order approximation', no stress change from construction (GEC-10 p. 10-11); 2/3 or lower 'when these aspects of construction quality are not controlled properly' or soil caving is allowed (p. 10-12). 0 < K_over_Ko <= 1.
top_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the top of the shaft (m), in every layer, when given. Left out: none over the top 1.5 m in cohesive soil, GEC-10's 'top 5 ft' (p. 10-17, printed in Sec. 10.3.5.2 for cohesive soils, 'or to the depth of seasonal moisture change', 'subject to modification based on local experience and judgment of the designer'), and side resistance from the top in cohesionless soil and rock (Secs. 10.3.5.1 and 10.3.5.3 print no such zone; Examples 10-1 and 10-5 take the sand's from the surface, Example 10-4 the socket's over its whole length). Give 1.5 to leave the top 5 ft out of sand and rock too (frost, seasonal moisture, gapping from cyclic lateral load), or the depth of seasonal moisture change. casing_depth, where deeper, takes its place.
bottom_exclusionfloatoptionalSide resistance left out over the bottom of the shaft (m) in cohesive soil. Default 0: GEC-10 (2018) prints no such zone, and Example 10-2 (p. 10-18) takes the clay's side resistance to the base. FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 9-129 (O'Neill & Reese 1999) leaves out the bottom 5 ft (1.524 m), its Fig. 9-49 the bottom one diameter (give the diameter for that).
alpha_methodstroptionalCohesive side resistance. 'rational' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Sec. 10.3.5.2, Eq. 10-18 (p. 10-16): alpha = 0.30+0.17/(su(CIUC)/pa), f_SN = alpha*su(CIUC), su(CIUC) from cu by su_test_type. 'aashto' = O'Neill & Reese (1999) as FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-37a/b print it (p. 9-129): alpha = 0.55 for cu/pa <= 1.5, 0.55-0.1*(cu/pa-1.5) to 2.5, on cu; GEC-10 recommends Eq. 10-18 'as a revision' to it. allowed: rational, aashto
su_test_typestroptionalFor alpha_method 'rational': the lab test each layer's cu came from. 'ciuc' (default) = cu taken as su(CIUC), no transform; 'uc' / 'uu' = transformed to su(CIUC) on the layer's sigma'vo by GEC-10 Eq. 10-16 / 10-17 (Chen & Kulhawy 1993, p. 10-16; Example 10-2 takes a UU strength). The base in clay takes the same su(CIUC) (Example 10-3). allowed: ciuc, uc, uu
clay_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in cohesive soil. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) p. 10-19: q_BN = N*c*su (Eq. 10-19), su the mean of the cohesive soil over 2B below the base, by thickness (p. 10-19; the tip layer at its su(CIUC) as its side resistance took it, each clay layer below on its own cu, transformed alike; cohesionless or rock layers within 2B left out; where the profile ends short of 2B, the mean of what it gives, said in the choices), N*c from Table 10-2 by su (6.5 at 500 psf, 8.0 at 1,000 psf, 9.0 at 2,000 psf or more; held at 6.5 below 500 psf), (2/3)[1 + D/(6B)]*N*c*su where the depth D < 3B (Eq. 10-20), no upper limit. 'oneill_reese' = FHWA NHI-06-089 Eqs. 9-39, 9-40 (p. 9-131): Nc = 6[1 + 0.2 z/D] <= 9, x 0.67 where su < 0.5 ksf, q_t <= 80 ksf, on the tip layer's cu. allowed: gec10, oneill_reese
rock_base_methodstroptionalBase resistance with the tip in rock. 'gec10' (default) = GEC-10 (2018) Eq. 10-23 (p. 10-22): q_BN = 2.5*qu, for rock massive or tightly jointed to one diameter below the base, no cavities beneath, a clean base (Example 10-4 takes it with RQD 37 to 100); for a fractured rock mass the Hoek-Brown base, Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29 (pp. 10-23, 10-24; Turner and Ramey 2010): m_b = m_i*exp((GSI-100)/28), s = exp((GSI-100)/9), a = 1/2+(1/6)(exp(-GSI/15)-exp(-20/3)), A = sigma'vb + qu*(m_b*sigma'vb/qu + s)^a, q_BN = A + qu*(m_b*A/qu + s)^a, q_BN/qu limited to 2.5 (p. 10-24), on the tip rock layer's qu, GSI and m_i and the vertical effective stress at the base; resistance factor 0.50 (p. 10-24, Table 8-4); which of the two by rock_base_conditions_met. 'rqd' = q_b/q_u reduced by the tip rock's RQD below 70 (1.5 at 50, 0.8 at 25, 0.4 at 0), cited to GEC-10's 2010 edition, not in the reference library, and not a method GEC-10 Table 8-4 gives a resistance factor for. allowed: gec10, rqd
rock_base_conditions_metbooloptionalFor rock_base_method 'gec10' with the tip in rock: whether the rock below the base meets the three conditions GEC-10 p. 10-22 sets on q_BN = 2.5*qu (massive or tightly jointed, no compressible seams or joints, to at least one diameter below the base; no solution cavities or voids beneath it; a clean base achieved and verified). The engineer's judgment: Example 10-4 takes 2.5 with RQD 37 to 100 because 'Rock coring and local experience indicate the rock mass below the socket tip is competent'. true = 2.5*qu (Eq. 10-23) as stated. false = GEC-10's base for a fractured rock mass, the Hoek-Brown base (Eqs. 10-24 to 10-29), on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i; refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them. Left out = taken as met, said in the result's choices, where every layer within one base diameter below the base is rock with RQD 100 (the layer default), with the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i beside it where they are given; where a layer there has an RQD below 100 or is soil, the Hoek-Brown base on the tip rock layer's GSI and m_i (2.5*qu bounds it above), and the call is refused, naming them, where that layer does not give them.
large_base_reductionbooloptionalO'Neill & Reese's (1999) reduction of base resistance for a large base: 1.27/B in cohesionless soil for a base wider than 1.27 m, F_r = 2.5/(a*B + 2.5*b) <= 1 in cohesive soil for a base wider than 1.90 m (B the bell's where there is one). Default false: GEC-10 (2018) prints neither (Eqs. 10-14, 10-19, 10-20); true applies it.
pafloatoptionalAtmospheric pressure (kPa) for the rational chains.
rock_side_CfloatoptionalC in the rock side resistance f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) (GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, p. 10-20). Default 1.0, 'recommended for design of "normal" rock sockets' (pp. 10-20, 10-21; Example 10-4): conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls, no caving, no smearing. 0.65 = the value of Eq. 10-22 with alpha_E = 1.0 (rock_side_method 'caving' takes alpha_E from Table 10-3 by RQD). 1.9 for roughened sockets, verified by load tests or local experience (p. 10-22). For rock_side_method 'normal'; refused with 'caving', which takes no C. Needs a rock layer.
rock_side_methodstroptionalRock side resistance. 'normal' (default) = GEC-10 Eq. 10-21, f_s = C*pa*sqrt(qu/pa) with rock_side_C, for a 'normal' socket: conventional equipment, nominally clean sidewalls (pp. 10-20, 10-21). 'caving' = Eq. 10-22 (O'Neill and Reese 1999), f_s = 0.65*alpha_E*pa*sqrt(qu/pa), alpha_E from Table 10-3 (p. 10-21) by each rock layer's RQD and rock_joints (closed joints 1.00, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.45; open or gouge-filled 0.85, 0.55, 0.55, 0.50, 0.45 at RQD 100, 70, 50, 30, 20 %; linear between the rows, held at 0.45 below RQD 20), for highly fractured or weathered rock that cannot be drilled without artificial support (casing, plug-ahead) or where caving is anticipated. Needs a rock layer. allowed: normal, caving
rock_jointsstroptionalFor rock_side_method 'caving': the joint condition of GEC-10 Table 10-3, 'closed' (default) or 'open' (open or gouge-filled joints), from the cores. allowed: closed, open
socket_diameterfloatoptionalRock socket diameter (m). Defaults to shaft diameter. One diameter for every rock layer: GEC-10 sizes a socket by one diameter B (Eq. 10-21, Example 10-4) and gives none per rock layer. The rock side resistance and, with the tip in rock, the base (pi/4*B^2, GEC-10 Example 10-4, p. 10-28) take it.
bell_diameterfloatoptionalBelled base diameter (m).
casing_depthfloatoptionalPermanent casing depth (m, no side resistance).
fractured_rock_thicknessfloatoptionalDecomposed or fractured rock (m) below the top of the first rock layer that is 'not considered part of the socket for design purposes' (GEC-10 p. 8-15): no rock side resistance over it, while the soil above keeps its own (casing_depth takes both). 0 = all rock is socket. Needs a rock layer.
concrete_fcfloatoptionalCompressive strength f'c of the shaft concrete (kPa; 28 MPa = 28000, at least 1000). The rock side resistance takes qu no higher than it: 'For design, the value of qu used in Equation 10-21 should not exceed the compressive strength of the drilled shaft concrete' (GEC-10 p. 10-21; Example 10-4 gives qu 360 ksf and f'c 576 ksf), in Eq. 10-22 alike. Left out, that limit is not checked and the result's choices say so. No structural check of the shaft is made. Needs a rock layer.

project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf

downdrag_package — Run downdrag analysis and generate calc package, with tables (CSV + printed) of axial load, unit skin friction and soil settlement along the pile, and every neutral-plane method side by side (CSV).

ParameterTypeDescription
pile_lengthfloatrequiredPile length (m).
pile_diameterfloatrequiredPile diameter (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of {thickness, soil_type, unit_weight, phi, cu, beta, alpha, skin_friction_method, soil_class, settling, description} dicts. soil_type must be 'cohesionless' or 'cohesive' (NOT 'sand'/'clay'/'settling_fill'). Skin friction: cohesionless = beta x sigma'v (Beta method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-7), beta as given, else from phi' by GEC-12 Table 7-9 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-15, driven piles) for the layer's soil_class ('silt' 0.25-0.50 over 28-34 deg, 'sand' 0.30-0.90 over 32-40 deg, the default, 'gravel' 0.35-0.80 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; soil_class also picks the toe's Nt row (Nt_method); cohesive = alpha x cu (Alpha method, UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-8, the default; alpha as given, else read off alpha_chart: UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-16 and Fig 6-14 by default), or with skin_friction_method 'beta' beta x sigma'v for long-term, drained conditions (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.1; GEC-12 7.2.1.3.4), beta required (GEC-12 Table 7-9: clay 0.15-0.35; cu then only for a toe in the layer). A cohesive layer takes no phi, and beta only with skin_friction_method 'beta'; a cohesionless layer takes no alpha. Mark settling layers with settling=True; a settling layer also needs its compressibility: cohesionless -> E_s (elastic modulus, kPa, > 0) and optional nu_s; cohesive -> Cc and e0 (optional Cr, sigma_p kPa) or C_ec/C_er.
Q_deadfloatoptionalDead load at pile top (kN).
fill_thicknessfloatoptionalFill thickness causing downdrag (m).
fill_unit_weightfloatoptionalFill unit weight (kN/m3).
gw_drawdownfloatoptionalGroundwater drawdown (m).
gwt_depthfloatoptionalGroundwater depth (m).
pile_EfloatoptionalPile elastic modulus (kPa). Default is steel.
pile_perimeterfloatoptionalPile perimeter (m). Computed from diameter if omitted.
pile_areafloatoptionalPile cross-section area (m2). Computed from diameter if omitted.
structural_capacityfloatoptionalPile structural capacity (kN) for the max-load check.
allowable_settlementfloatoptionalAllowable pile settlement (m) for the settlement check.
NtfloatoptionalToe bearing capacity factor: R_toe = Nt x sigma'v(toe) x A_toe in cohesionless soil, Nt x cu x A_toe in cohesive. Give the MOBILIZED value -- the toe resistance actually developed at the pile's settlement -- not the ultimate. Omitted, Nt is the ULTIMATE value: 9 in clay (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.3.3), and in cohesionless soil from the toe layer's phi' by Nt_method (60-120 in dense sand at 34-38 deg by the default); then the load and resistance curves often do not intersect and the neutral plane is where the pile and soil settle equally, the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; see neutral_plane_method). UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.2: check 0 %, 50 % and 100 % toe mobilization.
Nt_methodstringoptionalWhere a cohesionless toe's ultimate Nt comes from when Nt is not given, both UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17 (p. 421; qb = Nq sigma'zD, Eq 6-20): 'fellenius' (default) = its Fellenius (2021) column, the same values as GEC-12 Table 7-9, by the toe layer's soil_class (silt 20-40 over 28-34 deg, sand 30-150 over 32-40 deg, gravel 60-300 over 35-45 deg), a straight line in phi' between GEC-12 Table 7-9's range ends (the module's reading; the table prints only the ends), held at the ends outside the range; 'cheng' = its equation after Cheng (2004), Nq ~= 1.2 (Z/b)^-0.437 exp[6.34 (Z/b)^0.0486 tan phi'], Z the pile length and b pile_diameter, at most 200 unless project-specific information supports more (give Nt then). The result's choices give the other route's value. allowed: fellenius, cheng
pile_unit_weightfloatoptionalPile material unit weight (kN/m3), times pile_area for the pile's own weight; used only when include_pile_weight is true. Default 78.5 = steel, the same material as the pile_E default (concrete is about 24). For an H or pipe pile give pile_area as the steel area (pile_area defaults to the solid circle).
include_pile_weightbooloptionalWhether the load curve carries the pile's own weight. Default false: left out, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 7.3.6.1 (and their worked examples) do. True adds the weight of the pile above the neutral plane to Q_np and the drag force.
n_sublayersintoptionalSublayers per soil layer for the depth discretization.
neutral_plane_methodstringoptionalWhich method gives the reported numbers; every method is evaluated and returned in neutral_plane_comparison whatever is chosen. 'auto' (default) = the UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 procedure: the intersection of the load and resistance curves with the toe at toe_mobilization, or, when they do not intersect, where the pile and soil settle equally with the toe force compatible with the toe penetration (UFC 6-5.8.4.3, Fig 6-19). 'force_equilibrium' (the curves' intersection only; error if they do not intersect); 'settlement_compatibility' (pile and soil settle equally, toe force compatible with the toe penetration); 'bearing_layer_top' (top of the bearing layer, end-bearing pile, UFC 6-7.4 step 5); 'pile_toe' (whole shaft in negative skin friction, upper bound); 'endo' (Endo et al. 1969, CGPR #56 Table 3.1 fraction of the embedment; needs endo_bearing_condition). allowed: auto, force_equilibrium, settlement_compatibility, bearing_layer_top, pile_toe, endo
toe_mobilizationfloatoptionalFraction (0-1) of the nominal toe resistance mobilized where the load and resistance curves intersect. 1.0 = UFC 6-7.4 step 3 full mobilization ('a conservative approach for evaluating the drag force'); 0.5 and 0 = the other UFC 6-5.8.4.2 / GEC-12 7.3.6.1 cases for settlement (all three always reported in the comparison).
endo_bearing_conditionstringoptionalCGPR #56 Table 3.1 condition for Endo et al. (1969). allowed: floating, stiff_flexible, end_bearing
skin_friction_stressstringoptionalEffective stress for Beta-method skin friction (sand, and clay with skin_friction_method 'beta') and the sand toe: 'final' (default; sigma'v0 + fill/drawdown change, as UFC 3-220-20 6-7.4 step 2 requires) or 'initial' (sigma'v0). allowed: final, initial
influence_depth_criterionstringoptionalHow deep below the toe the toe load is counted in the settlement (toe force spread 2V:1H from an equivalent footing as wide as the pile): to where its stress increase falls below 'bearing_stress' (default) = 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3; 2.16 pile widths for a single pile) or 'effective_stress' = 10% of the existing vertical effective stress (FHWA GEC-12 Vol I step 1c: 7.3.5.3 for clay below the toe, 7.3.5.6 for sand, 7.3.5.5 for both; deeper for a loaded toe in soft soil). Either way the fill / drawdown, which does not decay with depth, compresses the settling layers below the toe down to the bottom of the soil profile; give the profile down to the base of the compressible soil. allowed: bearing_stress, effective_stress
influence_depth_warning_percentfloatoptionalThe result warns when the two influence_depth_criterion rules (UFC 3-220-20 6-5.8.4.3 and FHWA GEC-12 step 1c) give pile head settlements or drag forces that differ by more than this percentage of the larger of the two (of allowable_settlement / structural_capacity where given), and whenever a settlement or structural check passes with one rule and fails with the other. The rule used is not changed. Default 25 %: the engineer's call, not a reference's figure; neither reference says how far two settlement estimates may differ before it matters.
alpha_chartstringoptionalWhere a cohesive layer's alpha comes from when the layer leaves it out (a given alpha is kept). 'ufc_fig_6_14' (default; UFC 3-220-20 6-5.4.2, pp. 415-417, as its drag example App. B-5.4 reads it): soft clay (su below 800 psf) alpha 1 by Table 6-16; firm to very stiff clay off Fig 6-14 by su/Pa, curve A at Z of 40b or more, curve B at Z = 10b, linear between, Z from the ground surface to the clay's base or the pile toe and b = pile_diameter. 'gec12_fig_7_17': FHWA GEC-12 7.2.1.3.2 Step 1, Ca off Fig. 7-17 by su, D/b and fig_7_17_curve, as drawn (Ca may exceed su). choices states each clay's alpha and where it came from. Refused (with fig_7_17_curve and alpha_transition_zone) where no cohesive layer along the pile leaves alpha out. allowed: ufc_fig_6_14, gec12_fig_7_17
fig_7_17_curvestringoptionalWith alpha_chart 'gec12_fig_7_17' only, and then required where a clay leaves alpha out: the Fig. 7-17 curves for the pile, 'concrete_timber_corrugated' (concrete, timber or corrugated steel; an H-pile takes the corrugated curve, GEC-12 p. 247) or 'smooth_steel'. allowed: concrete_timber_corrugated, smooth_steel
alpha_transition_zonebooloptionalWhether the top 10 pile widths of a stiff or very stiff clay (su 1500 psf or more) directly under soft clay take UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-9, alpha = 0.28 (su/Pa)^-0.44 with the unit side resistance at least the soft clay's, and under sand alpha 1.0 (pp. 416-417, as App. B-5.4 does). Left out: true with alpha_chart 'ufc_fig_6_14', false with 'gec12_fig_7_17'. Applies only where the stiff clay's alpha is left out; refused where no such clay lies under soft clay or sand. The zone runs 10 pile widths from the top of the stiff clay however it is split into layers.
ground_elevationfloatoptionalElevation of the ground surface the depths are measured from (m): the top of the layers, where the pile head is taken (the original ground under a fill). Figures only: the calc package's profiles are drawn against elevation; every result stays in depth and no number changes.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header.
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf

seismic_package — Run seismic geotechnical analysis and generate calc package.

ParameterTypeDescription
analysis_typestroptionalWhich analysis to run and report: the site_classification, seismic_earth_pressure or liquefaction_evaluation tool. allowed: site_classification, seismic_earth_pressure, liquefaction
vs30floatoptionalTime-averaged shear wave velocity (m/s).
layer_thicknessesarrayoptionalLayer thicknesses for Vs30/N-bar calc (m).
layer_vsarrayoptionalLayer shear wave velocities (m/s).
layer_NarrayoptionalLayer SPT N values for N-bar calc (with layer_thicknesses).

su_layer_thicknessesarrayoptionalCohesive layer thicknesses for su-bar calc (m).
layer_suarrayoptionalLayer undrained strengths (kPa) for su-bar calc.
su_barfloatoptionalAverage undrained strength (kPa) (alternative to vs30).

FCarrayoptionalRequired when analysis_type is liquefaction. Fines content (%).

retaining_wall_package — Run retaining wall analysis and generate calc package.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_typestroptionalThe wall to analyse and report: 'cantilever' (the cantilever_wall tool). An MSE wall has no package; run the mse_wall tool. allowed: cantilever
wall_heightfloatrequiredTOTAL wall height H (m), measured from the UNDERSIDE of the base slab (footing) to the top of the stem: H = base_thickness + stem height. The active thrust acts over H on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. If you know the height retained above the top of the footing, add base_thickness (4.0 m retained on a 0.5 m footing is wall_height 4.5).
gamma_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill unit weight (kN/m3).
phi_backfillfloatrequiredBackfill friction angle (degrees).
base_widthfloatoptionalBase width (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
toe_lengthfloatoptionalToe length (m). Auto-sized if omitted.
stem_thickness_topfloatoptionalStem thickness at top (m).
stem_thickness_basefloatoptionalStem thickness at base (m).
base_thicknessfloatoptionalBase slab thickness (m). Auto-sized if omitted: H/10 (FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a), p. 10-38: H/12 to H/10).
stem_batterstroptionalWhich face of a tapered stem (thicker at its base than at its top) is battered. 'back' (default): the front face vertical, the backfill over the battered back counted as resisting weight. 'front': the back face vertical, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1 Fig. B-2 (p. 598) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-16(a) and Example 10-3 (p. 10-52) draw it. allowed: back, front
embedment_depthfloatoptionalDepth of the underside of the base below the ground in front of the wall, Df (m), 0 to wall_height. Left out: the base thickness, the ground in front at the top of the base. Deeper, the soil over the toe counts as resisting weight (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220: 'Weight includes ... weight of soil above footing'; App. B-1.3, p. 599), at gamma_foundation, and include_passive's passive resistance acts over Df.
has_shear_keybooloptionalInclude a shear key below the base (with key_depth). It acts only with include_passive: the sliding check then takes the passive resistance over the depth of the key only, from the underside of the base (depth embedment_depth below the ground in front) to the bottom of the key (embedment_depth + key_depth), the trapezoid UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29 draws below the toe (p. 224: 'the passive pressure is applied only along the depth of the key and not along the entire burial depth of the wall'; GEC-6 Fig. 5-22 likewise), in place of the passive over the embedment; with the undrained rule it counts cu, as GEC-6 Eq. 5-41 (p. 101) counts Pp in front of the key. GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 (pp. 100-101): keys in granular soils 'are not very efficient in developing passive pressures'; its key method is for stiff, overconsolidated clays and soft rock. UFC: 'it is also prudent to consider some amount of future excavation in front of the wall'.
key_depthfloatoptionalShear key depth below the underside of the base slab (m).
surchargefloatoptionalUniform LIVE-load surcharge on the backfill (kPa), e.g. traffic. Its thrust K*q*H drives every check. Over the heel it is NOT a resisting force in sliding, overturning or the eccentricity check by default (live_load_resists), and it does load the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing). A pavement or slab is not a surcharge here: model it as retained soil up to the ground surface (it then rests on the heel and resists like the backfill). Any other surcharge is transient live load: its thrust counts in every check, but its weight over the heel does not resist sliding or overturning. A permanent load you want carried as a surcharge goes in dead_load_surcharge.
dead_load_surchargefloatoptionalUniform DEAD-load (permanent) surcharge on the backfill (kPa), a permanent load that is not part of the retained soil (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.4.2). Pavements and slabs are normally modelled as retained soil up to the ground surface instead. Its thrust drives every check, added to the live load's. Over the heel it is not a resisting force by default (dead_load_resists=true counts it as resisting weight in sliding and overturning); it loads the base in the bearing pressures (surcharge_in_bearing).
live_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the live-load surcharge over the heel (and its share of a sloped or Coulomb thrust's vertical component) as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5 (p. 10-43), 'the live load surcharge is not considered as a stabilizing force over the heel of the wall when sliding resistance is being checked'; UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.2 (p. 597), 'For overturning and sliding checks, it is assumed that the traffic pressure does not act over the wall heel'. true = the free body with the load over the heel, which none of these references uses for a live load. The result's choices say which was used.
dead_load_resistsbooloptionalCount the dead-load surcharge over the heel as a resisting force in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check. Default false: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3 (p. 10-41), for CIP semi-gravity walls the surcharge loads are 'conservatively neglected within the width of the base slab since they contribute to overturning and sliding resistance'. true = counted as a permanent load: GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-22 (AASHTO), loads that increase sliding resistance are included 'only if those loads are permanent'.
surcharge_in_bearingbooloptionalCount the surcharges over the heel in the bearing pressures (q_toe, q_heel, FOS_bearing). Default true: UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.6 (p. 602), 'it is conservative to include the surcharge over the heel of the wall, if this is possible to occur, in the bearing capacity check'; GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-26. false = the surcharge taken as located behind the heel (NHI-06-089 p. 10-41).
backfill_slopefloatoptionalBackfill slope angle (degrees), rising away from the wall. A backfill descending away from the wall (below 0) is refused.
c_backfillfloatoptionalBackfill cohesion (kPa). The active pressure Ka sigma_v - 2 c sqrt(Ka) is taken as zero where it is negative, the tension zone (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-5 Note A; FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-15); the result's choices give the thrust with c neglected and with NHI's minimum active pressure of 5z kN/m2 beside it.
phi_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil friction angle (deg), FULL value — the sliding check applies delta_b = (2/3)*phi_foundation INTERNALLY. Do NOT pre-reduce (passing 2/3*phi here double-counts the reduction). To set the base friction angle directly, use delta_base instead. Defaults to phi_backfill. phi_foundation = 0 gives an undrained strength (c_foundation = cu): sliding_cohesion then defaults to 'undrained'.
c_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil cohesion (kPa), FULL value, no 2/3 factor. The sliding check counts it by sliding_cohesion: NOT at all with 'drained' (the default unless phi_foundation is 0), as the undrained shear strength cu with 'undrained' (ca = cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1). To set the adhesion directly, use base_adhesion.
sliding_cohesionstroptionalHow the sliding check counts the foundation soil's cohesion, by the rule a reference prints. Default depends on phi_foundation: 'undrained' when phi_foundation is 0 (c_foundation is then cu), else 'drained'. 'drained': R = V tan delta_b, c_foundation NOT counted (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 Eq. 5-38, p. 100: 'Equations 5-38 and 5-39 should not be combined for use at the same time'; EN 1997-1 6.5.3(10): 'Any effective cohesion c' should be neglected'). 'undrained': R = ca B alone, no friction, ca = c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength cu, or base_adhesion (GEC-6 Eq. 5-39: 'ca is typically taken as equal to the undrained shear strength'). 'friction_plus_adhesion': R = V tan delta_b + Ca Be, Ca from UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 (p. 184) at c_foundation taken as the undrained shear strength (up to 191.5 kPa), or base_adhesion; Be = B - 2e, the effective base width (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223, which adds that the minimum FS 'may also need to be increased when base adhesion is included'). The result's choices give the rule used, its basis and each other rule's FOS_sliding on the same wall. allowed: drained, undrained, friction_plus_adhesion
delta_basefloatoptionalBase interface friction angle delta_b (deg), used DIRECTLY in the sliding check with NO 2/3 factor. Overrides the (2/3)*phi_foundation default. delta_b = phi_foundation for concrete cast against the ground (GEC-6 Sec. 5.4, p. 99: tan delta 'will be equal to the tangent of the friction angle (tan phi) for the soil supporting the footing'). The result's choices state the delta_b used, its basis and the other reading. Refused with sliding_cohesion 'undrained', which counts no friction.
base_adhesionfloatoptionalBase adhesion ca (kPa), used DIRECTLY with sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (in place of cu) or 'friction_plus_adhesion' (in place of the UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1 value). Refused with 'drained', which counts no adhesion: give sliding_cohesion with it.
include_passivebooloptionalInclude passive resistance in front of the wall in the sliding check (Rankine's Kp unless passive_theory says otherwise; UFC 3-220-20 p. 219: 'typically ignored', and with it considered FSL >= 2.0, Fig. 4-27, so FOS_sliding_required then defaults to 2.0), acting over the embedment, from the ground in front to the underside of the base (embedment_depth, default the base thickness), or with has_shear_key over the depth of the key only (from embedment_depth to embedment_depth + key_depth below the ground in front, UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29). With the undrained rule it counts the foundation's cu, Kp sigma_v + 2 cu sqrt(Kp) (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-7, p. 178, and p. 181); with the other rules c_foundation is not counted in it (p. 179).
gamma_foundationfloatoptionalFoundation soil unit weight (kN/m3): the passive resistance in front of the wall and the soil over the toe (embedment_depth below the top of the base). Defaults to gamma_backfill.
passive_theorystroptionalWith include_passive, the passive coefficient in front of the wall: 'rankine' (default) = Rankine's Kp, no wall friction; 'log_spiral' (or 'caquot_kerisel', the same) = the log-spiral Kp of log_spiral_source at passive_wall_friction_deg. UFC 3-220-20 (Sec. 4-5.1, Figs. 4-27 and 4-29, pp. 219-224) names no theory for it; choices give the other theory's Kp and FOS_sliding and the FOS with no passive. allowed: rankine, log_spiral, caquot_kerisel
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the printed source of Kp, as earth_pressure_coefficient takes it: 'ufc_3_220_20' (default) = UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), its log-spiral Kp for a vertical face and level ground at any wall friction; 'caquot_kerisel_1948' = the Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 chart, and 'dm7_2_eq_4_12' = UFC Eq. 4-12 by name, both needing passive_wall_friction_deg given; 'dm7_2_fig_4_12' / 'dm7_2_fig_4_13' = UFC's charts, drawn for delta/phi' 0.66 only. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13
passive_wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWith passive_theory 'log_spiral', the wall friction delta in front of the wall (deg), 0 to phi_foundation: the engineer's call (UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184). Left out: delta/phi' = 0.66 (UFC p. 191, 'a common assumption'); refused with 'caquot_kerisel_1948' or 'dm7_2_eq_4_12', which need it given (Caltrans p. 4-29: 'Given delta').
q_allowablefloatoptionalAllowable bearing pressure (kPa) for the bearing check. On soil (bearing_pressure 'uniform', the default) it is compared with q_eq = V/(B - 2e), the uniform pressure over the effective width B' = B - 2e, so give the allowable bearing pressure for B' (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119: 'Bf in Equation 5-14 may be replaced by B'f'); with 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock), with the larger edge pressure. Without it the bearing check is NOT RUN: FOS_bearing and passes_bearing are null and checks_not_run lists 'bearing' (q_toe / q_heel are still reported).
gamma_concretefloatoptionalConcrete unit weight (kN/m3). Default 23.6, 150 pcf, as UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.3 (p. 599) and FHWA NHI-06-089 Example 10-3 (p. 10-53) take it.
FOS_sliding_requiredfloatoptionalRequired sliding FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on include_passive: 1.5 (GEC-6 Eq. 5-40, p. 100; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), 2.0 with the passive resistance counted (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27, p. 220, and Sec. 4-5.1.3, p. 223: 'If passive resistance is included, the minimum FSL should be increased to 2.0'). The result's choices say which was taken.
FOS_overturning_requiredfloatoptionalRequired overturning FOS; the check passes at or above it. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 2.0 on soil, 1.5 on rock (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5, p. 10-44: 'approximately of 2.0 for soils and 1.5 for rocks'; GEC-6 Sec. 7.3, p. 124: 'greater than about 2.0 for permanent dead loads'). UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2 (p. 223) asks FOT >= 1.5 for any wall.
pressure_methodstroptionalEarth pressure theory. The active thrust acts on the vertical plane through the back of the heel. 'rankine' (default): the thrust parallel to the backfill slope. 'coulomb': Coulomb's Ka (UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-10) at the wall friction on that plane, wall_friction_deg, by default the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20 and Example 10-3; delta = 0 behind level backfill). At that default Coulomb's Ka on a vertical plane is Rankine's (sloped) Ka, the same thrust (NHI Example 10-3's 0.35 at phi 30, beta 10 is both), so 'coulomb' changes the result only with wall_friction_deg given. allowed: rankine, coulomb
wall_friction_degfloatoptionalWall friction delta on the vertical plane through the back of the heel (deg), with pressure_method 'coulomb', 0 to phi_backfill. Left out: the backfill slope (FHWA NHI-06-089 p. 10-20: on that plane 'there is soil-to-soil contact ... it is generally conservative to assume that the earth pressure is parallel to the slope of the backfill'). Refused with 'rankine'. The result's choices give the delta used and the other reading's Ka.
interface_gap_possiblebooloptionalWhether water or air can reach the base-clay interface. With sliding_cohesion 'undrained' (an undrained clay under the base) the base resistance is then held to 0.4 V (EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(12)P, Eq. 6.5, p. 65). GEC-6 and UFC 3-220-20 print no such limit. Refused with the other rules. The result's choices give FOS_sliding under the other reading.
founded_on_rockbooloptionalWhether the wall is founded on rock. On rock the eccentricity limit is B/4, the middle half, in place of B/6 (GEC-6 Sec. 6.4.1, p. 119; UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 4-5.1.2, p. 223; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17), FOS_overturning_required defaults to 1.5 and bearing_pressure to 'linear'.
bearing_pressurestroptionalThe bearing pressure compared with q_allowable. Default depends on founded_on_rock: 'uniform' on soil, 'linear' on rock. 'uniform' (the default on soil): q_eq = V / B', B' = B - 2e (GEC-6 Eq. 6-6 and Sec. 6.4.2, p. 119; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17: 'Use uniform stress, qeq, for soils'; UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-27 and Sec. 4-5.1.4, p. 224, for soil that is 'relatively ductile'). 'linear' (the default with founded_on_rock): the larger edge pressure of the trapezoid or triangle, q_toe or q_heel (UFC Sec. 4-5.1.4: 'For more brittle materials, such as rock and sensitive clays'; FHWA NHI-06-089 Fig. 10-17). The result's choices give the other pressure's FOS_bearing. allowed: uniform, linear
key_distance_from_toefloatoptionalDistance from the toe to the front face of the shear key (m), for the wall section figure only: the sliding check takes the passive resistance on the plane below the toe over the key's depth, wherever the key is. Not given: the key is drawn under the stem, an assumption: UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-29 (p. 224, a gravity wall) and GEC-6 Fig. 5-22 (p. 101, a footing) print no key position for a cantilever wall. Set it here.
key_widthfloatoptionalWidth of the shear key (m), for the wall section figure only. Not given: the stem's thickness at its base, an assumption: no printed basis for a cantilever wall's key width.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header.
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf

ground_improvement_package — Run ground improvement analysis and generate calc package.

ParameterTypeDescription
methodstroptionalWhich method to analyse and report: the wick_drains, aggregate_piers, surcharge_preloading ('surcharge') or vibro_compaction ('vibro') tool. allowed: wick_drains, aggregate_piers, surcharge, vibro
spacingfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains or aggregate_piers. method=wick_drains: Center-to-center drain spacing (m). | method=aggregate_piers: Center-to-center spacing (m). Alternatively give area_replacement_ratio (As/A, 0.1-0.35 typical) and spacing is back-calculated.
chfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains. method=wick_drains: Horizontal coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr). | method=surcharge: Horizontal coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr). Give with drain_spacing to include wick drains.
cvfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains or surcharge. Vertical coefficient of consolidation (m2/yr).
HdrfloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains or surcharge. Vertical drainage path (m).
timefloatoptionalRequired when method is wick_drains. Analysis time (years).
dwfloatoptionalmethod=wick_drains: Equivalent drain diameter (m). Default 2.5 in (0.0635 m), GEC-13 p. 2-35: 'Various diameters ranging from 1.5 inch to 5.5 inch have been used, but the most common is to use 2.5 inch.' A band drain's is 2(a + b)/pi (Eq. 2-3). | method=surcharge: Equivalent drain diameter (m). Default 2.5 in (0.0635 m), GEC-13 p. 2-35: 'Various diameters ranging from 1.5 inch to 5.5 inch have been used, but the most common is to use 2.5 inch.' A band drain's is 2(a + b)/pi (Eq. 2-3). With drains.
patternstroptionalmethod=wick_drains: Installation pattern. | method=vibro: Probe pattern. GEC-13 p. 4-77: a square pattern 'requires 5 to 8 percent more points to achieve the same minimum densities in large areas'. allowed: triangular, square
smear_ratiofloatoptionalmethod=wick_drains: Smear zone ratio s = ds/dw. Not given: smear ignored (F_s = 0), GEC-13 p. 2-35, 'The effects of both soil disturbance and well resistance are often ignored for typical projects.' Above 1, F_s = (kh/ks) ln(s) is added to F(n), as UFC 3-220-10 (2026) Eq. 5-25 prints it; GEC-13 prints no F_s formula, only 'a sample disturbance factor Fs ≈ 2 may be considered' in highly plastic, sensitive soils whose ch is accurately determined. | method=surcharge: Smear zone ratio s = ds/dw, with drains. Not given: smear ignored (F_s = 0), GEC-13 p. 2-35, 'The effects of both soil disturbance and well resistance are often ignored for typical projects.' Above 1, F_s = (kh/ks) ln(s) is added to F(n), as UFC 3-220-10 (2026) Eq. 5-25 prints it; GEC-13 prints no F_s formula, only 'a sample disturbance factor Fs ≈ 2 may be considered' in highly plastic, sensitive soils whose ch is accurately determined.
kh_ks_ratiofloatoptionalmethod=wick_drains: Permeability ratio kh/ks, used only with smear_ratio above 1 (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-25). | method=surcharge: Permeability ratio kh/ks, with drains, used only with smear_ratio above 1 (UFC 3-220-10 Eq. 5-25).
n_time_pointsintoptionalPoints in the time-settlement curve.
column_diameterfloatoptionalRequired when method is aggregate_piers. Pier column diameter (m).
area_replacement_ratiofloatoptionalArea replacement ratio As/A (0.1-0.35 typical). Used to compute spacing when spacing is not given.
E_soilfloatoptionalSurrounding soil modulus (kPa). With settlement_method 'stress_ratio', used only for the composite modulus E_comp = E_soil*[1 + as*(n-1)]; the GEC-13 Fig. 5-21 methods need it given, for E_c/E_s.
nfloatoptionalStress concentration ratio sigma_c/sigma_s; sets the improved bearing and, with settlement_method 'stress_ratio', the settlement reduction factor. GEC-13 for stone columns: measured 'between 2.0 and 5.0' (p. 5-31), and 'For preliminary design, a ratio of 2.5 is often conservatively used for stability and bearing resistance calculations' (p. 5-32); for rammed aggregate piers 5 to 10 under flexible embankment loading and 10 under rigid footings (p. 5-43); 'stress concentration ratios range from 4 to 45 for rigid footings' (p. 5-45).
settlement_methodstroptionalHow the settlement over the columns is worked out. 'stress_ratio' (default): SRF = 1/[1 + as*(n-1)] from n. The others give the settlement ratio (settlement without columns / with them; GEC-13 p. 5-36 prints it as 'n', which is not the stress ratio n) by E_c/E_s off GEC-13 Fig. 5-21, and need E_column and E_soil: 'weighted_modulus' (curve 2, settlement ratio = 1 + as*(E_c/E_s - 1), any E_c/E_s); 'balaam_rigid' (curves 5b, 5c: E_c/E_s 5 to 10, A/A_c 1.75 to 9); 'balaam_flexible' (curve 5a: E_c/E_s = 10, A/A_c 1.5 to 8.5). GEC-13 p. 5-37: the FHWA (1983) Equilibrium Method, 'roughly equivalent to the Balaam relationships', 'represents an average or lower bound estimate suitable for preliminary analyses'; the Priebe curve (priebe_improvement_factor) 'the upper bound effectiveness'. allowed: stress_ratio, weighted_modulus, balaam_rigid, balaam_flexible
E_columnfloatoptionalAggregate column modulus E_c (kPa), with E_soil, for the settlement_method 'weighted_modulus', 'balaam_rigid' or 'balaam_flexible' (E_c/E_s, GEC-13 Fig. 5-21). Refused with 'stress_ratio', which takes n instead. Alias: column_modulus.
q_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced bearing capacity (kPa). 0 = not computed.
S_unreinforcedfloatoptionalUnreinforced settlement (mm). 0 = not computed.
S_ultimatefloatoptionalRequired when method is surcharge. Ultimate consolidation settlement under the surcharge (m). Compute first via the settlement module if unknown.
surcharge_kPafloatoptionalRequired when method is surcharge. Applied surcharge pressure (kPa).
target_UfloatoptionalTarget degree of consolidation (percent).
drain_spacingfloatoptionalWick drain spacing (m), if drains are used.
sigma_v0floatoptionalCurrent effective stress at layer center (kPa).
fines_contentfloatoptionalRequired when method is vibro. Percent passing #200 sieve (0-100). GEC-13 p. 4-65: 'proper densification generally cannot be achieved when the granular soil contains more than 12 to 15 percent silt OR more than 2 percent clay'; p. 4-67: fines below 10 percent ideally suited. Above 15 not feasible, 12 to 15 marginal.
initial_N_sptfloatoptionalRequired when method is vibro. Current SPT blow count (blows/ft), read as a density by GEC-13 Table 4-8 (normally consolidated sand). Very dense (N above 50, relative density 85 to 100 percent) is not feasible: p. 4-75, 'It is unlikely, even for heavy loading, that it will be necessary to achieve a relative density above 85 percent.'
target_relative_densityfloatoptionalTarget relative density (%), 55 to 90: the probe spacing is read off GEC-13 Fig. 4-34 (p. 4-77), relative density versus probe spacing for silty sands, the lower bound gradation (p. 4-76); refused outside 55 to 90, where the curve is not printed. GEC-13 p. 4-77: 60 percent for floor slabs, flat bottom tanks, embankments; 70 to 75 percent for column and bridge footings; 80 percent for machinery and mat foundations. Not given: no spacing. Alias: target_Dr.
project_namestroptionalProject name for header.
project_numberstroptionalProject number for header.
engineerstroptionalEngineer name for header.
checkerstroptionalChecker name for header.
companystroptionalCompany name for header.
datestroptionalDate string (auto-filled if empty).
assumptionsdictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user did not give, as {input name: its basis}, e.g. {"unit_weight": "not given; typical of the soil described"}. An assumption that is not an input is its own row: {"drained": "long-term condition"}. The package lists them under Assumed Inputs with the analysis's own defaults, so no assumption reads as given. A misspelt input name is refused with a did-you-mean.
givenlist|dictoptionalThe inputs you pass that the user gave, by the names you pass them under, e.g. ["width", "depth", "friction_angle"], or with the user's own words, {"friction_angle": "phi 32 deg from the boring logs"}. Only these print under Given Inputs. Every other input you pass prints under Assumed Inputs as passed, not stated as given (with its basis when it is in assumptions); left out, no input is the user's. A value you read off, worked out or chose is assumed, not given.
output_pathstroptionalFile path to save output. Auto-generated if omitted.
formatstroptionalOutput format: 'html' (recommended, self-contained with embedded CSS), 'latex' (raw .tex source), or 'pdf' (requires pdflatex installed). HTML is always available; PDF requires a LaTeX compiler on the system. allowed: html, latex, pdf

R_minfloatoptionalMin resistance (kN).

pile_group_package — Run rigid-cap pile group analysis (CPGA stiffness method) and generate calc package; with method_6dof, tables (CSV + printed) of the force and displacement at every pile head.

ParameterTypeDescription
method_6dofbooloptionalFalse: the pile_group_simple tool (vertical load and moments on a rigid cap); True: the pile_group_6dof tool (all six load components; needs the pile stiffnesses). allowed: False, True
n_rowsintoptionalRows for rectangular layout.
n_colsintoptionalmethod_6dof=False: Columns for rectangular layout. | method_6dof=True: Columns.
spacing_xfloatoptionalX spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacing_yfloatoptionalY spacing (m). Or give a single 'spacing' for both directions.
spacingfloatoptionalUniform center-to-center spacing (m), used for both x and y.
pilesarrayoptionalmethod_6dof=False: Explicit pile list [{x, y, batter_x, batter_y, ...}] instead of n_rows/n_cols. | method_6dof=True: Explicit pile list [{x, y, batter_x, batter_y, axial_stiffness, lateral_stiffness, label}] instead of n_rows/n_cols.
VzfloatoptionalDefault: True 0.0 (method_6dof). Required when method_6dof is False. Vertical load (kN).
MxfloatoptionalMoment about x (kN-m).
MyfloatoptionalMoment about y (kN-m).
axial_capacity_compressionfloatoptionalPer-pile compression capacity (kN) for utilization checks (rectangular layout).
axial_capacity_tensionfloatoptionalPer-pile tension capacity (kN) (rectangular layout).
axial_stiffnessfloatoptionalRequired when method_6dof is True. Pile-head axial stiffness ka (kN/m), e.g. from a load test or E*A/L for an end-bearing pile. REQUIRED for every pile: give it here with n_rows/n_cols, or on each piles[] entry.
lateral_stiffnessfloatoptionalPile-head lateral stiffness kl (kN/m), here with n_rows/n_cols or on each piles[] entry. Needed for vertical piles to carry Vx/Vy (0 if omitted).
VxfloatoptionalLateral load x (kN).
VyfloatoptionalLateral load y (kN).
MzfloatoptionalTorsion about z (kN-m).
pile_diameterfloatoptionalPile diameter or width (m). With n_rows, n_cols, spacing and soil_type, the package adds the group efficiency factor eta_g, as the group_efficiency tool reads it (GEC-12 Sec. 7.2.2; UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26). The plan view draws the piles to scale at it.
soil_typestroptionalFor the group efficiency factor eta_g, with pile_diameter and the spacing: the stratum giving most of the resistance, as the group_efficiency tool takes it. Not given: no eta_g, and the package says what it needs. allowed: cohesionless, cohesive
cap_in_contactbooloptionalFor eta_g: whether the pile cap is in firm contact with the ground, as the group_efficiency tool takes it (left out where the row depends on it: not in contact, the lower eta_g, said in the choices).
cufloatoptionalFor eta_g with soil_type 'cohesive': the clay's undrained shear strength (kPa), set against 2 ksf, as the group_efficiency tool takes it.
pile_typestroptionalFor eta_g: the column of UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-26, as the group_efficiency tool takes it (driven piles when not given). allowed: driven, drilled_shaft, cfa, ddp, micropile
north_degfloatoptionalDirection of north on the plan view, degrees clockwise from the cap's +y axis (up on the plan), -360 to 360, as the plan the layout came from shows it. Not given: north is drawn up and the figure says so.
cap_outlinearrayoptionalThe pile cap's outline on the plan view: its corners [[x, y], ...] in the cap's x, y axes (m, the axes the pile coordinates use), at least three, drawn closed. For the figure only. Not given: no cap is drawn and the figure says so.
property_linearrayoptionalThe property line on the plan view: its points [[x, y], ...] in the cap's x, y axes (m), at least two, drawn dash-dot as given (repeat the first point last to close it). For the figure only. Not given: none is drawn and the figure says so.

sheet_pile_package — Run sheet pile wall analysis and generate calc package, with a table (CSV + printed) of pressure, shear and moment along the wall.

ParameterTypeDescription
wall_typestroptionalWhich wall to analyse and report: the cantilever_wall or anchored_wall tool. allowed: cantilever, anchored
excavation_depthfloatrequiredExcavation depth (m).
layersarrayrequiredArray of soil-layer dicts, top down: {thickness (m, required), unit_weight (kN/m3, required; alias gamma), friction_angle (deg, default 30; alias phi), cohesion (kPa, default 0), wall_friction_deg (deg, 0 to friction_angle; alias delta), interface_soil (the soil against the steel, a row of the steel sheet pile wall friction table printed in UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-1, p. 184, EM 1110-2-2504 Table 3-3, p. 3-4, and the USS Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual Table 4, p. 13: 'clean_gravel' 22 deg (clean gravel, gravel-sand mixtures, well-graded rock fill with spalls), 'clean_sand' 17 (clean sand, silty sand-gravel mixture, single size hard rock fill), 'silty_sand' 14 (silty sand, gravel or sand mixed with silt or clay), 'fine_sandy_silt' 11 (fine sandy silt, nonplastic silt); at most friction_angle; not with wall_friction_deg)}. wall_friction_deg or interface_soil is used on both sides by pressure_method 'coulomb' and 'log_spiral'. A layer giving neither takes, with 'log_spiral', the clean_sand row (17 deg, at most its phi') on the passive side when it has no cohesion and no wall friction on the active side or in a layer with cohesion (UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-37 step 1, p. 237: 'Passive pressures for clean coarse grained soils include wall friction (see Table 4-1)'; it ignores wall friction in other soils, so give wall_friction_deg 0 in a silty sand or silt); with 'coulomb' none (UFC 3-220-20 p. 190: passive pressure 'should be calculated using the log spiral method and not the Coulomb method'). The result's choices give each layer's wall friction and its Kp at the other rows and at delta = 0, and where a layer took the clean sand row by default the embedment with none.
surchargefloatoptionalSurface surcharge (kPa).
FOS_passivefloatoptionalFOS applied to passive resistance.
gwt_depth_activefloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Groundwater depth on active (retained) side (m). | wall_type=anchored: Groundwater depth on active side (m).
gwt_depth_passivefloatoptionalwall_type=cantilever: Groundwater depth on passive (excavated) side (m). | wall_type=anchored: Groundwater depth on passive side (m).
pressure_methodstroptionalEarth pressure theory. 'log_spiral' uses Coulomb active + the log-spiral PASSIVE coefficient from log_spiral_source (avoids Coulomb's over-prediction of Kp at high delta/phi). 'coulomb' and 'log_spiral' take each layer's wall friction (layers: wall_friction_deg or interface_soil; what a layer giving neither takes is in the layers description). allowed: rankine, coulomb, log_spiral
log_spiral_sourcestroptionalWith pressure_method 'log_spiral', the printed source of the passive Kp. 'ufc_3_220_20' (default): UFC 3-220-20 (DM 7.2), the source the wall's geometry calls for (pp. 191-193); a sheet pile has a vertical face and the tool takes level ground in front of it, so that is Eq. 4-12 (p. 191), at each layer's wall_friction_deg. 'caquot_kerisel_1948': the Caquot and Kerisel (1948) chart, Kp at delta = phi times the printed reduction factor R(delta/phi), Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual Fig. 4-20 (p. 4-30), the method its Sec. 4-6 uses for passive pressure. 'dm7_2_fig_4_12', 'dm7_2_fig_4_13': UFC 3-220-20 Figs. 4-12 (p. 192, theta = 0 curve) and 4-13 (p. 193, beta = 0 row), Kerisel and Absi (1990), drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66 only, so every layer's wall_friction_deg must be 0.66 x its friction_angle; UFC 3-220-20 p. 260 says Kp for a tied-back wall 'should be obtained from Figure 4-12'. 'dm7_2_eq_4_12': Eq. 4-12 by name. They differ: at phi 30, delta/phi 0.66 the 1948 chart gives 5.4, the UFC charts 5.3 and Eq. 4-12 5.1. UFC 3-220-20 footnote 21 (p. 191): the 1982 DM 7.2 charts 'used delta/phi' = 1 along with reduction ratios', which 'were averages that introduced substantial inaccuracy for some cases'; the 1948 chart takes that form (Kp at delta = phi times R). UFC 3-220-20 Table 4-2 (p. 194) is not used: the log-spiral Kp in its row headed delta/phi' = 0.5, 5.3, 8.0, 12 and 20 at phi' = 30, 35, 40 and 45, are Fig. 4-13's values, drawn for delta/phi' = 0.66 (5.30, 8.00, 12.0, 20), and the Coulomb Kp printed beside them, 6.1, 9.8, 18 and 44, are Coulomb's at delta = 0.66 phi' (at 0.5 it gives 5.0, 7.4, 11.8 and 21.4). Eq. 4-12 at delta/phi' = 0.5 gives 4.46, 6.33, 9.33 and 14.3. The tool reads Fig. 4-13 at the 0.66 it is drawn for and Eq. 4-12 at the wall friction given. The result's choices give each layer's Kp from the source used and from the others. allowed: ufc_3_220_20, caquot_kerisel_1948, dm7_2_eq_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_12, dm7_2_fig_4_13
embedment_increasefloatoptionalMultiplier on the computed embedment (e.g. 1.2 for the traditional 20% rule). Use 1.0 (default) when FOS_passive already provides the safety basis — do not double-count.
anchor_depthfloatoptionalRequired when wall_type is anchored. Anchor depth below surface (m).
