10.1.40 gsa_collapse — gsa_collapse

addition_triggers_existing_building_evaluation — Section 2.1 / Commentary C2.1: a new building addition is always itself designed to these Guidelines' new-construction requirements (per the applicable FSL). The requirement does NOT extend to the EXISTING portion of the building unless the addition is 50% or more of the existing building's gross area AND the existing portion is undergoing a major structural renovation -- in which case the existing portion must also be evaluated under these Guidelines' existing- building provisions (printed p. C4).

ParameterTypeDescription
addition_gross_areafloatrequiredGross floor area of the new addition (ft2 or m2).
existing_gross_areafloatrequiredGross floor area of the existing building (same units).
existing_undergoing_major_renovationfloatrequiredTrue if the existing portion is undergoing a major structural renovation concurrently with the addition (see `B1` definition of "Major Modernization").

counts_as_story — Section 2.3.2: a mechanical penthouse or parking level is NOT counted as a "story" toward the FSL III/IV 4-story applicability threshold (printed p. 5).

ParameterTypeDescription
is_mechanical_penthouse_or_parkingfloatrequiredTrue if the level is an unoccupied mechanical penthouse or a parking level.

fsl_applicability — Section 2.3 and Figure 2.1 (Applicability Flow Chart): determines whether these Guidelines apply to a facility of a given Facility Security Level (FSL), and if so which design procedures are required (printed pp. 4-6).

ParameterTypeDescription
fslfloatrequired'I', 'II', 'III', 'IV', or 'V'.
num_storiesfloatoptionalNumber of stories (per `counts_as_story`), counted from the lowest point of exterior grade to the highest point of elevation. Required to resolve applicability for FSL III/IV; unused for FSL I/II/V.

adjacent_element_removal_trigger — Sections 3.2.9.2.2/3.2.9.2.3 (columns): if another load-bearing column is within a horizontal distance of 30% of the largest dimension of the associated bay from the primary removal location, it must be removed SIMULTANEOUSLY (printed pp. 13-14).

ParameterTypeDescription
distancefloatrequiredDistance from the primary removal location to the other column (ft or m).
reference_dimensionfloatrequiredLargest dimension of the associated bay, same units as distance.

classify_action — Section 3.2.5: classifies a component action as deformation- or force-controlled from its ASCE-41-style force-deformation curve type (Figure 3.7) and its e/g ratio (printed pp. 9-10). Printed with IDENTICAL wording and thresholds to UFC 4-023-03 Section 3-2.5 (see module docstring cross-check note).

ParameterTypeDescription
curve_typefloatrequired1, 2, or 3 (Figure 3.7 force-deformation curve type).
e_over_gfloatrequiredRatio of deformation e to g on the component's curve (Figure 3.7).
is_primaryfloatrequiredTrue for a primary component (Section 3.2.4), False for secondary.

component_capacity_linear — Table 3: component-capacity basis for the Linear Static Procedure (printed p. 12).

ParameterTypeDescription
deformation_controlledfloatrequiredTrue for a deformation-controlled action, False for force- controlled.

component_capacity_nonlinear — Table 2: component-capacity basis for the Nonlinear Static and Nonlinear Dynamic Procedures (printed p. 11).

ParameterTypeDescription
deformation_controlledfloatrequiredTrue for a deformation-controlled action, False for force- controlled.

dcr — Equation 3.2: Demand-Capacity Ratio, used only to determine LSP applicability for an irregular structure (printed p. 20).

ParameterTypeDescription
q_udlimfloatrequiredDeformation-controlled action from a linear model with gravity dead/live loads increased by the Omega_LD load increase factor (Section 3.2.11.1.2).
q_cefloatrequiredExpected strength of the component (Chapters 4-8).

deformation_controlled_capacity_check — Equation 3.6: Linear Static Procedure acceptance check for deformation-controlled actions, all primary and secondary components (printed p. 25).

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredStrength reduction factor from the applicable material code.
mfloatrequiredComponent/element demand modifier (m-factor) from Chapters 4-8.
q_cefloatrequiredExpected strength of the component for the deformation-controlled action.
q_udfloatrequiredDeformation-controlled action from the Linear Static model.

deformation_controlled_capacity_check_nonlinear — Sections 3.2.12.7.1 (NSP) / 3.2.13.6.1 (NDP): for deformation- controlled actions, primary and secondary elements must have an EXPECTED DEFORMATION CAPACITY greater than the maximum calculated deformation demand -- no m-factor or Phi is applied (unlike the LSP's Equation 3.6), since the nonlinear analysis itself already produces an inelastic deformation demand to compare directly against the deformation limit (printed pp. 28, 31).

ParameterTypeDescription
expected_deformation_capacityfloatrequiredPermissible inelastic deformation limit (e.g. plastic rotation angle, radians) per Chapters 4-8.
demandfloatrequiredMaximum calculated deformation demand from the nonlinear model.

deformation_controlled_load_lsp — Equation 3.3: increased gravity load for DEFORMATION-controlled actions, applied to bays immediately adjacent to and at all floors above the removed element (printed p. 21).

ParameterTypeDescription
omega_ldfloatrequiredLoad increase factor for deformation-controlled actions, from `table_4_load_increase_factor`.
dfloatrequiredDead load including facade loads (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
lfloatoptionalLive load including live-load reduction, capped at 50 lb/ft2 (244 -- printed as kN/m2, though dimensionally this is 2.4 kN/m2; see module docstring). Default 0.
sfloatoptionalSnow load (lb/ft2 or kN/m2). Default 0. Use L or S, not both.

disproportionate_collapse_allowance — Section 3.2.10.2 (Existing Buildings only): if any primary or secondary elements exceed the acceptance criteria, the existing building may STILL be considered to satisfy the Alternate Path requirements provided the resulting extent of collapse is not "disproportionate" -- defined as floor framing within a single structural bay on each side, immediately adjacent to and at the floor level directly above the removed element, not exceeding 15% of the total floor area (exterior removal) or 30% of the total floor area (interior removal) for each respective floor (printed p. 17, Figures 3.13/3.14).

ParameterTypeDescription
is_exterior_removalfloatrequiredTrue for an exterior column/wall removal scenario, False for interior.

enhanced_local_resistance_removed — Section 3.3: "This UFC section has been removed in its entirety" (printed p. 31). Enhanced Local Resistance (ELR) is likewise removed from every material chapter (Sections 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.6, 8.5).

No parameters.

force_controlled_capacity_check — Equations 3.7 (LSP), 3.10 (NSP), 3.12 (NDP): acceptance check for force-controlled actions, all primary and secondary components, identical in form across all three procedures (printed pp. 25-26, 28-29, 31).

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredStrength reduction factor from the applicable material code.
q_clfloatrequiredLower-bound strength of the component for the force-controlled action.
q_uffloatrequiredForce-controlled action from the analysis model (LSP, NSP, or NDP).

force_controlled_load_lsp — Equation 3.5: increased gravity load for FORCE-controlled actions in the LSP (printed pp. 21-22).

ParameterTypeDescription
omega_lffloatrequiredLoad increase factor for force-controlled actions (always 2.0 per Table 4).
dfloatrequired
lfloatoptional
sfloatoptional

gravity_load_away_from_removal — Equation 3.4 (also restated as Equation 3.9 for NSP and Equation 3.11 for NDP, applied to the whole structure): gravity load for bays NOT loaded with the increased (LIF/DIF) load (printed pp. 21, 27, 30).

ParameterTypeDescription
dfloatrequired
lfloatoptional
sfloatoptional

irregularity_check — Section 3.2.11.1.1: a structure is IRREGULAR (restricting LSP use, see `lsp_applicable`) if ANY of four printed conditions is true (printed pp. 19-20):

ParameterTypeDescription
has_discontinuityfloatoptional
has_asymmetric_bay_stiffnessfloatoptional
has_asymmetric_wall_stiffnessfloatoptional
has_nonorthogonal_lateral_elementsfloatoptional

lrfd_strength_check — Equation 3.1: general LRFD design-strength adequacy check used throughout the Alternate Path method (printed p. 8).

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredStrength reduction factor from the applicable material-specific code.
rnfloatrequiredNominal strength -- the expected strength QCE for deformation- controlled actions, or the lower-bound strength QCL for force- controlled actions (Section 3.2.6).
rufloatrequiredRequired strength (Sum gamma_i * Q_i).

lsp_applicable — Section 3.2.11.1: determines whether the Linear Static Procedure (LSP) may be used (printed p. 19), independent of the 10-story limit (`lsp_story_limit`).

ParameterTypeDescription
is_irregularfloatrequiredFrom `irregularity_check`.
max_dcrfloatoptionalLargest component DCR in the structure (required if irregular).

lsp_story_limit — Section 3.2.11.1: the Linear Static Procedure (LSP) is limited to structures of 10 STORIES OR LESS (printed p. 19) -- a limitation NOT present in UFC 4-023-03's own LSP applicability section, which has no story-count cap.

No parameters.

nonlinear_dynamic_load — Equation 3.11: gravity load applied to the ENTIRE structure for the Nonlinear Dynamic Procedure, before the column/wall section is removed (printed p. 30). Identical form to Equation 3.4/3.9, no load increase factor (the dynamic effect is captured by the removal-duration requirement of Section 3.2.13.4.2, not a static multiplier).

ParameterTypeDescription
dfloatrequired
lfloatoptional
sfloatoptional

nonlinear_static_load — Equation 3.8: increased gravity load for the Nonlinear Static Procedure, both deformation- and force-controlled actions together (printed p. 27).

ParameterTypeDescription
omega_nfloatrequiredDynamic increase factor from `table_5_dynamic_increase_factor`.
dfloatrequired
lfloatoptional
sfloatoptional

removal_locations_fsl_3_4 — Section 3.2.9(1): for FSL III and IV, vertical load-bearing elements are removed at EXTERIOR locations at the first floor above grade, and at ALL elements (interior and exterior) within underground parking, loading docks, and areas of uncontrolled public access (printed p. 12). "Controlled public access" requires BOTH badge-ID access control with guard inspection AND x-ray/magnetometer screening of visitors and their property.

No parameters.

removal_locations_fsl_5 — Section 3.2.9(2): for FSL V, BOTH interior and exterior vertical load-bearing elements are removed AT EACH FLOOR LEVEL of the building (printed p. 12) -- unlike FSL III/IV, there is no restriction to the ground floor or to uncontrolled-access areas. Commentary C2.3 notes this whole-building removal scope is why Redundancy Requirements (Section 3.4) need not be separately applied to FSL V facilities (see `applicability.fsl_applicability`).

No parameters.

removed_element_extent — Section 3.2.9.1: for ANY column removal, remove the full clear height between lateral restraints. For an external/internal load-bearing WALL corner, remove a length equal to the clear story height H in each direction (Sections 3.2.9.2.4/3.2.9.2.5); a non-corner wall removal (Section 3.2.9.2.4 "as a minimum... near the middle") uses the same clear-story-height extent by convention of the accompanying figures (printed pp. 12, 14-15).

ParameterTypeDescription
clear_height_or_story_heightfloatrequiredClear column height between lateral restraints, OR clear story height H for a wall removal (ft or m).

table_4_load_increase_factor — Table 4: Linear Static load increase factors Omega_LD (deformation-controlled) and Omega_LF (force-controlled, always 2.0) (printed p. 22).

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatrequired'steel', 'reinforced_concrete', 'masonry', 'wood', or 'cold_formed_steel'.
structure_typefloatrequired'framed' (steel or reinforced_concrete only) or 'load_bearing_wall'.
m_liffloatrequiredSmallest primary-beam/girder/spandrel/wall m-factor per the definition above.

table_5_dynamic_increase_factor — Table 5: Nonlinear Static dynamic increase factor Omega_N (printed p. 28). For steel-framed and RC-framed structures, Omega_N is a function of the normalized rotation ratio theta_pra/theta_y (choose the SMALLEST such ratio for any primary element/connection within or touching the region loaded with the increased gravity load; columns excluded). Load-bearing-wall structures of any material are fixed at 2.0.

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatrequired'steel', 'reinforced_concrete', 'masonry', 'wood', or 'cold_formed_steel'.
structure_typefloatrequired'framed' or 'load_bearing_wall'.
theta_prafloatoptionalPlastic rotation angle acceptance-criteria limit (radians) for the governing primary element/connection. Required for framed steel or RC.
theta_yfloatoptionalYield rotation angle (radians) for the same element. Required for framed steel or RC.

tie_forces_removed — Section 3.1: "This UFC section is removed in its entirety," including Figures 3.1 through 3.6 (printed p. 7). GSA's Guidelines do not permit Tie Forces as an alternative to, or supplement of, the Alternate Path method for ANY Facility Security Level or occupancy (Commentary C3.1).

No parameters.

fixed_fixed_flexural_stiffness — Appendix D worked example (printed pp. D52-D53), per Figure 3.20's support-condition-dependent stiffness definitions: flexural stiffness of a fixed-fixed beam under a uniformly distributed load, used as the component stiffness KC when reinforcement is continuous through both end connections (fix-fix boundary conditions, prior to column/wall removal).

ParameterTypeDescription
ecfloatrequiredModulus of elasticity of concrete (ksi or equivalent).
icrfloatrequiredCracked moment of inertia of the transformed section, typically 0.3*Ig per Section 10.4.1.2 modeling guidance (in4 or equivalent).
lengthfloatrequiredClear or center-to-center beam length, consistent with the as-built support condition (in or equivalent).

load_redistribution_average_stiffness — Equation 3.19: average flexural stiffness of ALL load redistribution systems up the height of the building, for a given exterior ground-level removal location (printed p. 36).

ParameterTypeDescription
kr_valuesfloatrequiredFlexural stiffness KRi (`load_redistribution_system_stiffness`) of each of the n load redistribution systems.

load_redistribution_average_strength — Equation 3.16: average design strength of ALL load redistribution systems up the height of the building, for a given exterior ground-level removal location (printed p. 33).

ParameterTypeDescription
qr_valuesfloatrequiredDesign strength QRi (`load_redistribution_system_strength`) of each of the n load redistribution systems.

load_redistribution_stiffness_ratio — Equation 3.17: for each exterior ground-level column/wall plan removal location, the variation of the flexural stiffness of any load redistributing system shall be within +/-30% of the average flexural stiffness up the height of the building (printed p. 34). Interior column/wall plan removal scenarios need not be considered.

ParameterTypeDescription
kr_ifloatrequiredFlexural stiffness of the load redistributing system at a single floor level (`load_redistribution_system_stiffness`).
kr_barfloatrequiredAverage flexural stiffness up the height of the building (`load_redistribution_average_stiffness`).

load_redistribution_strength_ratio — Equation 3.14: for each exterior ground-level column/wall plan removal location, the variation of the design strength of any load redistributing system shall be within +/-30% of the average design strength up the height of the building (printed p. 31). Interior column/wall plan removal scenarios need not be considered.

ParameterTypeDescription
qr_ifloatrequiredDesign strength of the load redistributing system at a single floor level (`load_redistribution_system_strength`).
qr_barfloatrequiredAverage design strength up the height of the building (`load_redistribution_average_strength`).

load_redistribution_system_stiffness — Equation 3.18: flexural stiffness of a given load redistributing system at a single floor level (printed p. 35).

ParameterTypeDescription
component_stiffnessesfloatrequiredFlexural stiffness KC of each contributing horizontal member (e.g. kip/in), based on its as-built (pre-removal) support conditions and a uniformly distributed load (Figure 3.20).
phi_factorsfloatoptionalStrength reduction factor Phi for each member, if applying Equation 3.18 literally. Default None (KC summed directly, per the Appendix D worked-example convention).

load_redistribution_system_strength — Equation 3.15: design strength of a given load redistributing system at a single floor level, associated with an exterior ground-level column/wall removal location (printed p. 32).

ParameterTypeDescription
component_strengthsfloatrequiredExpected strength QC of each contributing horizontal member or connection (consistent force/moment units, e.g. kip-in).
phi_factorsfloatrequiredStrength reduction factor Phi for each corresponding member, from the appropriate material-specific code.

minimum_load_redistribution_systems — Equation 3.13: minimum number of vertical load redistribution systems required up the height of the building (printed p. 31).

ParameterTypeDescription
total_floorsfloatrequiredN, the total number of floors in the building.

column_deformation_controlled_shear_check — Appendix D worked example (printed p. D13): for PRELIMINARY column m-factor evaluation, a column may be assumed deformation-controlled if the shear-demand-to-shear-capacity ratio Vp/Vo <= 0.6 (per ASCE 41 Table 10-9 guidance, cross-referenced by Section 4.4.3). This assumption must be VERIFIED after the column-removal analysis is performed (Section 3.2.10/D4.3): any column with Vp/Vo >= 0.6 must be reclassified as force-controlled and reevaluated under the force-controlled modeling assumptions -- consistent with every column in the Appendix D example ultimately being governed as force- controlled (Table D17).

ParameterTypeDescription
vpfloatrequiredColumn shear demand.
vofloatrequiredColumn shear capacity using expected material properties.

table_6_beam_flexure_modeling — Table 6(i): nonlinear modeling parameters (a, b, c) and acceptance- criteria plastic rotations for a reinforced-concrete beam controlled by FLEXURE (printed p. 39, replaces ASCE 41 Table 10-7). Linear interpolation between the printed grid points is permitted (footnote 1) and performed here over rho_diff_over_rho_bal in [0.0, 0.5] and vw_ratio in [3, 6].

ParameterTypeDescription
rho_diff_over_rho_balfloatrequired(rho - rho') / rho_bal for the section, clamped to [0.0, 0.5] for interpolation.
transverse_reinffloatrequired'C' (conforming) or 'NC' (nonconforming) -- footnote 4: conforming means hoops spaced <= d/3 within the flexural plastic hinge region, and (for components of moderate/high ductility demand) the strength provided by the hoops (Vs) is at least 3/4 of the design shear.
vw_ratiofloatrequiredV / (bw d sqrt(f'c)) [psi units, f'c in psi], clamped to [3, 6] for interpolation.

table_6_beam_other_modeling — Table 6(ii-iv): nonlinear modeling parameters for RC beams controlled by SHEAR, inadequate development/splicing, or inadequate embedment into the beam-column joint (printed p. 39).

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'shear', 'development', or 'inadequate_embedment'.
stirrup_spacing_le_d2floatoptionalTrue if stirrup spacing <= d/2 (governs 'shear' and 'development' only). Default True.

table_7_beam_flexure_mfactor — Table 7(i): linear-model m-factors for an RC beam controlled by FLEXURE, primary and secondary components (printed p. 40, replaces ASCE 41 Table 10-13). Bilinear interpolation over rho_diff_over_rho_bal in [0.0, 0.5] and vw_ratio in [3, 6] (footnote 1).

ParameterTypeDescription
rho_diff_over_rho_balfloatrequired(rho - rho') / rho_bal, clamped to [0.0, 0.5].
transverse_reinffloatrequired'C' (conforming) or 'NC' (nonconforming).
vw_ratiofloatrequiredV / (bw d sqrt(f'c)), clamped to [3, 6].

table_7_beam_other_mfactor — Table 7(ii-iv): linear-model m-factors for an RC beam controlled by shear, inadequate development/splicing, or inadequate embedment (printed p. 40).

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'shear', 'development', or 'inadequate_embedment'.
stirrup_spacing_le_d2floatoptionalTrue if stirrup spacing <= d/2. Default True.

table_8_slab_flexure_modeling — Table 8(i): nonlinear modeling parameters and acceptance criteria for a two-way slab or slab-column connection controlled by FLEXURE (printed p. 41, replaces ASCE 41 Table 10-15). Interpolated over Vg/Vo in [0.2, 0.4] (footnote 1); the residual strength ratio c is undefined ('-') when continuity_reinforcement=False, matching the printed table (no residual capacity without continuity reinforcement).

ParameterTypeDescription
vg_over_vofloatrequiredRatio of gravity shear on the slab critical section (Vg, per ACI 318) to the direct punching shear strength (Vo, per ACI 318), clamped to [0.2, 0.4].
continuity_reinforcementfloatrequiredTrue ('Yes') if at least one main bottom bar (or, for post-tensioned slabs, one tendon) in each direction is effectively continuous through the column cage; else False ('No').

table_8_slab_other_modeling — Table 8(ii-iii): nonlinear modeling parameters for a two-way slab controlled by inadequate development/splicing, or inadequate embedment into the slab-column joint (printed p. 41).

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'development' or 'inadequate_embedment'.

table_9_slab_flexure_mfactor — Table 9(i): linear-model m-factors for a two-way slab or slab-column connection controlled by FLEXURE (printed p. 42, replaces ASCE 41 Table 10-16). Interpolated over Vg/Vo in [0.2, 0.4].

ParameterTypeDescription
vg_over_vofloatrequiredVg/Vo per ACI 318, clamped to [0.2, 0.4].
continuity_reinforcementfloatrequiredTrue ('Yes') or False ('No') per the continuity-reinforcement definition in `table_8_slab_flexure_modeling`.

table_9_slab_other_mfactor — Table 9(ii-iii): linear-model m-factors for a two-way slab controlled by inadequate development/splicing or inadequate embedment into the slab-column joint (printed p. 42). BOTH conditions print a primary m-factor of "-" (not applicable) and a secondary m-factor of 4 -- see module docstring cross-check note.

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'development' or 'inadequate_embedment'.

column_axial_classification — Section 5.4.3: classifies a steel column's P-M interaction as force- or deformation-controlled based on the axial-load ratio P/PCL (printed pp. 43-44).

ParameterTypeDescription
pfloatrequiredAxial load from the analysis (kip or kN).
p_clfloatrequiredLower-bound axial compressive strength, PCL (kip or kN).

list_table_c1_1_connection_types — Lists the connection-type keys in `TABLE_C1_1_CONNECTION_TYPES`.

ParameterTypeDescription
restraintfloatoptionalFilter to 'FR' or 'PR' (matches connections classified purely as that type; the one 'FR or PR' entry, bolted_flange_plates, is excluded from both filters -- request it directly by name). Default None (return all).

table_10_fr_connection_mfactor — Table 10, Fully Restrained Moment Connections: linear-model m-factors as a function of beam depth d (printed p. 45).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequiredOne of 'improved_wuf_bolted_web', 'reduced_beam_section', 'wuf', 'sideplate'.
dfloatrequiredBeam depth (inch).

table_10_pr_flexible_connection_mfactor — Table 10, Partially Restrained Simple/Moment Connections (Flexible): linear-model m-factors as a function of bolt-group depth dbg (printed p. 45).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_angles' (requires limit_state) or 'simple_shear_tab'.
dbgfloatrequiredDepth of the bolt group (inch).
limit_statefloatoptionalFor 'double_angles': 'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', or 'flexure_in_angles'. Not used for 'simple_shear_tab'.

table_10_pr_stiff_connection_mfactor — Table 10, Partially Restrained Moment Connections (Relatively Stiff): constant linear-model m-factors by limit state (printed p. 45).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_split_tee'.
limit_statefloatrequired'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', 'tension_in_tee', or 'flexure_in_tee'.

table_11_fr_connection_modeling — Table 11, Fully Restrained Moment Connections: nonlinear modeling parameters (a, b, c) and acceptance criteria (equal to a, b per the printed table) as a function of beam depth d (printed p. 46).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequiredOne of 'improved_wuf_bolted_web', 'reduced_beam_section', 'wuf', 'sideplate'.
dfloatrequiredBeam depth (inch).

table_11_pr_flexible_connection_modeling — Table 11, Partially Restrained Simple/Moment Connections (Flexible): nonlinear modeling parameters and acceptance criteria as a function of bolt-group depth dbg (printed p. 46).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_angles' (requires limit_state) or 'simple_shear_tab'.
dbgfloatrequiredDepth of the bolt group (inch).
limit_statefloatoptionalFor 'double_angles': 'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', or 'flexure_in_angles'.

table_11_pr_stiff_connection_modeling — Table 11, Partially Restrained Moment Connections (Relatively Stiff): constant nonlinear modeling parameters and acceptance criteria by limit state (printed p. 46).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_split_tee'.
limit_statefloatrequired'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', 'tension_in_tee', or 'flexure_in_tee'.

table_c1_1_connection_type — Table C1.1: steel frame beam-to-column connection-type inventory -- description, Fully/Partially Restrained (FR/PR) classification, and illustrating figure (printed p. C19). This is a descriptive/ classification inventory (Appendix C commentary); the corresponding numeric m-factors and modeling parameters, where this document specifies its own values, are in `table_10_*/table_11_*` above.

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequiredA key of `TABLE_C1_1_CONNECTION_TYPES` (e.g. 'reduced_beam_section', 'shear_tab_connection').

cfs_material_basis — Section 8.1: ASCE 41 provides default expected-strength values for light-metal-framing shear walls (printed p. 50).

No parameters.

cfs_phi_basis — Section 8.2: strength reduction factor Phi for cold-formed steel is per the AISI/COS/NASPEC North American Specification for the Design of Cold-Formed Steel Structural Members (printed p. 50).

No parameters.

default_lower_bound_factor — Sections 7.1 and 8.1: when default LOWER BOUND strength values are needed for wood or cold-formed steel construction (and statistically- determined values are unavailable), multiply the default EXPECTED strength values by 0.85 (printed pp. 48, 50).

No parameters.

masonry_material_basis — Section 6.1: over-strength factors for masonry are per ASCE 41 Table 11-1 (printed p. 47).

No parameters.

masonry_phi_basis — Section 6.2: strength reduction factor Phi for masonry is per ACI 530, Building Code Requirements for Masonry Structures (printed p. 47).

No parameters.

masonry_wood_cfs_performance_level — Sections 6.4.2, 7.5.2, 8.4.2: masonry, wood, and cold-formed steel each use ASCE 41's LIFE SAFETY (not Collapse Prevention) modeling parameters, nonlinear acceptance criteria, and linear m-factors for primary and secondary components, from ASCE 41 Chapter 11 (masonry) or Chapter 12 (wood, cold-formed steel) (printed pp. 47, 49, 50). Commentary C6/C7/C8 (printed p. C23) attributes this to a lack of available test data supporting a change to Collapse Prevention for these materials -- contrast reinforced concrete and structural steel (Chapters 4-5), which DO use Collapse Prevention.

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatrequired'masonry', 'wood', or 'cold_formed_steel'.

wood_material_basis — Section 7.1: default expected-strength values for wood materials are based on design resistance values from AF&PA/ASCE 16 (1996), per ASCE 41; ASCE 41 also provides default expected strengths for shear walls and wood diaphragms (printed p. 48).

No parameters.

wood_phi_basis — Section 7.2: strength reduction factor Phi for wood is per AF&PA/AWC National Design Specification (NDS) for Wood Construction (printed p. 48).

No parameters.

wood_time_effect_factor — Section 7.3: the wood time-effect factor lambda is 1.0 (printed p. 48) -- IDENTICAL to UFC 4-023-03's own printed value (see `geotech_references.ufc_collapse`'s docstring reference to this factor).

No parameters.

retrieve_section — Retrieve one section by its ID, at any level: its own text, 'under' (the sections above it) and 'children' (ID and title of each subsection, fetched by its own ID). A missing ID's error names the nearest section above it and the sections numbered under it.

ParameterTypeDescription
section_idstrrequiredSection identifier at any level (e.g. '2', '1.2.1', '3.2.9.1.1').
include_subsectionsbooloptionalInline the subsections' text too, when the whole fits in 12,000 characters; otherwise they stay listed in 'children' with a note.

search_sections — Keyword search across every section and subsection, best first: each hit is a section's number, title, chapter, 'under' (the sections above it) and a snippet of its text, never the whole text (retrieve_section fetches that). As many hits as fit; 'next_offset' and a note say how to get more.

ParameterTypeDescription
querystrrequiredSearch query (case-insensitive, multi-word AND).
limitintoptionalMost hits to return (at most 50; fewer when they would not fit).
offsetintoptionalSkip this many of the best hits: the 'next_offset' of the last call.

list_chapters — List chapters and their sections by ID and title, subsections included (a nested one carries parent_id). Without 'chapter': every chapter, with its sections when the whole listing fits one result (otherwise titles and section counts, and a note). With 'chapter': that chapter's sections.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintoptionalChapter number: list its sections. Leave out for every chapter.

load_chapter — Load a whole chapter: every section's text. A chapter too long for one result (most are) comes back as its list of sections with a note: fetch the ones you need with retrieve_section.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintrequiredChapter number.

10.1.41 pavement_design — pavement_design

flexible_pavement_design — AASHTO 1993 flexible pavement design (Fig 3.1/3.2): required SN + layered D1/D2/D3 split with drainage m, Sec 3.1.4 minimums and forward check; or adequacy check of a given section. US customary units.

ParameterTypeDescription
w18numberrequiredDesign-lane 18-kip ESALs over the performance period (use design_traffic_esals to build it).
layersarrayrequiredList of layer dicts, TOP-DOWN; first must be layer_type 'asphalt'. Each: {layer_type: asphalt|granular_base|granular_subbase|cement_treated_base|bituminous_treated_base; modulus_psi (EAC/EBS/ESB -- required on non-surface layers in design mode); ucs_7day_psi (cement-treated); marshall_stability_lb (bituminous-treated); a (direct coefficient override); m (drainage, unbound layers) or drainage_quality + pct_saturation_time ('<1%'|'1-5%'|'5-25%'|'>25%'); thickness_in (set on EVERY layer for a check instead of a design); min_thickness_in}.
reliability_pctnumberoptionalReliability R % (50-99.99), Table 4.1 -> ZR. Or give zr.
zrnumberoptionalStandard normal deviate directly (overrides reliability_pct).
sonumberoptionalOverall standard deviation (flexible range 0.40-0.50).
mr_psinumberoptionalEffective roadbed resilient modulus, psi (or monthly_mr_psi).
monthly_mr_psiarrayoptionalSeasonal roadbed MR list (psi) -> Fig 2.3/2.4 effective MR.
ptnumberoptionalTerminal serviceability.
ponumberoptionalInitial serviceability.
delta_psinumberoptionalServiceability loss directly (else po - pt).
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound-UP increment.
enforce_minimumsbooleanoptionalApply Sec 3.1.4 minimum AC/base thicknesses.
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionalFrost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr.
design_period_yrnumberoptionalAnalysis period (yr); required with swelling/frost -- their dPSI loss is subtracted from the design budget before the solve.

rigid_pavement_design — AASHTO 1993 rigid (PCC slab) design (Fig 3.7): required slab thickness D with k from direct value, MR/19.4, or the full Sec 3.2 composite-k worksheet (iterated with D); or adequacy check. US customary units.

ParameterTypeDescription
w18numberrequiredDesign-lane 18-kip ESALs.

slab_thickness_innumberoptionalGive to CHECK a slab instead of designing.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound-UP increment.
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionalFrost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr.
design_period_yrnumberoptionalAnalysis period (yr); required with swelling/frost -- their dPSI loss is subtracted from the design budget before the solve.

design_traffic_esals — Design-lane cumulative 18-kip ESALs: axle-load spectrum (Appendix D LEFs, single/tandem/triple), per-vehicle truck factors, or a base-year total; compound growth + directional DD + lane DL.

ParameterTypeDescription
axle_groupsarrayoptional[{axle_config: single|tandem|triple, load_kips, daily_count (two-way)}]; LEFs at the assumed sn/d_in/pt.
vehiclesarrayoptional[{description, daily_count, truck_factor (ESALs/pass)}].
base_year_w18_two_waynumberoptionalFirst-year two-way ESALs directly.
growth_rate_pctnumberoptionalAnnual growth rate %.
design_period_yrnumberoptionalPerformance period, yr.
pavement_typestringoptionalFor LEF selection. allowed: flexible, rigid
snnumberoptionalAssumed SN for flexible LEFs.
d_innumberoptionalAssumed slab D for rigid LEFs.
ptnumberoptionalTerminal serviceability for LEFs.
directional_factornumberoptionalDD split (0.3-0.7).
num_lanes_per_directionintegeroptionalFor the DL table.
lane_factornumberoptionalDL fraction directly (else table midpoint).

effective_subgrade_modulus — Effective roadbed resilient modulus from seasonal (monthly) MR values via the Fig 2.3/2.4 relative-damage average (flexible design input).

ParameterTypeDescription
monthly_mr_psiarrayrequiredSeasonal roadbed MR values, psi (typically 12).

flexible_pavement_design_ufc — UFC 3-250-01 (DoD roads/parking) flexible design — the CBR-method ALTERNATIVE to AASHTO: Figure E-1 cover curves, Table 7-2 minimums, optional seasonal-frost reduced-subgrade-strength check. US customary.

ParameterTypeDescription
passes_18kipnumberrequiredDesign-life passes of the 18-kip single axle (design lane). NOT interchangeable with AASHTO W18 conceptually — same count, different damage model.
cbr_subgradenumberrequiredSubgrade design CBR (%).
cbr_basenumberoptionalBase course design CBR.
cbr_subbasenumberoptionalSubbase CBR (omit for a 2-layer section).
frostobjectoptional{uscs_class, finer_than_0_02mm_pct} -> Ch 19 reduced-subgrade-strength frost check; governing section reported.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound layer thicknesses up to this increment (in).

rigid_pavement_design_ufc — UFC 3-250-01 rigid (plain concrete) design — Figure F-1 (flexural strength x k x 18-kip passes) with the Eq 13-1 stabilized-foundation reduction. US customary.

ParameterTypeDescription
passes_18kipnumberrequired18-kip single-axle passes.
flexural_strength_psinumberrequiredConcrete flexural strength R (psi).

stabilized_foundationobjectoptional{ef_psi, hs_in} -> Eq 13-1 reduction.
thickness_increment_innumberoptionalRound the slab up to this increment (in).

compare_pavement_methods — Run AASHTO 1993 AND UFC 3-250-01 flexible designs on a shared 18-kip pass count and compare sections side by side, with every cross-guide assumption (CBR<->Mr correlation, AASHTO-only reliability) stated in notes.

ParameterTypeDescription
passes_18kipnumberrequired18-kip single-axle passes (= AASHTO W18; LEF 1.0 by definition).
cbr_subgradenumberoptionalSubgrade CBR (Mr derived via FHWA 2555*CBR^0.64). Give this OR mr_psi.

reliability_pctnumberoptionalAASHTO-side reliability.
sonumberoptionalAASHTO overall standard deviation.

ebs_psinumberoptionalAASHTO base modulus override.

mixed_traffic_ufc — UFC 3-250-01 automated mixed-traffic reduction (Table G-1 procedure): per-vehicle thickness from the Appendix E curves at a representative CBR, controlling vehicle, allowable-passes inversion, equivalent-pass roll-up. Feeds flexible_pavement_design_ufc.

ParameterTypeDescription
vehiclesarrayrequired[{vehicle: E-1 (18-kip ESAL) or E-2..E-31 / registry slug, design_passes, name?}].

performance_period — Predicted performance period of a DESIGNED section under roadbed swelling / frost heave (the guide's Table 3.1 iteration): environmental dPSI shrinks the traffic budget until trial period and traffic-derived period converge.

ParameterTypeDescription

delta_psi_designnumberrequiredTotal design dPSI (po - pt).
base_year_w18numberrequiredFirst-year design-lane ESALs.
growth_rate_pctnumberoptionalAnnual traffic growth %.
swellingobjectoptionalRoadbed swelling spec (Appendix G / Fig G.4): {vr_in: potential vertical rise (in), ps_pct: percent of area subject to swell, theta: swell rate constant (~0.04-0.20)}. Requires design_period_yr.
frostobjectoptionalFrost heave spec (Appendix G / Fig G.8): {phi_mm_day: heave rate, pf_pct: percent of area subject to heave, delta_psi_max: max loss (Fig G.7, from drainage quality x frost depth)}. Requires design_period_yr.
max_performance_period_yrnumberoptionalCap / default trial seed.
initial_trial_yrnumberoptionalFirst trial performance period (yr); default 0.9 x the cap.
snnumberoptionalFlexible: as-built structural number.
mr_psinumberoptionalFlexible: effective roadbed MR.
d_innumberoptionalRigid: as-built slab thickness.
sc_psinumberoptionalRigid: PCC modulus of rupture.
ec_psinumberoptionalRigid: PCC elastic modulus.
jnumberoptionalRigid: load transfer J.
cdnumberoptionalRigid: drainage Cd.
k_pcinumberoptionalRigid: design k.
ptnumberoptionalTerminal serviceability.
zrnumberoptionalStandard normal deviate (or give reliability_pct).
reliability_pctnumberoptionalReliability R % -> ZR.
