10.1.42 profile_figure — profile_figure

subsurface_profile — Draw a subsurface profile schematic (PNG): soil layers with names/descriptions, water table, optional fill + surcharge, optional pile/micropile/drilled-shaft/footing/wall overlay, and callouts (e.g. neutral plane) at any elevation or depth. Saves the file and returns an <img> tag ready for a report.

ParameterTypeDescription
layersarrayrequiredStrata TOP-DOWN. Each dict: 'name' plus 'thickness' (m) — or a 'top_elevation'/'bottom_elevation' (or 'top_depth'/'bottom_depth') pair. Optional: 'description' (short properties string shown under the name, e.g. 'su = 25 kPa, N=8'), 'settling' (true marks a compressible layer with down-arrows — use it for downdrag/consolidation figures), 'color', 'hatch'. Layers must stack continuously; a gap or overlap is an error.
titlestroptionalFigure title (name the project/boring).
ground_elevationfloatoptionalOriginal ground surface (m). Defaults to the first layer's top_elevation, else 0.0 — with thickness-only layers the axis then reads as depth below ground.
water_elevationfloatoptionalWater-table elevation (m).
water_depthfloatoptionalWater-table depth below ground (m). Alternative to water_elevation.
fillobjectoptionalFill/embankment ABOVE existing grade: {'name', 'thickness'} (or 'top_elevation'), optional 'settling'. A bare number is read as a thickness.
surchargeobjectoptionalSurface surcharge drawn as load arrows: {'pressure': kPa, 'label'} — a bare number is the pressure.
foundationobjectoptionalFoundation overlay: {'type': 'pile'|'micropile'|'drilled_shaft'|'footing'|'wall', 'diameter' (or 'width' for a footing), 'tip_elevation' or 'tip_depth' or 'length', optional 'head_elevation'/'head_depth' (defaults to the top of the section), optional 'label'}. Drawn to true DEPTH; its width is exaggerated so it is visible, with the real dimension in the label.
annotationsarrayoptionalCallouts: [{'elevation' or 'depth', 'text', 'side': 'left'|'right'}] — the neutral plane, a sample depth, top of rock, a design assumption. Drawn as a dashed line across the section with a labelled leader.
axisstroptionalVertical-axis labelling. 'auto' = depth for thickness-only input, elevation once any elevation is given. Presentation only — geometry is unchanged. allowed: auto, elevation, depth
output_pathstroptionalPNG path. A bare filename lands in the working folder. Auto-generated if omitted.
dpiintoptionalRaster resolution; 150 suits a report page.
width_infloatoptionalFigure width (inches).
height_infloatoptionalFigure height (inches).
include_base64booloptionalAlso return the PNG as base64. Rarely needed and VERY large (tens of thousands of characters) — html_to_pdf embeds a local PNG path for you, so leave this off.

plot_data — Generic data plot: one or more x/y series — an SPT or CPT profile against elevation, settlement vs time, load vs displacement, a parameter sweep or method comparison, the cases of a sensitivity study, a plan view of borings and a footprint drawn to scale. Shows in chat as an INTERACTIVE chart (zoom/hover) and saves a PNG for reports, with an <img> tag ready to paste.

ParameterTypeDescription
seriesarrayrequired[{'x': [...], 'y': [...], 'label': str, optional 'style': 'both'|'line'|'markers'|'step'|'polygon', 'color'}]. x and y are equal-length lists. Optional per series: 'marker' (circle, square, triangle, triangle-down, diamond, x, cross, star, hexagon), 'marker_size' (points), 'marker_edge' (outline colour), 'marker_open' (hollow), 'line_dash' (solid, dash, dot, dashdot), 'line_width', 'labels' (one name per point, written beside it, '' to skip one), 'hover' (one text per point, shown on hover in the interactive chart; '
' breaks a line), 'in_legend' (false hides it). Style 'polygon' closes the outline (a footprint, a site boundary, a zone); 'fill': true or a colour, 'fill_opacity' (default 0.2), 'hatch' ('/', '\', 'x', '-', '|', '+', '.') to mark a zone over what lies under it. x given as names (cases, scenarios, borings) puts them along the x axis in order: draw separate cases with style 'markers', since a line between unrelated cases shows a trend that is not there. Name points on the figure with 'labels' rather than a legend entry each.
annotationsarrayoptionalText placed where you put it: a note, the name of a zone or a line, a reading at a point. It is never moved (point names keep clear of it). [{'text', 'x', 'y'}] in data units (a case's name for x on a case axis), or with 'coords': 'axes' in fractions of the plot (0, 0 bottom left; 1, 1 top right). Optional: 'point': [x, y] in data units, the point the note marks, drawn as a leader arrow from the text; 'align': the side of the text that stands at x, y (center, left, right, top, bottom, or e.g. 'top left'); 'box': true for a plain white box behind the text (or a colour); 'halo': true for a thin ring of the background round the letters, so hatching or a grid behind them stops short (the PNG); 'color'; 'font_size' (pt). A new line or '
' breaks a line. The warnings say when a note overlaps other lettering, a line runs through it or it stands outside the plot.
equal_aspectbooloptionalDraw one unit across as long as one unit up: set it for every plan view, site map, footprint or section drawn to scale (x and y both lengths in the same unit). The figure takes the data's own proportions and the legend moves outside the map.
plan_viewbooloptionalDraw a site plan as a drawing, not a chart: to scale, no axes, axis numbers or grid, a scale bar with xlabel (name the coordinate system there) under it, and a north arrow from north_deg. Use it for a plan of a site, compound or property; draw the property line as a polygon with line_dash 'dashdot'.
north_degfloatoptionalDirection of north on the page, degrees clockwise from straight up, as the plan the data came from (or the project's other plans) shows it. Not given: drawn straight up, and the result says so.
scale_unitsstroptionalLength unit written on the scale bar: m, km, cm, mm, ft, in, yd, mi.
xlimarrayoptional[start, end] of the x axis, kept in the order given: [100, 0.001] runs it from high to low (on a log axis too). Else fitted.
ylimarrayoptional[start, end] of the y axis, kept in the order given (with depth_axis, y runs downward whatever the order). Else fitted.
x_on_topbooloptionalPut the x axis along the top, as a boring log reads, on a profile against elevation (depth_axis does this by itself).
legend_positionstroptionalWhere the legend goes; auto = outside a drawing to scale, inside otherwise. allowed: auto, inside, outside, below
titlestroptionalFigure title.
xlabelstroptionalX-axis label WITH units.
ylabelstroptionalY-axis label WITH units.
depth_axisbooloptionalA profile has elevation on y by default (leave this false, y = elevations): borings start at different ground levels. True when y is depth (only when no elevations are given; say so in ylabel) or settlement: y increases DOWNWARD and the x axis sits at the top (boring-log convention).
logxbooloptionalLog-scale x axis.
logybooloptionalLog-scale y axis.
hlinesarrayoptionalHorizontal reference lines: [{'value': y, 'label': str}] — e.g. a water table or an allowable value.
vlinesarrayoptionalVertical reference lines: [{'value': x, 'label': str}].
gridbooloptionalDraw a light grid.
legendbooloptionalShow the legend. Default: when more than one series is in it (reference lines are named on the line).
output_pathstroptionalPNG path. A bare filename lands in the working folder. Auto-generated if omitted.
interactivebooloptionalAlso write the interactive chart beside the PNG (<name>.plotly.json) — that is what the chat displays. Set false only when a static image is all you want.
dpiintoptionalRaster resolution.
width_infloatoptionalFigure width (inches).
height_infloatoptionalFigure height (inches). Default 4.5, or the data's proportions with equal_aspect.
include_base64booloptionalAlso return the PNG as base64 — VERY large; html_to_pdf embeds the saved path for you, so leave this off.
reference_chartstroptionalA standard chart's lines drawn under the data as the reference prints them, not from memory: 'uscs_plasticity' (the plasticity chart, UFS 3-220-10 Figure 1-2 as in ASTM D2487: the A-line, level at PI = 4 up to LL = 25.5 and then PI = 0.73(LL - 20); the U-line; LL = 50; PI = LL; the CL-ML zone, hatched as GEC 5 Figure 4-11 prints it; the zone names), 'aashto_plasticity' (GEC 5 Figure 4-12: LL = 40, PI = 10, PI = LL - 30 and the group names) or 'uscs_particle_sizes' (the sieve sizes that bound fines, sand, gravel, cobbles and boulders, on a log grain-size axis). The lines are grey and named on the line; the chart's own axis names and frame are used unless xlabel, ylabel, xlim or ylim are given. The result's reference_chart gives the source, page and each line's equation, for the caption.

10.1.43 ufc_collapse — ufc_collapse

is_story — Section 1-2.1: a penthouse or below-grade level counts as a "story" (toward the 3-story threshold) only if it is designed for human occupancy AND equipped with means of egress, light, and ventilation meeting local code (printed p. 1). An unoccupied level (mechanical equipment, storage) is OMITTED from the story count.

ParameterTypeDescription
has_human_occupancy_egress_light_ventilationfloatrequiredTrue if the level is designed for human occupancy with the listed life-safety features.

partial_occupancy_threshold — Section 1-2.2: when DoD personnel occupy 25% or more of the net interior usable space, this UFC's requirements apply to the ENTIRE structure -- not just the DoD-occupied portion -- superseding the per-portion rule in UFC 4-010-01 (printed p. 1-2).

No parameters.

rc4_tie_force_minimum_exempt — Table 2-2 Footnote A: for progressive-collapse RC IV buildings that are UFC 3-301-01 Risk Category IV, the Tie Force minimum structural requirements (Section 3-1.1: bay-count/wall-length checks) MAY be exempted. For UFC 3-301-01 Risk Category V buildings (also mapped to progressive-collapse RC IV per Table 2-1), those minimum requirements REMAIN mandatory (printed p. 8; restated Section 2-2.4.1, printed pp. 10-11).

ParameterTypeDescription
ufc_3_301_01_risk_categoryfloatrequired'IV' or 'V' (the structure's UNDERLYING UFC 3-301-01 Risk Category, not the progressive-collapse RC).

story_count_threshold — Section 1-2: this UFC's requirements are MANDATORY for all new construction of 3 or more stories; for existing buildings, application is at the discretion of the project proponent or AHJ (printed p. 1).

No parameters.

table_2_1_risk_category — Table 2-1: progressive-collapse Risk Category (RC I-IV) and its corresponding UFC 3-301-01 nature-of-occupancy description (printed p. 7). Note: UFC 3-301-01 Risk Categories IV AND V both map to progressive-collapse RC IV -- there is no progressive-collapse RC V.

ParameterTypeDescription
risk_categoryfloatrequired'I', 'II', 'III', or 'IV'.

table_2_2_design_requirements — Table 2-2: the progressive-collapse design requirement (Tie Forces / Alternate Path / Enhanced Local Resistance combination) for a given Risk Category (printed p. 8).

ParameterTypeDescription
risk_categoryfloatrequired'I', 'II', 'III', or 'IV'.

effective_wf_for_nonuniform_load — Section 3-1.3.2.2: determines the effective wF for a floor with non-uniform bay loading (printed pp. 16-17).

ParameterTypeDescription
bay_loads_and_areasfloatrequiredEach bay's (or bay-group's) wF (Equation 3-2, psf or kN/m2) and its plan area (ft2 or m2).

floor_load_wf — Equation 3-2: floor load used for all Tie Force calculations (printed p. 15).

ParameterTypeDescription
dead_loadfloatrequiredDead load, D (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
live_loadfloatrequiredLive load, L (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).

internal_tie_force_framed — Equation 3-3: internal (longitudinal or transverse) tie force for FRAMED structures, including flat plate/flat slab (printed p. 20).

ParameterTypeDescription
wffloatrequiredFloor load per `floor_load_wf` (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
l1floatrequiredGreater of the distances between centers of columns/frames/walls supporting any two adjacent floor spaces, in the direction under consideration (ft or m).

internal_tie_force_one_way_wall — Equation 3-5: internal tie force for ONE-WAY-SPAN load-bearing wall structures (printed p. 22). Same form as Equations 3-3/3-4; L1 is either LL (longitudinal, greatest wall-center spacing) or LT (transverse, from `one_way_wall_transverse_length`).

ParameterTypeDescription
wffloatrequiredFloor load (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
l1floatrequiredLL or LT as defined above (ft or m).

internal_tie_force_two_way_wall — Equation 3-4: internal tie force for TWO-WAY-SPAN load-bearing wall structures (printed p. 21). Same form as Equation 3-3.

ParameterTypeDescription
wffloatrequiredFloor load (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
l1floatrequiredGreater of the distances between centers of walls supporting any two adjacent floor spaces, in the direction under consideration.

max_force_in_column_or_wall_strip — Section 3-1.4.1.1/3-1.4.1.2: for flat-plate/flat-slab framed buildings (no beams/girders/spandrels) or the wall strip of a two-way load-bearing wall building, no more than TWICE the required tie strength (force per unit length) may be concentrated in the column/ wall strip, 0.2*L wide and centered on the column/wall line (printed pp. 20-21). Reproduces the printed worked example: Fi=10-k/ft, LT=20-ft -> strip width=4-ft, max total force = 2*10*0.2*20 = 80-k.

ParameterTypeDescription
fi_per_lengthfloatrequiredRequired internal tie force per unit length, Fi (k/ft or kN/m).
l_transverse_or_longitudinalfloatrequiredLT or LL for the direction under consideration (ft or m).

max_tie_spacing — Maximum spacing of internal (longitudinal/transverse) ties, common to framed, two-way wall, and one-way wall construction: 0.2*LT or 0.2*LL as appropriate (printed pp. 17, 21, 22).

ParameterTypeDescription
l_transverse_or_longitudinalfloatrequiredLT or LL, the relevant bay/wall spacing (ft or m).

minimum_bays_for_tie_force — Section 3-1.1: checks whether a structure meets the minimum geometric requirements to apply the Tie Force method (printed p. 13-14).

ParameterTypeDescription
bays_direction_1floatrequiredNumber of bays in the (primary/one-way-span) direction.
bays_direction_2floatoptionalNumber of bays in the orthogonal direction (framed/two-way only).
one_way_wallfloatoptionalTrue for a one-way load-bearing wall structure. Default False.
wall_lengthfloatoptionalLength of the load-bearing wall / building width (one-way only).
clear_story_heightfloatoptionalClear story height hw (one-way only, same units as wall_length).

one_way_wall_transverse_length — Section 3-1.4.1.2: the transverse-direction L1 (LT) for ONE-WAY load-bearing wall structures is the lesser of 5*hw or the building width (printed p. 22).

ParameterTypeDescription
clear_story_heightfloatrequiredClear story height, hw (ft or m).
building_widthfloatrequiredBuilding width in the transverse direction (ft or m).

perimeter_column_effective_wf — Averages a perimeter column's cladding (facade) dead load into an effective wF for use with `vertical_tie_force`, reproducing the Appendix D worked example for corner column A1 (printed p. 125):

ParameterTypeDescription
wf_floorfloatrequiredFloor-distributed wF per `floor_load_wf` (psf or kN/m2).
cladding_dead_load_psffloatrequiredCladding (facade) dead load per unit wall area (psf or kN/m2).
clear_story_heightfloatrequiredClear story height, hw (ft or m).
cladding_tributary_widthfloatrequiredTotal length of exterior wall tributary to this column (ft or m), e.g. half-bay on each side.
column_tributary_areafloatrequiredColumn's floor tributary area (ft2 or m2).

peripheral_tie_force_one_way — Equation 3-7: peripheral tie force for ONE-WAY load-bearing wall buildings (printed pp. 24-25).

ParameterTypeDescription
wffloatrequiredFloor load (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
l1floatrequiredFor ties perpendicular to the load-bearing walls (longitudinal): greatest wall-center spacing. For ties parallel to the walls (transverse): 2*hw. At openings: the bay length. (ft or m)
wcfloatrequired1.2 x dead load of cladding over the length of L1, in lb (or kN in SI -- NOT kip); 0 for the end wall (the wall itself is the facade).
wwfloatrequired1.2 x dead load of the wall over the length of hw, in lb (or kN in SI -- NOT kip).
lpfloatoptionalPeripheral-tie width, 3.3 ft (1.0 m). Default 3.3.

peripheral_tie_force_two_way — Equation 3-6: peripheral tie force for FRAMED and TWO-WAY load- bearing wall buildings (printed p. 23).

ParameterTypeDescription
wffloatrequiredFloor load (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
l1floatrequiredGreater of the distances between centers of columns/frames/walls at the building perimeter (or, at openings, the bay length), in the direction under consideration (ft or m).
wcfloatrequired1.2 x dead load of cladding over the length of L1, in lb (or kN in SI -- NOT kip in US customary units, see UNITS note above); the 1.2 LRFD dead-load factor is baked into WC per the source.
lpfloatoptionalPeripheral-tie width, 3.3 ft (1.0 m) per the source. Default 3.3 (ft); pass 1.0 for SI units.

required_tie_area — Rearranges Equation 3-1 to solve for the required steel tie area, following the reinforced-concrete worked example in Appendix D (printed p. 126):

ParameterTypeDescription
rufloatrequiredRequired tie strength (kip or kN).
fyfloatrequiredLower-bound (specified) yield strength of the tie steel (ksi or MPa).
phifloatoptionalStrength reduction factor. Default 0.75 (reinforced-concrete rebar in tension, Section 4-3).
overstrength_factorfloatoptionalFactor translating lower-bound to expected material strength. Default 1.25 (ASCE 41 rebar factor, as used in Appendix D); use the appropriate ASCE 41 Chapter 9-12 factor for other materials.

splice_exclusion_zone — Section 3-1.6.1: for cast-in-place (and topped precast) RC floor ties, Type 1 mechanical splices, welded splices, and Class B lap splices must be located no closer than 20% of the bay/span distance to any vertical load-carrying element -- i.e. splices are permitted only within the middle 60% of the bay/span (printed p. 26). Type 2 mechanical splices are exempt and may be used anywhere in the slab.

ParameterTypeDescription
bay_or_span_lengthfloatrequiredBay spacing (internal ties) or span distance (peripheral ties) in the tie direction (ft or m).

tie_strength_check — Equation 3-1: LRFD tie-strength adequacy check (printed p. 14).

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredStrength reduction factor.
rnfloatrequiredNominal tie strength (material code + ASCE 41 over-strength).
rufloatrequiredRequired tie strength (Sum of gamma_i * Q_i), e.g. from `internal_tie_force_framed, peripheral_tie_force_two_way, or vertical_tie_force`.

vertical_tie_force — Section 3-1.4.3: required vertical tie strength -- the largest vertical load received by a column or load-bearing wall from any one story, using the tributary area and wF (printed p. 25).

ParameterTypeDescription
tributary_areafloatrequiredTributary floor area for the column/wall at one story (ft2 or m2).
wffloatrequiredFloor load per `floor_load_wf`, including any averaged cladding contribution for perimeter columns (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).

adjacent_element_removal_trigger — Section 3-2.9.2.2/3-2.9.2.3 (columns) and 3-2.9.2.4/3-2.9.2.5 (walls): if another load-bearing element is within 30% of the reference dimension from the primary removal location, it must be removed SIMULTANEOUSLY (printed pp. 37-41). The reference dimension is the largest bay dimension for column removals, or the clear story height H for wall removals.

ParameterTypeDescription
distancefloatrequiredDistance from the primary removal location to the other element (ft or m).
reference_dimensionfloatrequiredLargest associated bay dimension (columns) or clear story height H (walls), same units as distance.

classify_action — Section 3-2.5: classifies a component action as deformation- or force-controlled from its ASCE-41-style force-deformation curve type (Figure 3-7) and its e/g ratio (printed pp. 31-32). This is the UFC's OPERATIVE classification rule; Table 3-1 ("Examples of Deformation Controlled and Force-Controlled Actions, from ASCE 41", printed p. 33) is an illustrative example table reproduced from ASCE 41 with a merged/bulleted layout that does not extract unambiguously -- consult the printed page directly for that table; classification should be performed with this function instead.

ParameterTypeDescription
curve_typefloatrequired1, 2, or 3 (ASCE 41 / Figure 3-7 force-deformation curve type).
e_over_gfloatrequiredRatio of deformation e to g on the component's curve (Figure 3-7).
is_primaryfloatrequiredTrue for a primary component (see Section 3-2.4), False for secondary.

dcr — Equation 3-9: Demand-Capacity Ratio, used only to determine LSP applicability for an irregular structure (printed p. 42).

ParameterTypeDescription
q_udlimfloatrequiredDeformation-controlled action from a linear model with gravity dead/live loads increased by the Omega_LD load increase factor (Section 3-2.11.1.2).
q_cefloatrequiredExpected strength of the component (Chapters 4-8).

deformation_controlled_capacity_check — Equation 3-13: Linear Static Procedure acceptance check for deformation-controlled actions, all primary and secondary components (printed p. 49).

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredStrength reduction factor from the applicable material code.
mfloatrequiredComponent/element m-factor (Chapters 4-8).
q_cefloatrequiredExpected strength of the component for the deformation-controlled action.
q_udfloatrequiredDeformation-controlled action from the Linear Static model.

deformation_controlled_load_lsp — Equation 3-10: increased gravity load for DEFORMATION-controlled actions, applied to bays immediately adjacent to and above the removed element (printed p. 44).

ParameterTypeDescription
omega_ldfloatrequiredLoad increase factor for deformation-controlled actions, from `table_3_4_load_increase_factor`.
dfloatrequiredDead load including facade loads (lb/ft2 or kN/m2).
lfloatoptionalLive load including live-load reduction (lb/ft2 or kN/m2). Default 0.
sfloatoptionalSnow load (lb/ft2 or kN/m2). Default 0. Use L or S, not both.

force_controlled_capacity_check — Equations 3-14 (LSP), 3-17 (NSP), 3-19 (NDP): acceptance check for force-controlled actions, all primary and secondary components, identical in form across all three procedures (printed pp. 49, 53, 56).

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredStrength reduction factor from the applicable material code.
q_clfloatrequiredLower-bound strength of the component for the force-controlled action.
q_uffloatrequiredForce-controlled action from the analysis model (LSP, NSP, or NDP).

force_controlled_load_lsp — Equation 3-12: increased gravity load for FORCE-controlled actions in the LSP (printed p. 45).

ParameterTypeDescription
omega_lffloatrequiredLoad increase factor for force-controlled actions (always 2.0 per Table 3-4).
dfloatrequired
lfloatoptional
sfloatoptional

gravity_load_away_from_removal — Equations 3-11 (LSP), 3-16 (NSP) and identical-form 3-18 (NDP, applied to the whole structure): gravity load for bays NOT loaded with the increased (LIF/DIF) load (printed pp. 44-45, 51, 55).

ParameterTypeDescription
dfloatrequired
lfloatoptional
sfloatoptional

irregularity_check — Section 3-2.11.1.1: a structure is IRREGULAR (restricting Linear Static Procedure use, see `lsp_applicable`) if ANY of the four printed conditions is true (printed p. 42):

ParameterTypeDescription
has_discontinuityfloatoptional
has_asymmetric_bay_stiffnessfloatoptional
has_asymmetric_wall_stiffnessfloatoptional
has_nonorthogonal_lateral_elementsfloatoptional

lrfd_strength_check — Equation 3-8: general LRFD design-strength adequacy check used throughout the Alternate Path method (printed p. 29).

ParameterTypeDescription
phifloatrequiredStrength reduction factor from the applicable material code.
rnfloatrequiredNominal strength (expected strength QCE for deformation-controlled actions, or lower-bound strength QCL for force-controlled actions -- see `deformation_controlled_capacity_check and force_controlled_capacity_check` for the m-factor and QCL forms).
rufloatrequiredRequired strength (Sum gamma_i * Q_i).

lsp_applicable — Section 3-2.11.1: determines whether the Linear Static Procedure (LSP) may be used (printed p. 41).

ParameterTypeDescription
is_irregularfloatrequiredFrom `irregularity_check`.
max_dcrfloatoptionalLargest component DCR in the structure (required if irregular).

nonlinear_static_load — Equation 3-15: increased gravity load for the Nonlinear Static Procedure, both deformation- and force-controlled actions together (printed p. 51).

ParameterTypeDescription
omega_nfloatrequiredDynamic increase factor from `table_3_5_dynamic_increase_factor`.
dfloatrequired
lfloatoptional
sfloatoptional

removed_column_extent — Section 3-2.9.1: for ANY column removal case (RC II Option 1 deficient tie, or RC II Option 2/III/IV prescribed removal), the removed extent is the full clear height between lateral restraints (printed p. 36).

ParameterTypeDescription
clear_height_between_lateral_restraintsfloatrequiredClear column height between lateral restraints (ft or m).

removed_wall_extent — Section 3-2.9.1: removed load-bearing-wall length (printed p. 36).

ParameterTypeDescription
clear_story_heightfloatrequiredClear story height, H (ft or m).
deficient_wall_lengthfloatoptionalLength of the wall segment found deficient in vertical tie strength. Required when option='deficient_tie'.
optionfloatoptional'prescribed' (default, RC II Opt 2/III/IV minimum locations) or 'deficient_tie' (RC II Option 1).

required_removal_stories — Section 3-2.9.2.2/3-2.9.2.4: for each PLAN location of a prescribed column or external-wall removal (RC II Option 2, RC III, RC IV), perform an AP analysis for each of these stories (printed pp. 36-38):

No parameters.

table_3_4_load_increase_factor — Table 3-4: Linear Static load increase factors Omega_LD (deformation-controlled) and Omega_LF (force-controlled, always 2.0) (printed p. 46).

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatrequired'steel', 'reinforced_concrete', 'masonry', 'wood', or 'cold_formed_steel'.
structure_typefloatrequired'framed' (steel or reinforced_concrete only) or 'load_bearing_wall'.
m_liffloatrequiredSmallest primary-beam/girder/spandrel/wall m-factor per the definition above.

table_3_5_dynamic_increase_factor — Table 3-5: Nonlinear Static dynamic increase factor Omega_N (printed p. 52). For steel-framed and RC-framed structures, Omega_N is a function of the normalized rotation ratio theta_pra/theta_y (choose the SMALLEST such ratio for any primary element/connection within or touching the region loaded with the increased gravity load, Figures 3-13/3-14; columns excluded). Load-bearing-wall structures of any material, and this equation's derivation, are fixed at 2.0.

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatrequired'steel', 'reinforced_concrete', 'masonry', 'wood', or 'cold_formed_steel'.
structure_typefloatrequired'framed' or 'load_bearing_wall'.
theta_prafloatoptionalPlastic rotation angle acceptance-criteria limit (radians) for the governing primary element/connection. Required for framed steel or RC.
theta_yfloatoptionalYield rotation angle (radians) for the same element. Required for framed steel or RC.

elr_location_requirement — Section 3-3.2: identifies where Enhanced Local Resistance must be applied for a given Risk Category (printed pp. 57-58). RC II ELR applies only under Option 1 (Tie Force + ELR); RC III and RC IV both require ELR at ALL perimeter first-story columns/walls (RC III via the Alternate Path option; RC IV in addition to Tie Force + AP).

ParameterTypeDescription
risk_categoryfloatrequired'II', 'III', or 'IV' (ELR is not applicable to RC I; RC II Option 2 does not require ELR at all -- see `applicability` module).
one_way_wallfloatoptionalTrue for a one-way load-bearing wall building. Default False (framed or two-way load-bearing wall).

elr_lrfd_check — Equation 3-20: ELR design-strength adequacy check (printed p. 56). Phi is always 1.0 for ELR (Section 3-3.1) and expected material strengths are used throughout, so this reduces to Rn >= Ru.

ParameterTypeDescription
rnfloatrequiredNominal strength using expected material strength and appropriate over-strength factors (Phi=1.0 baked in per Section 3-3.1).
rufloatrequiredRequired strength (shear or flexural demand).

rc4_column_flexural_demand — Section 3-3.5.1: for RC IV columns, the ELR flexural demand is the LARGER of (1) the baseline gravity-only-design nominal flexural strength multiplied by 2.0, and (2) the current (all-loads) design's nominal flexural strength (printed pp. 58-59). If condition 1 governs, the column must be redesigned to meet it.

ParameterTypeDescription
baseline_gravity_only_mnfloatrequiredNominal flexural strength of the column when designed for gravity loads only, after the AP procedure is applied.
current_design_mnfloatrequiredNominal flexural strength of the column as designed for all applicable loads (wind, seismic, gravity, etc.) after AP.

rc4_wall_flexural_demand — Section 3-3.5.1: for RC IV load-bearing walls, the ELR flexural demand is the LARGER of (1) the baseline gravity-only-design nominal flexural strength multiplied by 1.5, and (2) the current (all-loads) design's nominal flexural strength (printed p. 59).

ParameterTypeDescription
baseline_gravity_only_mnfloatrequiredNominal flexural strength of the wall when designed for gravity loads only, after the AP procedure is applied.
current_design_mnfloatrequiredNominal flexural strength of the wall as designed for all applicable loads after AP.

rebound_reaction_force — Section 3-3.6: connections at the top and bottom of ELR columns/ walls must be designed for a rebound reaction force equal to 50% of the inbound value, to resist the initial-inbound-then-rebound dynamic loading (printed p. 59).

ParameterTypeDescription
inbound_reaction_forcefloatrequiredDesign reaction force for the inbound (loading) phase (kip or kN).

shear_demand_pinned_fixed_column — Equation D-1 (Appendix D, printed p. 129): the ELR shear demand for a column considered pinned at its base and fixed (via floor-diaphragm continuity) at the first level above grade, developing a three-hinge mechanism (one hinge at the pin, one at the fixed end, one within the column). Derived from PDC TR-06-01 Table 4-4: the largest reaction for a pinned-fixed, uniformly loaded beam is Vu = 5*ru*L/8 with ru = 12*Mn/L^2, which rearranges to:

ParameterTypeDescription
mnfloatrequiredNominal flexural strength of the column cross-section, accounting for coexisting axial load (ft-kip or kN-m). In no case should the governing Mn be less than that with zero axial load (Section 3-3.1.2).
lfloatrequiredColumn clear height (ft or m).

table_4_1_beam_flexure_modeling — Table 4-1(i): nonlinear modeling parameters (a, b, c) and acceptance-criteria plastic rotations for a reinforced-concrete beam controlled by FLEXURE (printed p. 63, replaces ASCE 41 Table 10-7). Linear interpolation between the printed grid points is permitted (footnote 1) and performed here over rho_diff_over_rho_bal in [0.0, 0.5] and vw_ratio in [3, 6].

ParameterTypeDescription
rho_diff_over_rho_balfloatrequired(rho - rho') / rho_bal for the section, clamped to [0.0, 0.5] for interpolation.
transverse_reinffloatrequired'C' (conforming) or 'NC' (nonconforming) -- see footnote 4: conforming means hoops spaced <= d/3 within the plastic hinge region, and (for moderate/high ductility demand) Vs >= 3/4 of the design shear.
vw_ratiofloatrequiredV / (bw d sqrt(f'c)) [psi units, f'c in psi], clamped to [3, 6] for interpolation.
condition_governsfloatoptionalUnused placeholder for future multi-condition minimum-governs logic (footnote 3: when multiple i-iv conditions occur, use the minimum numerical value). Default 'minimum'.

table_4_1_beam_other_modeling — Table 4-1(ii-iv): nonlinear modeling parameters for RC beams controlled by SHEAR, inadequate development/splicing, or inadequate embedment into the beam-column joint (printed p. 63).

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'shear', 'development', or 'inadequate_embedment'.
stirrup_spacing_le_d2floatoptionalTrue if stirrup spacing <= d/2 (governs 'shear' and 'development' only). Default True.

table_4_2_beam_flexure_mfactor — Table 4-2(i): linear-model m-factors for an RC beam controlled by FLEXURE, primary and secondary components (printed p. 64, replaces ASCE 41 Table 10-11). Bilinear interpolation over rho_diff_over_rho_bal in [0.0, 0.5] and vw_ratio in [3, 6] (footnote 1).

ParameterTypeDescription
rho_diff_over_rho_balfloatrequired(rho - rho') / rho_bal, clamped to [0.0, 0.5].
transverse_reinffloatrequired'C' (conforming) or 'NC' (nonconforming).
vw_ratiofloatrequiredV / (bw d sqrt(f'c)), clamped to [3, 6].

table_4_2_beam_other_mfactor — Table 4-2(ii-iv): linear-model m-factors for an RC beam controlled by shear, inadequate development/splicing, or inadequate embedment (printed p. 64).

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'shear', 'development', or 'inadequate_embedment'.
stirrup_spacing_le_d2floatoptionalTrue if stirrup spacing <= d/2. Default True.

table_4_3_slab_flexure_modeling — Table 4-3(i): nonlinear modeling parameters and acceptance criteria for a two-way slab or slab-column connection controlled by FLEXURE (printed p. 65, replaces ASCE 41 Table 6-14). Interpolated over Vg/Vo in [0.2, 0.4] (footnote 1); the residual strength ratio c is undefined ('-') when continuity_reinforcement=False, matching the printed table (no residual capacity without continuity reinforcement).

ParameterTypeDescription
vg_over_vofloatrequiredRatio of gravity shear on the slab critical section (Vg, per ACI 318) to the direct punching shear strength (Vo, per ACI 318), clamped to [0.2, 0.4].
continuity_reinforcementfloatrequiredTrue ('Yes') if at least one main bottom bar (or, for post-tensioned slabs, one tendon) in each direction is effectively continuous through the column cage; else False ('No').

table_4_3_slab_other_modeling — Table 4-3(ii-iii): nonlinear modeling parameters for a two-way slab controlled by inadequate development/splicing, or inadequate embedment into the slab-column joint (printed p. 65).

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'development' or 'inadequate_embedment'.

table_4_4_slab_flexure_mfactor — Table 4-4(i): linear-model m-factors for a two-way slab or slab-column connection controlled by FLEXURE (printed p. 66, replaces ASCE 41 Table 6-15). Interpolated over Vg/Vo in [0.2, 0.4].

ParameterTypeDescription
vg_over_vofloatrequiredVg/Vo per ACI 318, clamped to [0.2, 0.4].
continuity_reinforcementfloatrequiredTrue ('Yes') or False ('No') per the continuity-reinforcement definition in `table_4_3_slab_flexure_modeling`.

table_4_4_slab_other_mfactor — Table 4-4(ii-iii): linear-model m-factors for a two-way slab controlled by inadequate development/splicing (primary m-factor not applicable, '-' in the printed table -- secondary only) or inadequate embedment into the slab-column joint (printed p. 66).

ParameterTypeDescription
conditionfloatrequired'development' or 'inadequate_embedment'.

tie_rebar_phi — Section 4-3: strength reduction factor Phi for properly anchored, embedded, or spliced reinforcement in TENSION providing Tie Force strength, based on ACI 318 strut-and-tie models (printed p. 61).

No parameters.

column_axial_classification — Section 5-4.3: classifies a steel column's P-M interaction as force- or deformation-controlled based on the axial-load ratio P/PCL (printed p. 68).

ParameterTypeDescription
pfloatrequiredAxial load from the analysis (kip or kN).
p_clfloatrequiredLower-bound axial compressive strength, PCL (kip or kN).

list_table_c1_connection_types — Lists the connection-type keys in `TABLE_C1_CONNECTION_TYPES`.

ParameterTypeDescription
restraintfloatoptionalFilter to 'FR' or 'PR' (matches connections classified purely as that type; the one 'FR or PR' entry, bolted_flange_plates, is excluded from both filters -- request it directly by name). Default None (return all).

table_5_1_fr_connection_mfactor — Table 5-1, Fully Restrained Moment Connections: linear-model m-factors as a function of beam depth d (printed p. 69).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequiredOne of 'improved_wuf_bolted_web', 'reduced_beam_section', 'wuf', 'sideplate'.
dfloatrequiredBeam depth (inch).

table_5_1_pr_flexible_connection_mfactor — Table 5-1, Partially Restrained Simple Connections (Flexible): linear-model m-factors as a function of bolt-group depth dbg (printed p. 69).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_angles' (requires limit_state) or 'simple_shear_tab'.
dbgfloatrequiredDepth of the bolt group (inch).
limit_statefloatoptionalFor 'double_angles': 'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', or 'flexure_in_angles'. Not used for 'simple_shear_tab'.

table_5_1_pr_stiff_connection_mfactor — Table 5-1, Partially Restrained Moment Connections (Relatively Stiff): constant linear-model m-factors by limit state (printed p. 69).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_split_tee'.
limit_statefloatrequired'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', 'tension_in_tee', or 'flexure_in_tee'.

table_5_2_fr_connection_modeling — Table 5-2, Fully Restrained Moment Connections: nonlinear modeling parameters (a, b, c) and acceptance criteria (equal to a, b per the printed table) as a function of beam depth d (printed p. 70).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequiredOne of 'improved_wuf_bolted_web', 'reduced_beam_section', 'wuf', 'sideplate'.
dfloatrequiredBeam depth (inch).

table_5_2_pr_flexible_connection_modeling — Table 5-2, Partially Restrained Simple Connections (Flexible): nonlinear modeling parameters and acceptance criteria as a function of bolt-group depth dbg (printed p. 70).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_angles' (requires limit_state) or 'simple_shear_tab'.
dbgfloatrequiredDepth of the bolt group (inch).
limit_statefloatoptionalFor 'double_angles': 'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', or 'flexure_in_angles'.

table_5_2_pr_stiff_connection_modeling — Table 5-2, Partially Restrained Moment Connections (Relatively Stiff): constant nonlinear modeling parameters and acceptance criteria by limit state (printed p. 70).

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequired'double_split_tee'.
limit_statefloatrequired'shear_in_bolt', 'tension_in_bolt', 'tension_in_tee', or 'flexure_in_tee'.

table_c1_connection_type — Table C-1: steel frame beam-to-column connection-type inventory -- description, Fully/Partially Restrained (FR/PR) classification, and illustrating figure (printed p. 111). This is a descriptive/ classification inventory (Appendix C commentary); the corresponding numeric m-factors and modeling parameters, where this UFC specifies its own values, are in `table_5_1_*/table_5_2_*` above.

ParameterTypeDescription
connection_typefloatrequiredA key of `TABLE_C1_CONNECTION_TYPES` (e.g. 'reduced_beam_section', 'shear_tab_connection').

cold_formed_steel_alternate_path_modeling_source — Section 8-4.2: cold-formed steel Alternate Path modeling parameters, nonlinear acceptance criteria, and linear m-factors are the Life-Safety values from ASCE 41 Chapter 12 for primary and secondary components -- NOT reprinted in this UFC (printed p. 75).

No parameters.

cold_formed_steel_default_lower_bound_factor — Section 8-1: when default LOWER-BOUND strength values are needed for cold-formed steel light-metal-framing shear walls (ASCE 41 defaults are otherwise expected-strength values), multiply the expected-strength value by 0.85 -- the SAME rule and factor as wood, Section 7-1 (printed p. 75).

No parameters.

cold_formed_steel_material_code_references — Section 8-2: cold-formed steel strength reduction factor Phi is NOT reprinted in this UFC -- apply the AISI/COS/NASPEC North American Specification for the Design of Cold-Formed Steel Structural Members (printed p. 75).

No parameters.

masonry_alternate_path_modeling_source — Section 6-4.2: masonry Alternate Path modeling parameters, nonlinear acceptance criteria, and linear m-factors are the Life-Safety values from ASCE 41 Chapter 11 for primary and secondary components -- NOT reprinted in this UFC (printed p. 71).

No parameters.

masonry_material_code_references — Sections 6-1, 6-2: masonry over-strength factors and strength reduction factor Phi are NOT reprinted in this UFC -- apply ASCE 41 Table 11-1 (lower-bound-to-expected-strength factors) and ACI 530 Building Code Requirements for Masonry Structures (Phi, by limit state), respectively (printed p. 71).

No parameters.

wood_alternate_path_modeling_source — Section 7-5.2: wood Alternate Path modeling parameters, nonlinear acceptance criteria, and linear m-factors are the Life-Safety values from ASCE 41 Chapter 12 for primary and secondary components -- NOT reprinted in this UFC (printed p. 74).

No parameters.

wood_default_lower_bound_factor — Section 7-1: when default LOWER-BOUND strength values are needed for wood (default strengths from AF&PA/ASCE 16 and ASCE 41 are otherwise expected-strength values), multiply the expected-strength value by 0.85 (printed p. 73).

No parameters.

wood_material_code_references — Section 7-2: wood strength reduction factor Phi is NOT reprinted in this UFC -- apply the ANSI/AF&PA National Design Specification (NDS) for Wood Construction, for the component/behavior under consideration (printed p. 73).

No parameters.

wood_time_effect_factor — Section 7-3: the wood time-effect factor lambda, used (per Section 3-1.2/3-2.7) in addition to the ASCE 41 Chapter 12 default expected- strength values, for both Tie Force and Alternate Path design (printed p. 73). Per Appendix C-10.1, this reflects a deliberate choice between the permanent-dead-load value (0.6) and the impact-load value (1.25), since post-damage stability need only persist long enough for rescue/ shoring, not permanently.

No parameters.

construction_document_requirements — Section 1603.1.9 [Addition]: information that must be indicated on the construction documents for a building designed to this UFC (printed p. 225).

No parameters.

qa_plan_detailed_requirements — Section 1710.1.2 [Addition]: when a QA plan is required, it must provide for these four items (printed p. 226).

No parameters.

qa_plan_required — Section 1710.1.1 [Addition]: a quality-assurance plan is required for structures designed to progressive-collapse Risk Category II, III, or IV; RC I requires no QA plan (printed pp. 225-226).

ParameterTypeDescription
risk_categoryfloatrequired'I', 'II', 'III', or 'IV'.

special_inspection_requirements — Section 1711 [Addition]: material-specific special inspection requirements for the progressive-collapse-resisting system (printed pp. 227-228). Special inspections under 1711.2-1711.5 apply to structures designed for RC II, III, or IV per the same triggers as `qa_plan_required`.

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatrequiredA key of the requirements table: 'structural_steel', 'wood', 'cold_formed_steel', or 'cast_in_place_concrete'.

structural_observation_required — Section 1712.1 [Addition]: structural observations of the progressive-collapse-resisting system are required when the contracting officer requires them, OR unconditionally for Risk Category IV structures (printed p. 228).

ParameterTypeDescription
contracting_officer_requiresfloatoptionalTrue if the contracting officer has required structural observation. Default False.
risk_categoryfloatoptional'I', 'II', 'III', or 'IV'. Default 'II'.

retrieve_section — Retrieve one section by its ID, at any level: its own text, 'under' (the sections above it) and 'children' (ID and title of each subsection, fetched by its own ID). A missing ID's error names the nearest section above it and the sections numbered under it.

ParameterTypeDescription
section_idstrrequiredSection identifier at any level (e.g. '1-1', '1-3.4.1', '3-2.11.1.1').
include_subsectionsbooloptionalInline the subsections' text too, when the whole fits in 12,000 characters; otherwise they stay listed in 'children' with a note.

search_sections — Keyword search across every section and subsection, best first: each hit is a section's number, title, chapter, 'under' (the sections above it) and a snippet of its text, never the whole text (retrieve_section fetches that). As many hits as fit; 'next_offset' and a note say how to get more.

ParameterTypeDescription
querystrrequiredSearch query (case-insensitive, multi-word AND).
limitintoptionalMost hits to return (at most 50; fewer when they would not fit).
offsetintoptionalSkip this many of the best hits: the 'next_offset' of the last call.

list_chapters — List chapters and their sections by ID and title, subsections included (a nested one carries parent_id). Without 'chapter': every chapter, with its sections when the whole listing fits one result (otherwise titles and section counts, and a note). With 'chapter': that chapter's sections.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintoptionalChapter number: list its sections. Leave out for every chapter.

load_chapter — Load a whole chapter: every section's text. A chapter too long for one result (most are) comes back as its list of sections with a note: fetch the ones you need with retrieve_section.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintrequiredChapter number.

10.1.44 ufc_concrete_practice — ufc_concrete_practice

dowel_bar_alignment_tolerance — Typical dowel bar alignment specification tolerances (Section 8-5.2.1.1).

No parameters.

dowel_bar_corner_clearance — Minimum/preferred dowel bar clearance at slab corners (Section 8-5.2.1.4).

No parameters.

dowel_bar_drilled_hole_oversize — Drilled hole oversize for drill-and-epoxy dowel installation (Section 8-5.2.3).

No parameters.

edge_slump_tolerance — Typical edge slump acceptance tolerance (Sections 8-11 and 10-5.1).

No parameters.

table_3_1_weather_severity — Categorize weather severity for aggregate deleterious-material limits (Table 3-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
air_freezing_indexfloatrequiredAir freezing index, coldest year in 30 (degree-days F, per UFC 3-260-02 calculation).
avg_monthly_precip_infloatrequiredAverage precipitation for any single month during the freezing period, inches.

table_3_2_deleterious_material_limit — Deleterious material limit, percent mass, airfield aggregates (Table 3-2).

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatrequiredDeleterious material key: 'clay_lumps_and_friable_particles' (or 'clay_lumps'/'friable_particles'), 'shale', 'material_finer_than_no_200' (or 'minus_200'/'no_200'), 'lightweight_particles', 'clay_ironstone', 'chert_and_cherty_stone' (or 'chert'/'cherty_stone'), 'claystone_mudstone_siltstone' (or 'claystone'/'mudstone'/'siltstone'), 'shaly_argillaceous_limestone' (or 'shaly_limestone'/'argillaceous_limestone'), 'other_soft_particles', 'total_deleterious_excl_minus_200', 'total_fine_incl_minus_200'.
aggregate_categoryfloatrequired'coarse_severe' (coarse aggregate, severe weather), 'coarse_moderate' (coarse aggregate, moderate weather), or 'fine' (fine aggregate, all weather).

table_3_3_aggregate_test_time — Lead time required for ASR/freeze-thaw aggregate testing (Table 3-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
test_methodfloatrequired'astm_c1260' (or 'c1260'/'crd_c_174'), 'astm_c1293' (or 'c1293'/'crd_c_175'), or 'astm_c666' (or 'c666'/'crd_c_20').

table_3_4_portland_cement_type — Portland cement type application (Table 3-4, ASTM C150/CRD-C 201).

ParameterTypeDescription
cement_typefloatrequired'type_i', 'type_ii', 'type_iii', 'type_iv', or 'type_v' (also accepts bare numerals/roman numerals, e.g. '1', 'I').

table_3_5_blended_cement_type — Blended cement type composition (Table 3-5, ASTM C595/CRD-C 203).

ParameterTypeDescription
cement_typefloatrequired'type_il' (or 'il'), 'type_is' (or 'is'), 'type_p' (or 'p'), 'type_ip' (or 'ip'), 'type_i_pm' (or 'ipm'), 'type_i_sm' (or 'ism'), 'type_s' (or 's').

table_3_6_hydraulic_cement_type — Performance-based hydraulic cement type use (Table 3-6, ASTM C1157/CRD-C 271).

ParameterTypeDescription
cement_typefloatrequired'type_gu', 'type_he', 'type_ms', 'type_hs', 'type_mh', or 'type_lh' (also accepts the bare 2-letter code, e.g. 'gu').

table_3_7_ggbf_slag_grade — GGBF slag grade properties (Table 3-7, ASTM C989/CRD-C 205).

ParameterTypeDescription
gradefloatrequired'grade_80' (or 80), 'grade_100' (or 100), 'grade_120' (or 120).

table_3_8_admixture_type — Chemical admixture type use (Table 3-8, ASTM C494/CRD-C 87).

ParameterTypeDescription
admixture_typefloatrequired'type_a' through 'type_g' (also accepts the bare letter, e.g. 'a').

table_8_1_dowel_misalignment_impact — Dowel bar misalignment type and its impact on performance (Table 8-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
misalignment_typefloatrequired'horizontal_translation', 'longitudinal_translation', 'vertical_translation', 'horizontal_skew', or 'vertical_skew'.

table_9_1_maximum_joint_spacing — Maximum joint spacing by slab thickness (Table 9-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
slab_thickness_infloatrequiredConcrete slab thickness, inches.
facility_typefloatoptional'airfield' (default) or 'road' (roads and parking lots use a narrower minimum spacing, 10-15 ft, in the < 9 in. thickness category only; the two categories are otherwise identical).

table_d1_cracking_causes — Early-age cracking type and possible causes (Table D-1, Appendix D).

ParameterTypeDescription
crack_typefloatrequired'plastic_shrinkage' (or 'plastic'), 'random_no_orientation' (or 'random'/'random_cracking'), 'longitudinal' (or 'longitudinal_cracking'), 'transverse' (or 'transverse_cracking'), 'corner' (or 'corner_cracking'), 'pop_off_ahead_of_sawing' (or 'pop_off'/'popoff'), 'late_cracking', 'sympathy_cracks' (or 'sympathy'), 'settlement_over_dowel_tie_bars' (or 'settlement_cracks'), 're_entrant' (or 're_entrant_cracks'/ 'reentrant').

table_e1_rcc_gradation — Recommended combined roller-compacted concrete (RCC) gradation (Table E-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm, one of 25, 19, 12.5, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.60, 0.30, 0.15, 0.075 (i.e. 1 in. down to No. 200). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

coarseness_factor — Combined-aggregate coarseness factor (Equation 7-1, Section 7-9.1.5).

ParameterTypeDescription
pct_retained_9_5mmfloatrequiredCumulative percent of the combined aggregate retained on the 9.5 mm (3/8 in.) sieve.
pct_retained_2_36mmfloatrequiredCumulative percent of the combined aggregate retained on the 2.36 mm (No. 8) sieve. Must be > 0.

workability_factor — Combined-aggregate workability factor (Equation 7-1, Section 7-9.1.5).

ParameterTypeDescription
pct_passing_2_36mmfloatrequiredCumulative percent of the combined aggregate passing the 2.36 mm (No. 8) sieve.
cementitious_content_kg_m3floatrequiredTotal cementitious material content of the mixture, kg/m3.

retrieve_section — Retrieve one section by its ID, at any level: its own text, 'under' (the sections above it) and 'children' (ID and title of each subsection, fetched by its own ID). A missing ID's error names the nearest section above it and the sections numbered under it.

ParameterTypeDescription
section_idstrrequiredSection identifier at any level (e.g. '1-1', '3-7.1.1', '3-12.2.2.1').
include_subsectionsbooloptionalInline the subsections' text too, when the whole fits in 12,000 characters; otherwise they stay listed in 'children' with a note.

search_sections — Keyword search across every section and subsection, best first: each hit is a section's number, title, chapter, 'under' (the sections above it) and a snippet of its text, never the whole text (retrieve_section fetches that). As many hits as fit; 'next_offset' and a note say how to get more.

ParameterTypeDescription
querystrrequiredSearch query (case-insensitive, multi-word AND).
limitintoptionalMost hits to return (at most 50; fewer when they would not fit).
offsetintoptionalSkip this many of the best hits: the 'next_offset' of the last call.

list_chapters — List chapters and their sections by ID and title, subsections included (a nested one carries parent_id). Without 'chapter': every chapter, with its sections when the whole listing fits one result (otherwise titles and section counts, and a note). With 'chapter': that chapter's sections.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintoptionalChapter number: list its sections. Leave out for every chapter.

load_chapter — Load a whole chapter: every section's text. A chapter too long for one result (most are) comes back as its list of sections with a note: fetch the ones you need with retrieve_section.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintrequiredChapter number.

10.1.45 ufc_flexible_practice — ufc_flexible_practice

spray_application_rate — Spray application rate range for prime coat / tack coat / fog seal / rejuvenator.

ParameterTypeDescription
application_typefloatrequired'prime_coat', 'tack_coat', 'fog_seal', or 'rejuvenator'.

table_2_12_pfc_gradation — Aggregate gradation band for Porous Friction Course (PFC) (Table 2-12).

ParameterTypeDescription
gradationfloatrequired'gradation_a' (19 mm / 3/4 in max, ~25 mm compacted lift) or 'gradation_b' (12.5 mm / 1/2 in max, ~19 mm compacted lift).
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 19.0, 12.5, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 0.60, 0.075). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_2_15_sma_gradation — Stone Matrix Asphalt (SMA) gradation guideline (Table 2-15, per NAPA 1999).

ParameterTypeDescription
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 19.0, 12.7, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 0.60, 0.30, 0.075). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table. The 9.5 mm (3/8 in) row is a maximum-only criterion (75% max, no minimum).

table_2_17_sma_mix_design_requirements — Stone Matrix Asphalt (SMA) Marshall mix design requirements (Table 2-17).

ParameterTypeDescription
parameterfloatoptionalIf given, returns just that parameter: 'vtm', 'asphalt_content', 'vma', 'stability', 'flow', 'compaction', or 'draindown'. If omitted, returns all parameters.

table_2_1_gradation_hma — Aggregate gradation band for HMA pavements (Table 2-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
gradationfloatrequired'gradation_1' (19 mm / 3/4 in nominal max), 'gradation_2' (12.5 mm / 1/2 in), or 'gradation_3' (9.5 mm / 3/8 in).
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 25.0, 19.0, 12.5, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.60, 0.30, 0.15, 0.075). If given, returns just that sieve's percent-passing band. If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_2_3_asphalt_grade_by_pti — Asphalt binder base grade selection by Pavement Temperature Index (Table 2-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
pti_cfloatrequiredPavement Temperature Index, cumulative degrees C. Must be >= 0.

table_2_5_asphalt_grade_by_freezing_index — Asphalt cement selection for cold regions by Design Air-Freezing Index (Table 2-5).

ParameterTypeDescription
dfi_cfloatrequiredDesign Air-Freezing Index, cumulative degrees C. Must be >= 0.

table_2_7_minimum_vma — Minimum percent voids in mineral aggregate (VMA) by gradation type (Table 2-7).

ParameterTypeDescription
gradationfloatrequired'gradation_1' (25 mm / 1 in max particle size), 'gradation_2' (19 mm / 3/4 in), or 'gradation_3' (12.5 mm / 1/2 in).

table_2_8_marshall_design_criteria — Marshall/Superpave mix acceptability criteria by mix type and compaction (Table 2-8).

ParameterTypeDescription
mix_typefloatrequired'hma' (HMA surface or intermediate course) or 'sand_asphalt'.
compactionfloatrequired'50_blows', '75_blows' (Marshall hammer), '50_gyrations', or '75_gyrations' (Superpave gyratory compactor). Not every combination with mix_type is tabulated (e.g. sand_asphalt has no 75-blow/75-gyration row) -- an unavailable combination raises ValueError.
propertyfloatoptionalIf given, returns just that property's criterion: 'stability', 'flow', 'vtm', 'vma', or 'vfa'. If omitted, returns the full criteria row.

table_3_2_tack_coat_temperature — Tack coat spray application temperature by material type and grade (Table 3-2).

ParameterTypeDescription
material_typefloatrequired'cutback', 'emulsion', or 'asphalt_cement'.
gradefloatrequiredGrade designation, e.g. 'rc_70', 'rc_250' (cutback); 'rs_1', 'ms_1', 'hfms_1', 'ss_1', 'ss_1h', 'crs_1', 'css_1', 'css_1h' (emulsion); '200_300_pen', '120_150_pen', '85_100_pen', 'ac_2.5', 'ac_5', 'ac_10', 'ar_1000', 'ar_2000', 'ar_4000', 'pg_58_22_64_22' (asphalt cement).

table_4_2_gradation_sbst — Aggregate gradation band for Single Bituminous Surface Treatment (SBST) (Table 4-2).

ParameterTypeDescription
designationfloatrequired'no_1' (ASTM D448 No. 6), 'no_2' (No. 7), or 'no_3' (No. 8) -- decreasing aggregate size.
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 25.0, 19.0, 12.5, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_4_3_gradation_dbst — Aggregate gradation band for Double Bituminous Surface Treatment (DBST) (Table 4-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
designationfloatrequired'no_1', 'no_2', 'no_3', or 'no_4' (see `spreading` in the returned dict for whether it is the first or second spreading of its pairing).
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 25.0, 19.0, 12.5, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.30). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_4_4_slurry_seal_gradation — Slurry seal aggregate gradation band by type (Table 4-4).

ParameterTypeDescription
type_floatrequired'type_1', 'type_2', or 'type_3'.
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.60, 0.30, 0.15, 0.075). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_4_5_frs_application_rate — Fuel-Resistant Sealer (FRS) minimum application rate and gradation (Table 4-5).

ParameterTypeDescription
gradationfloatrequired'coarse', 'medium', or 'fine'.
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 1.18, 0.85, 0.60, 0.425, 0.30, 0.212, 0.15, 0.106). If given, returns just that sieve's percent-passing band (plus the rate); if omitted, returns the full gradation band table (plus the rate).

table_4_7_micro_surfacing_gradation — Micro-surfacing aggregate gradation band by type (Table 4-7).

ParameterTypeDescription
type_floatrequired'type_2' or 'type_3'.
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.60, 0.30, 0.15, 0.075). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_6_1_cold_mix_gradation — Typical aggregate gradation for plant-mix cold-laid asphalt mixtures (Table 6-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
mix_typefloatrequired'dense_graded' or 'open_graded'.
columnfloatrequired1 or 2 (the two tabulated gradings for that mix_type).
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 12.5, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.60, 0.30, 0.15, 0.075). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_6_2_cold_mix_asphalt_selection — Asphalt type and grade selection for cold-mix asphalt by climate (Table 6-2).

ParameterTypeDescription
climatefloatrequired'cold' (< 16 C / 60 F), 'moderate' (16-27 C / 60-80 F), or 'hot' (> 27 C / 80 F) -- climatic conditions during construction or storage.

table_6_3_cold_mix_optimum_ac_selection — Criteria for selecting optimum asphalt content, cold-mix asphalt (Table 6-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
property_floatoptionalIf given, returns just that criterion: 'unit_weight', 'vtm', or 'vfa'. If omitted, returns all three.

table_6_4_mixing_temperature — Mixing temperature range for asphalt materials, cold-mix asphalt pugmill (Table 6-4).

ParameterTypeDescription
material_typefloatrequired'emulsified' or 'cutback'.
gradefloatrequired'ms_2', 'ms_2h', 'ss_1', 'ss_1h' (emulsified); 'rc_70', 'rc_250', 'rc_800', 'mc_70', 'mc_250', 'mc_800' (cutback).

table_7_2_ogam_gradation — Gradation limits for the open-graded asphalt mixture (OGAM) course of RMP (Table 7-2).

ParameterTypeDescription
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 19.0, 12.5, 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 0.60, 0.075). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_7_3_slurry_grout_gradation — Silica sand gradation for the cement slurry grout course of RMP (Table 7-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
sieve_mmfloatoptionalSieve size, mm (one of 1.18, 0.60, 0.075). If omitted, returns the full gradation band table.

table_7_4_grout_mix_proportions — Resin Modified Pavement (RMP) cement slurry grout mix proportions, percent by weight (Table 7-4).

ParameterTypeDescription
materialfloatoptionalIf given, returns just that material's range: 'silica_sand', 'fly_ash', 'water', 'type_i_cement', or 'cross_polymer_resin'. If omitted, returns all five ranges.

table_7_5_grout_viscosity — RMP cement slurry grout viscosity acceptance range, Marsh cone flow time (Table 7-5).

ParameterTypeDescription
time_elapsedfloatrequired'0_30_min' (0 to 30 minutes after polymer addition) or 'after_30_min'.

table_b1_surface_area_factor — Surface area factor for slurry-seal aggregate, by sieve size (Table B-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
sieve_mmfloatrequiredSieve size, mm (one of 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.60, 0.30, 0.15, 0.075).

air_voids_vtm — Air voids in total mix, Vv / VTM, percent (Section 2-4.2.8.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
gmbfloatrequiredBulk specific gravity of the compacted mixture.
gmmfloatrequiredTheoretical maximum specific gravity of the mixture (ASTM D2041). Must be > 0.

bulk_specific_gravity_gmb — Bulk specific gravity of a compacted mixture, Gmb (Section 2-4.2.8.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
wt_dry_airfloatrequiredDry weight of the specimen in air (g), Wdry.
wt_ssdfloatrequiredSaturated-surface-dry weight of the specimen (g), Wssd.
wt_submergedfloatrequiredWeight of the specimen submerged in water (g), Wsubmerged.

bulk_specific_gravity_gmb_geometric — Bulk specific gravity from measured specimen geometry (Section 7-3.1, RMP).

ParameterTypeDescription
wt_dry_airfloatrequiredDry weight of the specimen in air (g), WTair.
diameterfloatrequiredSpecimen diameter, D (cm).
heightfloatrequiredSpecimen height, H (cm).

fuller_thompson_max_density_passing — Fuller-Thompson maximum-density gradation curve, percent passing (Section 2-4.2.3.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
sieve_size_mmfloatrequiredSieve opening size, d (mm). Must be > 0 and <= max_particle_size_mm.
max_particle_size_mmfloatrequiredMaximum aggregate particle size, D (mm). Must be > 0.
nfloatoptionalGradation exponent (default 0.45, the standard Fuller-Thompson maximum-density value).

rmp_optimum_asphalt_content — RMP open-graded mixture estimated optimum asphalt content (Section 7-3.1, French method).

ParameterTypeDescription
sigmafloatrequiredConventional specific surface area (see `rmp_specific_surface_area`). Must be > 0.
apparent_sg_combined_aggregatefloatrequiredSG: apparent specific gravity of the combined aggregates. Must be > 0.

rmp_specific_surface_area — RMP open-graded mixture conventional specific surface area, Sigma (Section 7-3.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
pct_retained_no4floatrequiredG: percentage of material retained on the 4.75 mm (No. 4) sieve.
pct_passing_no4_retained_no30floatrequiredS: percentage of material passing the 4.75 mm (No. 4) sieve and retained on the 600 um (No. 30) sieve.
pct_passing_no30_retained_no200floatrequireds: percentage of material passing the 600 um (No. 30) sieve and retained on the 75 um (No. 200) sieve.
pct_passing_no200floatrequiredf: percentage of material passing the 75 um (No. 200) sieve.

slurry_seal_asphalt_for_film_thickness — Asphalt content to coat aggregate to a target film thickness, SAA (Equation B-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
csa_m2_per_kgfloatrequiredCSA, corrected surface area (see `slurry_seal_corrected_surface_area`), m^2/kg.
film_thickness_umfloatrequiredt: desired asphalt film thickness, micrometers (source design default: 8 micrometers / 3.15e-4 in.).
sg_asphaltfloatrequiredSGa: specific gravity of the asphalt. If unknown, the source permits assuming SGa = 1.0 without materially affecting the design (per Appendix B-1.2.1).

slurry_seal_corrected_surface_area — Corrected surface area of slurry-seal aggregate, CSA (Appendix B-1.2.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
surface_area_m2_per_kgfloatrequiredSA, total surface area (see `slurry_seal_surface_area`), m^2/kg.
apparent_sg_aggregatefloatrequiredASG: apparent specific gravity of the aggregate. Must be > 0.

slurry_seal_surface_area — Total surface area of slurry-seal job aggregate, SA (Appendix B-1.2.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
pct_passing_by_sieve_mmfloatrequiredMapping of sieve size (mm, matching `tables.table_b1_surface_area_factor` keys: 9.5, 4.75, 2.36, 1.18, 0.60, 0.30, 0.15, 0.075) to percent passing that sieve (0-100).

slurry_seal_total_asphalt_required — Total asphalt required for a slurry seal mixture, AR (Equations B-2/B-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
saa_pctfloatrequiredSAA: asphalt content to coat the aggregate surface area to the target film thickness, percent of dry aggregate weight (see `slurry_seal_asphalt_for_film_thickness`).
ka_pctfloatrequiredKA: kerosene absorbed by the aggregate in the centrifuge kerosene equivalent (CKE) test (ASTM D5148 sand-absorption cone per ASTM C128), percent of dry aggregate weight -- taken as the asphalt absorption requirement.

voids_filled_with_asphalt_vfa — Voids filled with asphalt, VFA, percent of VMA (Section 2-4.2.8.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
vma_percentfloatrequiredVoids in mineral aggregate, percent (see `voids_in_mineral_aggregate_vma`). Must be > 0.
vv_percentfloatrequiredAir voids in total mix, percent (see `air_voids_vtm`).

voids_in_mineral_aggregate_vma — Voids in mineral aggregate, VMA, percent of total mixture volume (Section 2-4.2.8.1).

ParameterTypeDescription
gmbfloatrequiredBulk specific gravity of the compacted mixture.
gsbfloatrequiredBulk specific gravity of the aggregate (ASTM C127/C128). Must be > 0.
pbfloatrequiredAsphalt content, decimal fraction of total mixture weight (e.g. 0.05 for 5.0 percent). Must be in [0, 1).

retrieve_section — Retrieve one section by its ID, at any level: its own text, 'under' (the sections above it) and 'children' (ID and title of each subsection, fetched by its own ID). A missing ID's error names the nearest section above it and the sections numbered under it.

ParameterTypeDescription
section_idstrrequiredSection identifier at any level (e.g. '1-1', '2-2.1.1', '2-4.2.3.1').
include_subsectionsbooloptionalInline the subsections' text too, when the whole fits in 12,000 characters; otherwise they stay listed in 'children' with a note.

search_sections — Keyword search across every section and subsection, best first: each hit is a section's number, title, chapter, 'under' (the sections above it) and a snippet of its text, never the whole text (retrieve_section fetches that). As many hits as fit; 'next_offset' and a note say how to get more.

ParameterTypeDescription
querystrrequiredSearch query (case-insensitive, multi-word AND).
limitintoptionalMost hits to return (at most 50; fewer when they would not fit).
offsetintoptionalSkip this many of the best hits: the 'next_offset' of the last call.

list_chapters — List chapters and their sections by ID and title, subsections included (a nested one carries parent_id). Without 'chapter': every chapter, with its sections when the whole listing fits one result (otherwise titles and section counts, and a note). With 'chapter': that chapter's sections.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintoptionalChapter number: list its sections. Leave out for every chapter.

load_chapter — Load a whole chapter: every section's text. A chapter too long for one result (most are) comes back as its list of sections with a note: fetch the ones you need with retrieve_section.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintrequiredChapter number.

10.1.46 ufc_stabilization — ufc_stabilization

table_2_1_min_ucs_requirements — Minimum unconfined compressive strength for stabilized soil (Table 2-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
layerstrrequired'base' or 'subbase_or_subgrade' (subbase course, select material, or subgrade).
pavement_typestrrequired'flexible' or 'rigid'.

table_2_2_durability_requirements — Maximum allowable weight loss after 12 wet-dry/freeze-thaw cycles (Table 2-2).

ParameterTypeDescription
soil_typestrrequired'granular_pi_lt_10' (granular, PI < 10), 'granular_pi_gt_10' (granular, PI > 10), 'silt', or 'clay'.

table_2_3_additive_selection_guide — Guide for selecting a stabilizing additive by gradation-triangle area (Table 2-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
areastrrequired'1a', '1b', '1c', '2a', '2b', '2c', or '3' (Figure 2-1 area).

table_3_1_cement_gradation — Gradation requirements for cement-stabilized base/subbase courses (Table 3-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
course_typestrrequired'base' or 'subbase'.
sievestroptional'1.5in', '0.75in' (base only), 'no4', 'no40', or 'no200'. If empty, returns the full gradation envelope for the course type.

table_3_2_cement_content_by_soil — Initial estimated cement content for moisture-density tests, by USCS class (Table 3-2).

ParameterTypeDescription
uscs_classstrrequiredUSCS classification symbol, e.g. 'GW', 'SC', 'CH'. Valid: gw, sw, gp, gw-gc, gw-gm, sw-sc, sw-sm, gc, gm, gp-gc, gp-gm, gm-gc, sc, sm, sp-sc, sp-sm, sm-sc, sp, cl, ml, mh, ch.

table_3_3_bituminous_subgrade_gradation — Recommended gradations for bituminous-stabilized subgrade materials (Table 3-3).

ParameterTypeDescription
sievestroptional'3in', 'no4', 'no30', or 'no200'. If empty, returns the full gradation envelope.

table_3_4_bituminous_base_subbase_gradation — Recommended gradations for bituminous-stabilized base/subbase materials (Table 3-4).

ParameterTypeDescription
max_sizestrrequired'1.5in', '1in', '0.75in', or '0.5in' (nominal maximum aggregate size / column of Table 3-4).
sievestroptionalOne of: 1.5in, 1in, 0.75in, 0.5in, 3/8in, no4, no8, no16, no30, no50, no100, no200. If empty, returns the full envelope for max_size.

table_3_5_emulsified_asphalt_requirements — Preliminary emulsified-asphalt content for subgrade stabilization (Table 3-5).

ParameterTypeDescription
percent_passing_200floatrequiredPercent of the aggregate passing the No. 200 (0.075 mm) sieve. Interpolated over the tabulated range 0-25%; clamped at endpoints.
percent_passing_no10floatrequiredPercent passing the No. 10 (2 mm) sieve. The table's column axis is categorical, not continuously interpolated: pass a numeric value < 50 (mapped to the '<50' column) or exactly one of 60, 70, 80, 90, 100; or pass the string 'lt_50' directly.

table_3_6_swell_potential — Swell potential of a soil from its Atterberg limits (Table 3-6).

ParameterTypeDescription
liquid_limitfloatrequiredLiquid limit, percent.
plasticity_indexfloatrequiredPlasticity index, percent.

table_a1_equivalency_factors — Equivalency factors for stabilized material thickness design (Table A-1).

ParameterTypeDescription
stabilizer_typestrrequired'asphalt', 'cement', 'lime', 'lime_cement_fly_ash', or 'unbound'.
soil_classstrrequiredA USCS class (e.g. 'GP', 'SC') appropriate to stabilizer_type, or 'all_bituminous_concrete' (asphalt only), or 'crushed_stone' / 'aggregate' (unbound only).

equation_cement_content_modifying_soils — Design cement content for soil modification (PI reduction), Sec 3-1.4.1.

percent_passing_no40floatrequiredB: fraction (0-1) of the soil sample passing the No. 40 (0.425 mm) sieve.
percent_cement_for_pifloatrequiredC: fraction (0-1) cement (of the minus-No.-40 fraction) found by trial testing to yield the desired PI.

equation_cement_pi_limit_table_2_3 — Maximum PI for portland cement in Table 2-3 areas 1C/2C (footnote c).

ParameterTypeDescription
percent_passing_no200floatrequiredPercent of the soil passing the No. 200 (0.075 mm) sieve (0-100).

equation_cutback_asphalt_content_estimate — Preliminary cutback-asphalt content for subgrade stabilization, Sec 3-4.4.

ParameterTypeDescription
percent_retained_no50floatrequireda, percent (0-100).
percent_no50_to_no100floatrequiredb, percent (0-100).
percent_no100_to_no200floatrequiredc, percent (0-100).
percent_passing_no200floatrequiredd, percent (0-100).
percent_solventfloatrequiredS, percent solvent in the cutback asphalt (0-100, must be < 100).

equation_gravimetric_percent_so4 — Percent sulfate (as SO4) in soil, gravimetric BaSO4 method, Sec A-3.1.5.

ParameterTypeDescription
weight_of_residue_gfloatrequiredIgnited BaSO4 precipitate weight, g, >= 0.
oven_dry_weight_gfloatrequiredOven-dry weight of the initial soil sample, g, > 0 (see `equation_oven_dry_weight_from_air_dry`).

equation_oven_dry_weight_from_air_dry — Oven-dry weight of a soil sample from its air-dry weight, Sec A-3.1.5.

ParameterTypeDescription
air_dry_weight_gfloatrequiredWeight of the air-dried soil sample, g, > 0.
air_dry_moisture_content_pctfloatrequiredMoisture content of the air-dried sample, percent (>= 0).

equation_stabilized_equivalent_thickness — Equivalent stabilized-layer thickness from a conventional design, Sec A-1.2.

ParameterTypeDescription
conventional_thickness_infloatrequiredThickness of the conventional (unstabilized) base or subbase layer being replaced, inches, > 0.
equivalency_factorfloatrequiredEF from Table A-1 for the stabilizer type / soil group / layer (base or subbase), > 0.

equation_turbidimetric_percent_so4 — Percent sulfate (as SO4) in soil, turbidimetric method, Sec A-3.2.4.

ParameterTypeDescription
concentration_ppmfloatrequiredC: sulfate concentration of the original (undiluted-aliquot) extracting solution, ppm, >= 0.
total_volume_mlfloatrequiredV: total volume of extracting solution obtained from the soil-to- solution extraction, ml, > 0.
dry_weight_gfloatrequiredW: oven-dry weight of the soil sample, g, > 0.

retrieve_section — Retrieve one section by its ID, at any level: its own text, 'under' (the sections above it) and 'children' (ID and title of each subsection, fetched by its own ID). A missing ID's error names the nearest section above it and the sections numbered under it.

As many hits as fit; 'next_offset' and a note say how to get more.

ParameterTypeDescription
querystrrequiredSearch query (case-insensitive, multi-word AND).
limitintoptionalMost hits to return (at most 50; fewer when they would not fit).
offsetintoptionalSkip this many of the best hits: the 'next_offset' of the last call.

list_chapters — List chapters and their sections by ID and title, subsections included (a nested one carries parent_id). Without 'chapter': every chapter, with its sections when the whole listing fits one result (otherwise titles and section counts, and a note). With 'chapter': that chapter's sections.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintoptionalChapter number: list its sections. Leave out for every chapter.

load_chapter — Load a whole chapter: every section's text. A chapter too long for one result (most are) comes back as its list of sections with a note: fetch the ones you need with retrieve_section.

ParameterTypeDescription
chapterintrequiredChapter number.

10.1.47 ufc_structural — ufc_structural

cybersecurity_requirement — Paragraph 1-8.4: facility-related control systems cybersecurity pointer (printed p. 5).

No parameters.

modification_action_definition — Paragraph 1-6: definition of one of the four modification actions used throughout Chapters 2, 3, 6, and 7 of this UFC (printed p. 1).

ParameterTypeDescription
actionfloatrequiredOne of 'addition', 'deletion', 'replacement', 'supplement' (case-insensitive).

progressive_collapse_applicability — Paragraph 1-8.2: progressive-collapse applicability pointer (printed p. 5). This UFC prints NO trigger table of its own -- applicability triggers (occupancy/risk-category/story-count thresholds) live entirely in UFC 4-023-03, not in UFC 3-301-01.

No parameters.

risk_category_v_note — Paragraph 1-8.3: Risk Category V is a DoD addition to the 2024 IBC/ASCE 7-22 risk-category scheme (printed p. 5), for national strategic military assets. RC V structures are designed to remain elastic during the MCER. The actual list of RC V occupancies is Table 2-2 (`risk_category_and_loads.table_2_2_risk_category('V')`); full RC V design is governed by UFC 3-301-02, not this UFC.

No parameters.

list_table_e1_occupancies — Lists the occupancy keys in `TABLE_E1_LIVE_LOADS`.

ParameterTypeDescription
